kakṣīvāṃśca trayastriṃśatsmṛtā hyāṅgirasā varāḥ //
meaning:
असिजो बृहदुक्थश्च ऋषिर्दीर्घतमास्तथा /
कक्षीवांश्च त्रयस्त्रिंशत्स्मृता ह्याङ्गिरसा वराः //
text_mt:
Asija, Bṛhaduktha, the seer Dīrghatamas,
and Kakṣīvat: these thirty-three are considered the foremost Āṅgirasas.

sanskrit_iast:
ete mantrakṛtaḥ sarve kāśyapāṃstu nibodhata /
kāśyapaścaiva vatsāro naidhruvo raibhya eva ca //
meaning:
एते मन्त्रकृतः सर्वे काश्यपांस्तु निबोधत /
काश्यपश्चैव वत्सारो नैध्रुवो रैभ्य एव च //
text_mt:
All these are mantra-makers. Now learn of the Kāśyapas:
Kāśyapa, Vatsāra, Naidhruva, Raibhya,

sanskrit_iast:
asito deva laścaiva ṣaḍete brahmavādinaḥ /
atrirarvasanaścaiva śyāvāśvaśca gaviṣṭhiraḥ //
meaning:
असितो देव लश्चैव षडेते ब्रह्मवादिनः /
अत्रिरर्वसनश्चैव श्यावाश्वश्च गविष्ठिरः //
text_mt:
Asita, and Devala: these six are proclaimers of the Veda.
Atri, Arvasana, Śyāvāśva, Gaviṣṭhira,

sanskrit_iast:
āvihotra ṛṣirddhīmāṃstathā pūrvātithiśca saḥ /
ityete cā trayaḥ proktā mantrakārā maharṣayaḥ //
meaning:
आविहोत्र ऋषिर्द्धीमांस्तथा पूर्वातिथिश्च सः /
इत्येते चा त्रयः प्रोक्ता मन्त्रकारा महर्षयः //
text_mt:
the wise seer Āvihotra, and Pūrvātithi:
these are declared the [seven] great seers, makers of mantras, of Atri's lineage.

sanskrit_iast:
vasiṣṭhaścaiva śaktiśca tathaiva ca parāśaraḥ /
caturtha indrapramatiḥ pañcamaśca bharadvasuḥ //
meaning:
वसिष्ठश्चैव शक्तिश्च तथैव च पराशरः /
चतुर्थ इन्द्रप्रमतिः पञ्चमश्च भरद्वसुः //
text_mt:
Vasiṣṭha, Śakti, and Parāśara,
fourthly Indrapramati, fifthly Bharadvasu,

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaṣṭhaśca maitrāvaruṇiḥ kuṇḍinaḥ saptamastathā /
iti sapta vaśiṣṭhāśca vijñeyā brahmavādinaḥ //
meaning:
षष्ठश्च मैत्रावरुणिः कुण्डिनः सप्तमस्तथा /
इति सप्त वशिष्ठाश्च विज्ञेया ब्रह्मवादिनः //
text_mt:
sixthly Maitrāvaruṇi, and seventhly Kuṇḍina:
these seven Vasiṣṭhas are to be known as proclaimers of the Veda.

sanskrit_iast:
viśvāmitrastu gādheyo devarātastathodgalaḥ /
tathā vidvānmadhucchandā ṛṣiścānyo 'ghamarṣaṇaḥ //
meaning:
विश्वामित्रस्तु गाधेयो देवरातस्तथोद्गलः /
तथा विद्वान्मधुच्छन्दा ऋषिश्चान्यो ऽघमर्षणः //
text_mt:
Viśvāmitra son of Gādhi, Devarāta, Udgala,
the learned Madhucchandas, and the other seer Aghamarṣaṇa,

sanskrit_iast:
aṣṭako lohitaścaiva kataḥ kolaśca tāvubhau /
devaśravāstathā reṇuḥ pūraṇo 'tha dhanañjayaḥ //
meaning:
अष्टको लोहितश्चैव कतः कोलश्च तावुभौ /
देवश्रवास्तथा रेणुः पूरणो ऽथ धनञ्जयः //
text_mt:
Aṣṭaka, Lohita, Kata, and Kola—both of them—
Devaśravas, Reṇu, Pūraṇa, and Dhanañjaya:

sanskrit_iast:
trayodaśaite dharmiṣṭhā vijñeyāḥ kuśikāvarāḥ /
agastyo 'yo dṛḍhāyuśca vidhmavāhastathaiva ca //
meaning:
त्रयोदशैते धर्मिष्ठा विज्ञेयाः कुशिकावराः /
अगस्त्यो ऽयो दृढायुश्च विध्मवाहस्तथैव च //
text_mt:
these thirteen most righteous ones are to be known as the foremost Kuśikas.
Agastya, Dṛḍhāyu, and Idhmavāha:

sanskrit_iast:
brahmiṣṭhāgastapā hyete trayaḥ paramakīrttayaḥ /
manurvaivasvataścaiva elo rājā purūkhāḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मिष्ठागस्तपा ह्येते त्रयः परमकीर्त्तयः /
मनुर्वैवस्वतश्चैव एलो राजा पुरूखाः //
text_mt:
these three foremost in renown are devoted to Brahman and asceticism.
Manu son of Vivasvat, and King Purūravas son of Ilā:

sanskrit_iast:
kṣatrriyāṇāṃ carāvetau vijñeyau mantravādinau /
bhalandanaśca vatsaśca saṃkīlaścaiva te trayaḥ //
meaning:
क्षत्र्रियाणां चरावेतौ विज्ञेयौ मन्त्रवादिनौ /
भलन्दनश्च वत्सश्च संकीलश्चैव ते त्रयः //
text_mt:
these two are to be known as the foremost mantra-proclaimers among the kṣatriyas.
Bhalandana, Vatsa, and Saṅkīla—these three:

sanskrit_iast:
ete mantrakṛtaścaiva vaiśyānāṃ pravarāḥ smṛtāḥ /
ityeṣā navatiḥ proktā mantrā yairṛṣibhiḥ kṛtāḥ /
brāhyaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyā ṛṣiputrānnibodhata //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte pūrvabhāge dvitīye 'nuṣaṅgapāde yugaprajālakṣaṇamṛṣipravaravarṇanaṃ ca nāma dvātriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
एते मन्त्रकृतश्चैव वैश्यानां प्रवराः स्मृताः /
इत्येषा नवतिः प्रोक्ता मन्त्रा यैरृषिभिः कृताः /
ब्राह्यणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्या ऋषिपुत्रान्निबोधत //
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते पूर्वभागे द्वितीये ऽनुषङ्गपादे युगप्रजालक्षणमृषिप्रवरवर्णनं च नाम द्वात्रिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
text_mt:
these are recorded as the mantra-makers, the foremost among the vaiśyas.
Thus have been declared these ninety seers by whom mantras were composed,
brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas. Now learn of the sons of the seers.

Thus ends the thirty-second chapter, entitled 'Characteristics of the People of the Yugas and Description of the Foremost Seers', in the second part, the Anuṣaṅgapāda, of the first half of the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa proclaimed by Vāyu.

sanskrit_iast:
sūta uvāca
ṛṣikāṇāṃ sutāścāpi vijñeyā ṛṣiputrakāḥ /
brāhyaṇānāṃ pravaktāro nāmataśca nibodhata //
meaning:
सूत उवाच
ऋषिकाणां सुताश्चापि विज्ञेया ऋषिपुत्रकाः /
ब्राह्यणानां प्रवक्तारो नामतश्च निबोधत //
text_mt:
The sūta said:
The sons of the female seers are also to be known as sons of seers.
Learn by name of those who were expositors among the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit_iast:
sapradhānāḥ pravakṣyante samāsācca śrutarṣayaḥ /
bahvṛco bhārgavaḥ pailaḥ sāṃkṛtyo jājalistathā //
meaning:
सप्रधानाः प्रवक्ष्यन्ते समासाच्च श्रुतर्षयः /
बह्वृचो भार्गवः पैलः सांकृत्यो जाजलिस्तथा //
text_mt:
The seers of revealed scripture will be declared in brief, along with their leaders:
the Ṛgveda reciter Bhārgava, Paila, Sāṅkṛtya, Jājali,

sanskrit_iast:
saṃdhyāstirmāṭharaścaiva yājñavalkyaḥ parāśaraḥ /
upamanyurindrapramatirmāḍūkiḥ śākaliśca saḥ //
meaning:
संध्यास्तिर्माठरश्चैव याज्ञवल्क्यः पराशरः /
उपमन्युरिन्द्रप्रमतिर्माडूकिः शाकलिश्च सः //
text_mt:
Saṃdhyāsti, Māṭhara, Yājñavalkya, Parāśara,
Upamanyu, Indrapramati, Māṇḍūki, and Śākali,

sanskrit_iast:
bāṣkaliḥ śokapāṇiśca nailaḥ pailo 'lakastathā /
pannagāḥ pakṣagantāśca ṣaḍaśītiḥ śrutarṣayaḥ //
meaning:
बाष्कलिः शोकपाणिश्च नैलः पैलो ऽलकस्तथा /
पन्नगाः पक्षगन्ताश्च षडशीतिः श्रुतर्षयः //
text_mt:
Bāṣkali, Śokapāṇi, Naila, Paila, Alaka,
Pannagas, Pakṣagantas—eighty-six seers of revealed scripture.

sanskrit_iast:
ete dvijātayo mukhyā bahvṛcānāṃ śrutarṣayaḥ /
vaiśaṃpāyanalauhityau kaṇṭhakālāvaśāvadhaḥ //
meaning:
एते द्विजातयो मुख्या बह्वृचानां श्रुतर्षयः /
वैशंपायनलौहित्यौ कण्ठकालावशावधः //
text_mt:
These twice-born are the foremost seers of revealed scripture among the reciters of the Ṛgveda.
Vaiśampāyana, Lauhitya, Kaṇṭhakāla, Avaśāvadha,

sanskrit_iast:
śyāmāpatiḥ palāḍuśca ālaṃbiḥ kamalāpatiḥ /
teṣāṃ śiṣyāḥ praśiṣyāśca ṣaḍaśīti śrutarṣayaḥ //
meaning:
श्यामापतिः पलाडुश्च आलंबिः कमलापतिः /
तेषां शिष्याः प्रशिष्याश्च षडशीति श्रुतर्षयः //
text_mt:
Śyāmāpati, Palāḍu, Ālambī, Kamalāpati:
their disciples and grand-disciples are eighty-six seers of revealed scripture.

sanskrit_iast:
ete dvijarṣayaḥ proktāścarakādhvaryavo dvijāḥ /
caiminiḥ sabharadvājaḥ kāvyaḥ pauṣyañjireva ca //
meaning:
एते द्विजर्षयः प्रोक्ताश्चरकाध्वर्यवो द्विजाः /
चैमिनिः सभरद्वाजः काव्यः पौष्यञ्जिरेव च //
text_mt:
These twice-born seers are declared to be Caraka priests of the Yajurveda.
Jaimini, along with Bharadvāja, Kāvya, Pauṣyañji,

sanskrit_iast:
hiraṇyanābhaḥ kauśilyo laugākṣiḥ kusumistathā /
laṅgalī śālihotraśca śaktirājaśca bhārgavaḥ //
meaning:
हिरण्यनाभः कौशिल्यो लौगाक्षिः कुसुमिस्तथा /
लङ्गली शालिहोत्रश्च शक्तिराजश्च भार्गवः //
text_mt:
Hiraṇyanābha, Kauśilya, Laugākṣi, Kusumi,
Lāṅgalin, Śālihotra, Śaktirājan, Bhārgava,

sanskrit_iast:
sāmagānāmathācārya ailo rājā purūravāḥ /
ṣaṭcatvāriṃśadanye vai teṣāṃ śiṣyāḥ śrutarṣayaḥ //
meaning:
सामगानामथाचार्य ऐलो राजा पुरूरवाः /
षट्चत्वारिंशदन्ये वै तेषां शिष्याः श्रुतर्षयः //
text_mt:
and the king Purūravas son of Ilā, the teacher of the Sāmaveda singers:
forty-six others, their disciples, are seers of revealed scripture.

sanskrit_iast:
kauśītiḥ kaṅkamudgaśca kuṇḍakaḥ saparāśaraḥ /
lobhālobhaśca dharmātmā tathā brahma balaśca saḥ //
meaning:
कौशीतिः कङ्कमुद्गश्च कुण्डकः सपराशरः /
लोभालोभश्च धर्मात्मा तथा ब्रह्म बलश्च सः //
text_mt:
Kauśīti, Kaṅkamudga, Kuṇḍaka, along with Parāśara,
the righteous Lobhālobha, and Brahmabala,

sanskrit_iast:
kranthalo 'tho madagalo mārkaṇḍeyo 'tha dharmavit /
ityete navatirjñeyā hotravadbrahmacāriṇaḥ //
meaning:
क्रन्थलो ऽथो मदगलो मार्कण्डेयो ऽथ धर्मवित् /
इत्येते नवतिर्ज्ञेया होत्रवद्ब्रह्मचारिणः //
text_mt:
Kranthala, then Madagala, and the righteous Mārkaṇḍeya:
these ninety are to be known as student-ascetics performing the hotṛ’s rites.

sanskrit_iast:
carakādhvaryavaścāpi hyanumaṃntraṃ tu brāhmaṇam /
calūbhiḥ sumatiścaiva tathā devavaraśca yaḥ //
meaning:
चरकाध्वर्यवश्चापि ह्यनुमंन्त्रं तु ब्राह्मणम् /
चलूभिः सुमतिश्चैव तथा देववरश्च यः //
text_mt:
The Caraka priests of the Yajurveda [chant] following the mantra of the Brāhmaṇa.
Calūbhi, Sumati, Devavara,

sanskrit_iast:
anukṛṣṇastathāyuśca anubhūmistathaiva ca /
tathāprītaḥ kṛśāśvaśva sumūlirbāṣkalistathā //
meaning:
अनुकृष्णस्तथायुश्च अनुभूमिस्तथैव च /
तथाप्रीतः कृशाश्वश्व सुमूलिर्बाष्कलिस्तथा //
text_mt:
Anukṛṣṇa, Āyu, Anubhūmi,
Aprīta, Kṛśāśva, Sumūli, and Bāṣkali:

sanskrit_iast:
carakādhvaryakādhvaryunamasyurbrahmacāriṇaḥ /
vaiyāsakiḥ śuko vidvāṃllaukirbhūriśravāstathā //
meaning:
चरकाध्वर्यकाध्वर्युनमस्युर्ब्रह्मचारिणः /
वैयासकिः शुको विद्वांल्लौकिर्भूरिश्रवास्तथा //
text_mt:
these are student-ascetics, adhvaryu priests among the Caraka-adhvaryus, worthy of homage.
Vyāsa's wise son Śuka, Lauki, Bhūriśravas,

sanskrit_iast:
somāviratunāntakyastathā dhaumyaśca kāśyapaḥ /
āraṇyā ilakaścaiva upamanyurvidastathā //
meaning:
सोमाविरतुनान्तक्यस्तथा धौम्यश्च काश्यपः /
आरण्या इलकश्चैव उपमन्युर्विदस्तथा //
text_mt:
Somāviratunāntakya, Dhaumya, Kāśyapa,
Āraṇya, Ilaka, Upamanyu, Vida,

sanskrit_iast:
bhārgavo madhukaḥ piṅgaḥ śveta ketustathaiva ca /
prajādarpaḥ kahoḍaśca yājñavalkyo 'tha śaunakaḥ //
meaning:
भार्गवो मधुकः पिङ्गः श्वेत केतुस्तथैव च /
प्रजादर्पः कहोडश्च याज्ञवल्क्यो ऽथ शौनकः //
text_mt:
Bhārgava, Madhuka, Piṅga, Śvetaketu,
Prajādarpa, Kahoḍa, Yājñavalkya, Śaunaka,

sanskrit_iast:
anaṅgo niratālaśca madhyamādhvaryavastute /
aditirdevamātā ca jalāpā caiva mānavī //
meaning:
अनङ्गो निरतालश्च मध्यमाध्वर्यवस्तुते /
अदितिर्देवमाता च जलापा चैव मानवी //
text_mt:
Anaṅga, and Niratāla: these are the intermediate adhvaryu priests.
Aditi the mother of the gods, Jalāpā daughter of Manu,

sanskrit_iast:
urvaśī viśvayoṣā ca hyapsaraḥpravare śubhe /
mudgalā cātujīvaiva tārā caiva yaśasvinī //
meaning:
उर्वशी विश्वयोषा च ह्यप्सरःप्रवरे शुभे /
मुद्गला चातुजीवैव तारा चैव यशस्विनी //
text_mt:
Urvaśī, Viśvayoṣā—the two auspicious foremost apsarases—
Mudgalā, Ātujīvā, the renowned Tārā,

sanskrit_iast:
prātimedhī ca mārgā ca sujātā ca mahātapā /
lopāmudrā ca dharmajñā yā ca kośītikā smṛtā //
meaning:
प्रातिमेधी च मार्गा च सुजाता च महातपा /
लोपामुद्रा च धर्मज्ञा या च कोशीतिका स्मृता //
text_mt:
Prātimedhī, Mārgā, Sujātā of great asceticism,
righteous Lopāmudrā, and she who is called Kauśītikī:

sanskrit_iast:
etāśca brahmavādinya apsaro rūpaṃsamatāḥ /
ityetā mukhyaśaḥ proktā mayā ca ṛṣiputrakāḥ //
meaning:
एताश्च ब्रह्मवादिन्य अप्सरो रूपंसमताः /
इत्येता मुख्यशः प्रोक्ता मया च ऋषिपुत्रकाः //
text_mt:
these are proclaimers of the Veda, equal in beauty to the apsarases.
Thus have the sons of the seers been chiefly declared by me.

sanskrit_iast:
vaidaśākhāpraṇayanāstataste ṛṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ /
īśvarā mantravaktāra ṛṣayo hyṛṣikāstathā //
meaning:
वैदशाखाप्रणयनास्ततस्ते ऋषयः स्मृताः /
ईश्वरा मन्त्रवक्तार ऋषयो ह्यृषिकास्तथा //
text_mt:
Because they founded branches of the Veda, they are considered seers.
The lords, the seers, and the female seers are the proclaimers of mantras.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣiputrāḥ pravaktaraḥ kalpānāṃ brāhmaṇasya tu /
īśvarāṇāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca ṛṣikāṇāṃ sahātmajaiḥ //
meaning:
ऋषिपुत्राः प्रवक्तरः कल्पानां ब्राह्मणस्य तु /
ईश्वराणामृषीणां च ऋषिकाणां सहात्मजैः //
text_mt:
The sons of the seers are the proclaimers of the ritual manuals and of the Brāhmaṇa.
Of the lords, the seers, and the female seers along with their sons,

sanskrit_iast:
tathā vākyāni janīṣva yathaiṣāṃ mantradṛṣṭayaḥ /
tatrājñāyuktamadvaitaṃ dīptaṃ gaṃbhīraśabdavat //
meaning:
तथा वाक्यानि जनीष्व यथैषां मन्त्रदृष्टयः /
तत्राज्ञायुक्तमद्वैतं दीप्तं गंभीरशब्दवत् //
text_mt:
recognize their utterances according to the visions of mantras that they have:
there, that which is endowed with authority, non-dual, radiant, with deep sound,

sanskrit_iast:
atyantamaparokṣaṃ ca liṅgaṃ nāma tathaiva ca /
sarvabhūtānyabhūtaṃ ca paridānaṃ ca yadbhavet //
meaning:
अत्यन्तमपरोक्षं च लिङ्गं नाम तथैव च /
सर्वभूतान्यभूतं च परिदानं च यद्भवेत् //
text_mt:
exceedingly direct, having distinctive marks and names,
which encompasses all beings and what is yet unbecome,

sanskrit_iast:
kvacinniruktaproktārthaṃ vākyaṃ svāyaṃbhuvaṃ viduḥ /
yatkiñcinmantrasaṃyuktaṃ tatra nāmavibhaktibhiḥ //
meaning:
क्वचिन्निरुक्तप्रोक्तार्थं वाक्यं स्वायंभुवं विदुः /
यत्किञ्चिन्मन्त्रसंयुक्तं तत्र नामविभक्तिभिः //
text_mt:
and whose meaning is in places declared by Nirukta, they know as the utterance originating from Svayambhū.
Whatever is joined with mantras, through case-endings of nominal stems,

sanskrit_iast:
pratyakṣābhihitaṃ caivamṛṣīṇāṃ vacanaṃ matam /
naigamairvividhaiḥ śabdairnipātairbahulaṃ ca yat //
meaning:
प्रत्यक्षाभिहितं चैवमृषीणां वचनं मतम् /
नैगमैर्विविधैः शब्दैर्निपातैर्बहुलं च यत् //
text_mt:
and directly expressed, is regarded as the speech of the seers;
that which abounds in various Vedic expressions and particles,

sanskrit_iast:
yaccāpyasti mahadvākyamṛṣīkāṇāṃ vacaḥ smṛtam /
avispaṣṭapadaṃ yacca yacca syādbahusaṃśayam //
meaning:
यच्चाप्यस्ति महद्वाक्यमृषीकाणां वचः स्मृतम् /
अविस्पष्टपदं यच्च यच्च स्याद्बहुसंशयम् //
text_mt:
and whatever great statement there is, is recorded as the speech of the female seers.
That which has indistinct words and that which contains much doubt

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣiputravacastadvai sarvāśca paridevatāḥ /
hetudṛṣṭānta bahulaṃ citraśabdamapārthakam //
meaning:
ऋषिपुत्रवचस्तद्वै सर्वाश्च परिदेवताः /
हेतुदृष्टान्त बहुलं चित्रशब्दमपार्थकम् //
text_mt:
is indeed the speech of the sons of the seers and of all the minor deities;
that which abounds in reasons and examples, with varied words, devoid of meaning,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvāstu tamaśaktaṃ ca vākyametattu mānuṣam /
miśrā iti samākhyātāḥ prabhāvādṛṣitāṃ gātāḥ //
meaning:
सर्वास्तु तमशक्तं च वाक्यमेतत्तु मानुषम् /
मिश्रा इति समाख्याताः प्रभावादृषितां गाताः //
text_mt:
and completely overcome by darkness, is human speech.
Those who have attained seerhood through spiritual power are designated as 'mixed'.

sanskrit_iast:
samutkarṣāya karṣābhyāṃ jātivyatyāsasaṃbhavāḥ /
bhūtabhavyabhavajjñāna janmaduḥkhacikitsanam //
meaning:
समुत्कर्षाय कर्षाभ्यां जातिव्यत्याससंभवाः /
भूतभव्यभवज्ज्ञान जन्मदुःखचिकित्सनम् //
text_mt:
Due to elevation and depression, they are produced from crossing of classes;
knowledge of the past, future, and present, the remedy for the suffering of rebirth,

sanskrit_iast:
miśrāṇāṃ tadbhavedvākyaṃ gurorbalapravarttanam /
dharmaśāstrapraṇetāro mahimnā sarvagāśca vai //
meaning:
मिश्राणां तद्भवेद्वाक्यं गुरोर्बलप्रवर्त्तनम् /
धर्मशास्त्रप्रणेतारो महिम्ना सर्वगाश्च वै //
text_mt:
and the application of the teacher's power belongs to the speech of the mixed ones.
They are authors of texts on dharma and, through their greatness, all-pervading.

sanskrit_iast:
tapaḥprakarṣaḥ sumahānyeṣāṃ te ṛṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ /
bṛhaspatiśca śukraśca vyāsaḥ sārasvatastathā //
meaning:
तपःप्रकर्षः सुमहान्येषां ते ऋषयः स्मृताः /
बृहस्पतिश्च शुक्रश्च व्यासः सारस्वतस्तथा //
text_mt:
Those whose excellence in asceticism is exceedingly great are considered seers:
Bṛhaspati, Śukra, Vyāsa, and Sārasvata.

sanskrit_iast:
vyāsāḥ śāstrapraṇayanā vedavyāsa iti smṛtāḥ /
yasmādavārajāḥ saṃtaḥ pūrvebhyo medhayādhikāḥ //
meaning:
व्यासाः शास्त्रप्रणयना वेदव्यास इति स्मृताः /
यस्मादवारजाः संतः पूर्वेभ्यो मेधयाधिकाः //
text_mt: The arrangers who compose treatises are known as Vedavyāsas, / because, though born later, they excel their predecessors in intellect.

sanskrit_iast:
aiśvaryeṇa ca saṃpannāstataste ṛṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ /
yasminkālo na caṃ vayaḥ pramāṇamṛṣibhāvane //
meaning:
ऐश्वर्येण च संपन्नास्ततस्ते ऋषयः स्मृताः /
यस्मिन्कालो न चं वयः प्रमाणमृषिभावने //
text_mt: And endowed with sovereign power, they are therefore traditionally remembered as seers, / in whose state of being a seer neither time nor age is a criterion.

sanskrit_iast:
dṛśyate hi pumānkaścitkaścijjyeṣṭhatamo dhiyā /
yasmādbuddhyā ca varṣīyānbalo 'pi śrutavānṛṣiḥ //
meaning:
दृश्यते हि पुमान्कश्चित्कश्चिज्ज्येष्ठतमो धिया /
यस्माद्बुद्ध्या च वर्षीयान्बलो ऽपि श्रुतवानृषिः //
text_mt: For a certain man is seen to be foremost on account of his intellect, / because one who is superior in understanding, though a child, is a learned seer.

sanskrit_iast:
yaḥ kaścitpādavānmadhye prayukto 'kṣara saṃpadā /
viniyuktāvasānāṃ tu tāmṛcaṃ paricakṣate //
meaning:
यः कश्चित्पादवान्मध्ये प्रयुक्तो ऽक्षर संपदा /
विनियुक्तावसानां तु तामृचं परिचक्षते //
text_mt: Whatever [mantra] has metrical feet and is employed in the middle with an abundance of syllables, / with its ending determined by its application, they call an ṛc.

sanskrit_iast:
yaḥ kaścitkaraṇairmantro na ca pādakṣarairmitaḥ /
atiyuktāvasānaṃ ca tadyajurvai pracakṣate //
meaning:
यः कश्चित्करणैर्मन्त्रो न च पादक्षरैर्मितः /
अतियुक्तावसानं च तद्यजुर्वै प्रचक्षते //
text_mt: Whatever mantra is used through actions and is not measured by metrical feet or syllables, / with its ending determined by [the end of the sentence], they declare to be a yajus.

sanskrit_iast:
hrīṅkāraḥ praṇavo gītaḥ prastāvaśca caturthakam /
pañcamaḥ pratihotraśca ṣaṣṭhamāhurupadravam //
meaning:
ह्रीङ्कारः प्रणवो गीतः प्रस्तावश्च चतुर्थकम् /
पञ्चमः प्रतिहोत्रश्च षष्ठमाहुरुपद्रवम् //
text_mt: The sound hrīṃ, the praṇava, the chanted [gīta], and the prastāva as the fourth, / the fifth is the pratihāra, and they call the upadrava the sixth.

sanskrit_iast:
nidhanaṃ saptamaṃ sāmnaḥ saptavindhya midaṃ smṛtam /
pañcavindhya iti proktaṃ hrīṅkāraḥ praṇavādṛte //
meaning:
निधनं सप्तमं साम्नः सप्तविन्ध्य मिदं स्मृतम् /
पञ्चविन्ध्य इति प्रोक्तं ह्रीङ्कारः प्रणवादृते //
text_mt: The nidhana is the seventh of the sāman; this is remembered as having seven divisions. / It is declared to have five divisions without the sound hrīṃ and the praṇava.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmaṇe dharmamatyuktau yattadā jñāpyater'thataḥ /
āśāstistu prasaṃkhyātā vilāpaḥ paridevanā //
meaning:
ब्रह्मणे धर्ममत्युक्तौ यत्तदा ज्ञाप्यतेर्ऽथतः /
आशास्तिस्तु प्रसंख्याता विलापः परिदेवना //
text_mt: When a matter of dharma is stated for Brahman, that which is then communicated by meaning, / along with benediction, is enumerated, [as well as] lamentation and bewailing,

sanskrit_iast:
krodhādvā dveṣaṇāccaiva praśrākhyānaṃ tathaiva ca /
etattu sarvavidyānāṃ vihitaṃ mantralakṣaṇam //
meaning:
क्रोधाद्वा द्वेषणाच्चैव प्रश्राख्यानं तथैव च /
एतत्तु सर्वविद्यानां विहितं मन्त्रलक्षणम् //
text_mt: or through anger or through hatred, and likewise inquiry and narration: / this is prescribed as the characteristic of mantras for all branches of learning.

sanskrit_iast:
mantrā navavidhāḥ proktā ṛgyajuḥ sāmalakṣaṇāḥ /
mūrtirnindā praśaṃsā cākrośastoṣastathaiva ca //
meaning:
मन्त्रा नवविधाः प्रोक्ता ऋग्यजुः सामलक्षणाः /
मूर्तिर्निन्दा प्रशंसा चाक्रोशस्तोषस्तथैव च //
text_mt: Mantras are declared to be of nine kinds, characterized by ṛc, yajus, and sāman: / form, censure, praise, revilement, and satisfaction,

sanskrit_iast:
praśrānujñāstathākhyānamāśāsmatividhayo matāḥ /
mantrabhedāṃśca vakṣyāmi caturviśatilakṣaṇān //
meaning:
प्रश्रानुज्ञास्तथाख्यानमाशास्मतिविधयो मताः /
मन्त्रभेदांश्च वक्ष्यामि चतुर्विशतिलक्षणान् //
text_mt: inquiry, permission, narration, and benediction are considered the modes. / And I will describe the varieties of mantras possessing twenty-four characteristics:

sanskrit_iast:
praśaṃsā stutirākrośo nindā ca paridevanā /
abhiśāpo viśāpaśca praśnaḥ prativacastathā //
meaning:
प्रशंसा स्तुतिराक्रोशो निन्दा च परिदेवना /
अभिशापो विशापश्च प्रश्नः प्रतिवचस्तथा //
text_mt: Praise, eulogy, revilement, censure, and lamentation, / curse, counter-curse, question, and answer,

sanskrit_iast:
āśīryajñastathākṣepa arthākhyānaṃ ca saṃkathā /
viyogā hyabhiyogāśca kathā saṃsthā varaśca vai //
meaning:
आशीर्यज्ञस्तथाक्षेप अर्थाख्यानं च संकथा /
वियोगा ह्यभियोगाश्च कथा संस्था वरश्च वै //
text_mt: blessing, sacrifice, objection, narration of an event, conversation, / separation, accusation, narrative, conclusion, and boon,

sanskrit_iast:
pratiṣedhopa deśau ca namaskāraḥ spṛhā tathā /
vilāpaśceti mantrāṇāṃ caturviṃśatiruddhṛtāḥ //
meaning:
प्रतिषेधोप देशौ च नमस्कारः स्पृहा तथा /
विलापश्चेति मन्त्राणां चतुर्विंशतिरुद्धृताः //
text_mt: prohibition, instruction, salutation, desire, / and bewailing: these twenty-four [varieties] of mantras have been extracted.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣibhiryajñatattvajñairvihitaṃ brahmaṇaṃ purā /
hetu rnirvacanaṃ nindā praśastiḥ saṃśayo nidhiḥ //
meaning:
ऋषिभिर्यज्ञतत्त्वज्ञैर्विहितं ब्रह्मणं पुरा /
हेतु र्निर्वचनं निन्दा प्रशस्तिः संशयो निधिः //
text_mt: In ancient times, the brāhmaṇa was ordained by the seers who knew the truth of sacrifice: / reason, etymology, censure, praise, doubt, injunction,

sanskrit_iast:
purākṛtipurākalpau vyavadhāraṇakalpanā /
upamā ca daśaite vai vidhayo brāhmaṇasya tu //
meaning:
पुराकृतिपुराकल्पौ व्यवधारणकल्पना /
उपमा च दशैते वै विधयो ब्राह्मणस्य तु //
text_mt: ancient deed, ancient myth, determination of meaning, / and simile: these ten are the rules of the brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
lakṣaṇaṃ brāhmaṇasyainadvihitaṃ sarvaśākhināma /
heturhanteḥ smṛto dhātoryannihantyuditaṃ paraiḥ //
meaning:
लक्षणं ब्राह्मणस्यैनद्विहितं सर्वशाखिनाम /
हेतुर्हन्तेः स्मृतो धातोर्यन्निहन्त्युदितं परैः //
text_mt: This characteristic of the brāhmaṇa is prescribed for all Vedic schools: / "reason" [hetu] is held to be from the root han-, because it refutes [nihanti] what is stated by opponents;

sanskrit_iast:
athavārthe pariprāpte hino tergatikarmaṇā /
tathā nirvacanaṃ brūyādvākyārthasyāvadhāraṇam //
meaning:
अथवार्थे परिप्राप्ते हिनो तेर्गतिकर्मणा /
तथा निर्वचनं ब्रूयाद्वाक्यार्थस्यावधारणम् //
text_mt: or when the meaning is obtained, from the root hi- having the sense of motion. / So one should explain "etymology" [nirvacana] as the ascertainment of the meaning of a sentence.

sanskrit_iast:
nindāṃ tāmāhurāyāryā yaddoṣe nindanaṃ vacaḥ /
prapūrvācchaṃsaterdhātoḥ praśaṃsāguṇavattayā //
meaning:
निन्दां तामाहुरायार्या यद्दोषे निन्दनं वचः /
प्रपूर्वाच्छंसतेर्धातोः प्रशंसागुणवत्तया //
text_mt: The noble call that "censure" [nindā] which is an utterance of blame regarding a fault. / ["Praise" is derived] from the root śaṃs- with the prefix pra-, on account of possessing virtues.

sanskrit_iast:
idaṃ tvidamidaṃ naidamityaniścitya saṃśayam /
idamevaṃ vidhātavyamityayaṃ vidhirucyate //
meaning:
इदं त्विदमिदं नैदमित्यनिश्चित्य संशयम् /
इदमेवं विधातव्यमित्ययं विधिरुच्यते //
text_mt: Thinking without certainty, "Is it this or not this?", is "doubt" [saṃśaya]. / "This must be performed in this way" is called "injunction" [vidhi].

sanskrit_iast:
anyasyānyasya cauktiryā budhaiḥ soktā purākṛtiḥ /
yo hyatyantaparokṣārthaḥ sa purākalpa ucyate //
meaning:
अन्यस्यान्यस्य चौक्तिर्या बुधैः सोक्ता पुराकृतिः /
यो ह्यत्यन्तपरोक्षार्थः स पुराकल्प उच्यते //
text_mt: That utterance concerning various persons is called by the wise an "ancient deed" [purākṛti]. / That whose object is entirely imperceptible is called an "ancient myth" [purākalpa].

sanskrit_iast:
purātikrāntavācitvātpurākalpasya kalpa nām /
mantrabrāhmaṇakalpaiśca nigamaiḥ śuddhavistaraiḥ //
meaning:
पुरातिक्रान्तवाचित्वात्पुराकल्पस्य कल्प नाम् /
मन्त्रब्राह्मणकल्पैश्च निगमैः शुद्धविस्तरैः //
text_mt: Because it expresses what is long past, it is a formulation of an ancient myth, / through mantras, brāhmaṇas, and kalpas, and through pure, extensive sacred scriptures.

sanskrit_iast:
aniścitya kṛtāmāhurvyavadhāraṇakalpanām /
yathā hīdaṃ tathā tadvai idaṃ caiva tathaiva tat //
meaning:
अनिश्चित्य कृतामाहुर्व्यवधारणकल्पनाम् /
यथा हीदं तथा तद्वै इदं चैव तथैव तत् //
text_mt: An arrangement made without final determination they call "determination of meaning" [vyavadhāraṇakalpanā]. / "Just as this is, so indeed is that; and this is just like that"—

sanskrit_iast:
ityevameṣā hyupamā daśamo brāhmaṇasya tu /
ityetadbrahmaṇasyādau vihitaṃ rakṣaṇaṃ budhaiḥ //
meaning:
इत्येवमेषा ह्युपमा दशमो ब्राह्मणस्य तु /
इत्येतद्ब्रह्मणस्यादौ विहितं रक्षणं बुधैः //
text_mt: thus this "simile" [upamā] is indeed the tenth [characteristic] of the brāhmaṇa. / In this way, this definition of the brāhmaṇa was ordained at the beginning by the wise.

sanskrit_iast:
tasya tadvidbhiruddiṣṭā vyākhyāmyanupadaṃ dvijaiḥ /
mantrāṇāṃ kalpanā caiva vidhidṛṣṭiṣu karmasu //
meaning:
तस्य तद्विद्भिरुद्दिष्टा व्याख्याम्यनुपदं द्विजैः /
मन्त्राणां कल्पना चैव विधिदृष्टिषु कर्मसु //
text_mt: Its explanation is expounded word by word by twice-born experts, / as well as the arrangement of mantras in rituals seen in injunctions.

sanskrit_iast:
mantro mantrayaterddhātorbrāhmaṇo brāhmaṇena tu /
alpākṣaramasaṃdigdhaṃ sāravadviśvatomukham /
astobhamanavadyaṃ ca sūtraṃ sūtravido viduḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte pūrvabhāge dvitīye 'nuṣaṅgapāde ṛṣilakṣaṇaṃ nāma trayastrinttamo 'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
मन्त्रो मन्त्रयतेर्द्धातोर्ब्राह्मणो ब्राह्मणेन तु /
अल्पाक्षरमसंदिग्धं सारवद्विश्वतोमुखम् /
अस्तोभमनवद्यं च सूत्रं सूत्रविदो विदुः //
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते पूर्वभागे द्वितीये ऽनुषङ्गपादे ऋषिलक्षणं नाम त्रयस्त्रिन्त्तमो ऽध्यायः
text_mt:
"Mantra" is from the root mantr- [to deliberate]; a brāhmaṇa [is explained] by means of a brāhmaṇa. / Having few syllables, free from ambiguity, containing the essence, facing in all directions, / free from superfluous words, and faultless: [such] the knowers of aphorisms understand an aphorism to be.

Thus ends the thirty-third chapter, named "The Definition of a Seer", in the second [section], the Anuṣaṅgapāda, in the first part of the venerable Brahmāṇḍa Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

sanskrit_iast:
vāyuruvāca
ṛṣayastadvacaḥ śrutvā sūtamāhustaduttaram /
kathaṃ vedāḥ punarvyastāstanno brūhi mahāmate //
meaning:
वायुरुवाच
ऋषयस्तद्वचः श्रुत्वा सूतमाहुस्तदुत्तरम् /
कथं वेदाः पुनर्व्यस्तास्तन्नो ब्रूहि महामते //
text_mt: Vāyu said: / Having heard those words, the seers addressed the bard in reply: / "How were the Vedas divided once again? Tell us that, O noble-minded one!"

sanskrit_iast:
sūta uvāca
dvāpare tu purāvṛtte manoḥ svāyaṃbhuvāntare /
brahmā manumuvācedaṃ rakṣavedaṃ mahāmate //
meaning:
सूत उवाच
द्वापरे तु पुरावृत्ते मनोः स्वायंभुवान्तरे /
ब्रह्मा मनुमुवाचेदं रक्षवेदं महामते //
text_mt: The bard said: / In the Dvāpara age that occurred formerly in the Svāyambhuva manvantara, / Brahmā said this to Manu: "Protect the Veda, O noble-minded one!

sanskrit_iast:
parivṛttaṃ yugaṃ tāta svalpavīryā dvijātayaḥ /
saṃvṛtā yugadoṣeṇa sarve caiva yathākramam //
meaning:
परिवृत्तं युगं तात स्वल्पवीर्या द्विजातयः /
संवृता युगदोषेण सर्वे चैव यथाक्रमम् //
text_mt: The age has turned, my son; the twice-born are of little strength, / and all are afflicted in regular order by the defect of the age.

sanskrit_iast:
tasya mānaṃ yugavaśādalpaṃ caiva hi dṛśyate /
daśasāhasrabhāgena hyavaśiṣṭaṃ kṛtoditam //
meaning:
तस्य मानं युगवशादल्पं चैव हि दृश्यते /
दशसाहस्रभागेन ह्यवशिष्टं कृतोदितम् //
text_mt: Its measure is seen to be diminished through the influence of the yuga, / for what was proclaimed in the Kṛta age remains only to the extent of a ten-thousandth part.

sanskrit_iast:
vāya tejo balaṃ cālpaṃ sarvaṃ caiva praṇaśyati /
vedakriyā hi kāryāḥ syurmābhūdvedavināśanam //
meaning:
वाय तेजो बलं चाल्पं सर्वं चैव प्रणश्यति /
वेदक्रिया हि कार्याः स्युर्माभूद्वेदविनाशनम् //
text_mt: Life span, brilliance, and strength are small, and everything perishes. / Vedic rituals must certainly be performed, lest the destruction of the Veda take place.

sanskrit_iast:
vede nāśamanuprāpte yajño nāśaṃ gamiṣyati /
yajñe naṣṭe vedanāśastataḥ sarvaṃ praṇaśyati //
meaning:
वेदे नाशमनुप्राप्ते यज्ञो नाशं गमिष्यति /
यज्ञे नष्टे वेदनाशस्ततः सर्वं प्रणश्यति //
text_mt: When the Veda meets with destruction, sacrifice will go to destruction. / When sacrifice is destroyed, there is destruction of the Veda, and then everything perishes.

sanskrit_iast:
ādyo vedaśca tuṣpādaḥ śatasāhasrasaṃmitaḥ /
punardaśaguṇaḥ kṛṣṇo yajño vai sarvakāmadhuk //
meaning:
आद्यो वेदश्च तुष्पादः शतसाहस्रसंमितः /
पुनर्दशगुणः कृष्णो यज्ञो वै सर्वकामधुक् //
text_mt: The original Veda had four parts and measured a hundred thousand [verses]. / Again, the black sacrifice yields all desires tenfold."

sanskrit_iast:
evamuktastathetyuktvā manurlaukahite rataḥ /
vedamekaṃ catuṣpādaṃ caturddhā vyabhajatprabhuḥ //
meaning:
एवमुक्तस्तथेत्युक्त्वा मनुर्लौकहिते रतः /
वेदमेकं चतुष्पादं चतुर्द्धा व्यभजत्प्रभुः //
text_mt: Having been spoken to thus, saying "So be it," Manu, devoted to the welfare of the world, / the lord divided the single four-part Veda into four.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmaṇo vacanāttāta lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā /
tadahaṃ varttamānena yuṣmākaṃ vedakalpanam //
meaning:
ब्रह्मणो वचनात्तात लोकानां हितकाम्यया /
तदहं वर्त्तमानेन युष्माकं वेदकल्पनम् //
text_mt: By Brahmā's word, my son, out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds, / I shall tell you the arrangement of the Veda according to the present

sanskrit_iast:
manvantareṇa vakṣyami vyatītānāṃ prakalpanam /
pratyakṣeṇa varokṣaṃvai tannibodhata sattamāḥ //
meaning:
मन्वन्तरेण वक्ष्यमि व्यतीतानां प्रकल्पनम् /
प्रत्यक्षेण वरोक्षंवै तन्निबोधत सत्तमाः //
text_mt: manvantara, [which also explains] the arrangement of those past; / perceive that which is imperceptible by means of the perceptible, O best of men!

sanskrit_iast:
asminyuge tadā vyāsaḥ pārāśaryaḥ parantapaḥ /
dvaipāyana iti khyāto viṣṇoraṃśaḥ sanātanaḥ //
meaning:
अस्मिन्युगे तदा व्यासः पाराशर्यः परन्तपः /
द्वैपायन इति ख्यातो विष्णोरंशः सनातनः //
text_mt: In this yuga, the Vyāsa was Parāśara's son, scorcher of foes, / known as Dvaipāyana, the eternal portion of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmaṇā coditaḥ so 'smin vedaṃ vaktuṃ pracakrame /
atha śiṣyānsajagrāha caturo vedakāraṇāt //
meaning:
ब्रह्मणा चोदितः सो ऽस्मिन् वेदं वक्तुं प्रचक्रमे /
अथ शिष्यान्सजग्राह चतुरो वेदकारणात् //
text_mt: Prompted by Brahmā, he set out to speak the Veda in this [age]; / then he took four disciples for the sake of the Vedas:

sanskrit_iast:
jaiminiṃ ca sumantuṃ ca vaiśaṃpāyanameva ca /
caturthaṃ pailameteṣāṃ pañcamaṃ lomaharṣaṇam //
meaning:
जैमिनिं च सुमन्तुं च वैशंपायनमेव च /
चतुर्थं पैलमेतेषां पञ्चमं लोमहर्षणम् //
text_mt: Jaimini, Sumantu, and Vaiśampāyana, / Paila as the fourth of these, and Lomaharṣaṇa as the fifth.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛgvedaśrāvakaṃ pailamagrahīdvidhivaddvijāḥ /
yajurvedapravaktāraṃ vaiśaṃpāyanameva ca //
meaning:
ऋग्वेदश्रावकं पैलमग्रहीद्विधिवद्द्विजाः /
यजुर्वेदप्रवक्तारं वैशंपायनमेव च //
text_mt: He duly took Paila as the reciter of the Ṛgveda, O twice-born ones, / and Vaiśampāyana as the proclaimer of the Yajurveda.

sanskrit_iast:
jaiminiṃ sāmavedārthaśrāvakaṃ so 'nvapadyata /
tathaivāthar vavedasya sumantumṛṣisattamam //
meaning:
जैमिनिं सामवेदार्थश्रावकं सो ऽन्वपद्यत /
तथैवाथर् ववेदस्य सुमन्तुमृषिसत्तमम् //
text_mt: He took Jaimini as the reciter of the meaning of the Sāmaveda, / and likewise Sumantu, the best of seers, for the Atharvaveda.

sanskrit_iast:
itihāsapurāṇasya kalapavākyasya caiva hi /
māṃ caiva pratijagrāha bhagavānīśvaraḥ prabhuḥ //
meaning:
इतिहासपुराणस्य कलपवाक्यस्य चैव हि /
मां चैव प्रतिजग्राह भगवानीश्वरः प्रभुः //
text_mt: And for the itihāsa and Purāṇa, and for the texts of the rituals, / the blessed lord, the master, accepted me.

sanskrit_iast:
eka āsīdyajurvedastaṃ caturddhā vyakalpayat /
cāturhetramabhūttasmiṃstena yajñamakalpayat //
meaning:
एक आसीद्यजुर्वेदस्तं चतुर्द्धा व्यकल्पयत् /
चातुर्हेत्रमभूत्तस्मिंस्तेन यज्ञमकल्पयत् //
text_mt: The Yajurveda was one; he arranged it into four parts. / The office of the four priests existed in it, and with it he arranged the sacrifice:

sanskrit_iast:
ādhvaryavaṃ yajurbhistu ṛgbhirhetraṃ tathaiva ca /
audgātraṃ sāmabhiścakre brahmatvaṃ cāpyatharvabhiḥ //
meaning:
आध्वर्यवं यजुर्भिस्तु ऋग्भिर्हेत्रं तथैव च /
औद्गात्रं सामभिश्चक्रे ब्रह्मत्वं चाप्यथर्वभिः //
text_mt: the duties of the adhvaryu through the yajus mantras, and the duties of the hotṛ through the ṛc mantras, / the duties of the udgātṛ through the sāman mantras, and the duties of the brahman priest through the atharvan mantras.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ sa ṛca uddhṛtya ṛgvedaṃ samakalpayat /
hotṛkaṃ kalpayattena yajurvedaṃ jagatpatiḥ //
meaning:
ततः स ऋच उद्धृत्य ऋग्वेदं समकल्पयत् /
होतृकं कल्पयत्तेन यजुर्वेदं जगत्पतिः //
text_mt: Then, having extracted the ṛc verses, he arranged the Ṛgveda; / with it, the lord of the world arranged the hotṛ's duties [and also] the Yajurveda.

sanskrit_iast:
sāmabhiḥ sāmavedaṃ ca tenaudgātramakalpayat /
rā5stvatharvavedena sarvakarmāṇyakārayat //
meaning:
सामभिः सामवेदं च तेनौद्गात्रमकल्पयत् /
रा5स्त्वथर्ववेदेन सर्वकर्माण्यकारयत् //
text_mt: With the sāmans [he arranged] the Sāmaveda, and with it he arranged the udgātṛ's duties; / and through the Atharvaveda the king caused all rites to be performed.

sanskrit_iast:
ākhyānaiścāpyupākhyānairgāthābhiḥ kalpajoktibhiḥ /
purāmasaṃhitāṃ cakre purāṇārthaviśāradaḥ //
meaning:
आख्यानैश्चाप्युपाख्यानैर्गाथाभिः कल्पजोक्तिभिः /
पुरामसंहितां चक्रे पुराणार्थविशारदः //
text_mt: With narratives, secondary narratives, verses, and sayings from the kalpas, / he who was skilled in the meaning of the Purāṇas made the Purāṇa collection.

sanskrit_iast:
yacchiṣṭaṃ tu yajurvede tena ya5mayuñjata /
yajanātsa yajurveda iti śāstraviniścayaḥ //
meaning:
यच्छिष्टं तु यजुर्वेदे तेन य5मयुञ्जत /
यजनात्स यजुर्वेद इति शास्त्रविनिश्चयः //
text_mt: What remained in the Yajurveda, with that they performed the sacrifice. / Because of sacrificial offering (yajana) it is the Yajurveda: such is the conclusion of the scriptures.

sanskrit_iast:
pādānāmuddhatatvācca yajūṃṣi viṣamāṇi ca /
śatenoddhatavīryastu ṛtvigbhirvedapāragaiḥ //
meaning:
पादानामुद्धतत्वाच्च यजूंषि विषमाणि च /
शतेनोद्धतवीर्यस्तु ऋत्विग्भिर्वेदपारगैः //
text_mt: And because the verses are uneven and the Yajus formulas irregular, / with a hundredfold raised energy, by the priests who have mastered the Vedas,

sanskrit_iast:
prayujyate hyaśvamedhastena vā puṣyate tu saḥ /
ṛco gṛhītvā pailastu vyabhajattu dvidhā punaḥ //
meaning:
प्रयुज्यते ह्यश्वमेधस्तेन वा पुष्यते तु सः /
ऋचो गृहीत्वा पैलस्तु व्यभजत्तु द्विधा पुनः //
text_mt: the horse sacrifice is performed, or by that it is enriched. / Taking the ṛc verses, Paila divided them again into two.

sanskrit_iast:
dve kṛtvā saṃhite caiva śiṣyābhyā madadādvibuḥ /
indrapramattaye caikāṃ dvitīyāṃ bāṣkalāya ca //
meaning:
द्वे कृत्वा संहिते चैव शिष्याभ्या मददाद्विबुः /
इन्द्रप्रमत्तये चैकां द्वितीयां बाष्कलाय च //
text_mt: Having made two collections, the lord gave them to his two disciples: / one to Indrapramati and the second to Bāṣkala.

sanskrit_iast:
catasraḥ saṃhitāḥ kṛtvā bāṣkalo dvijasattamaḥ /
śiṣyānadhyāpayā māsa śuśruṣābhiratānhitān //
meaning:
चतस्रः संहिताः कृत्वा बाष्कलो द्विजसत्तमः /
शिष्यानध्यापया मास शुश्रुषाभिरतान्हितान् //
text_mt: Having made four collections, Bāṣkala, the best of the twice-born, / taught them to his disciples, who were devoted to obedience and well-disposed:

sanskrit_iast:
bodhyāṃ tu prathamāṃ śākhāṃ dvitīyāmagnimātaram /
pārāśarīṃ tṛtīyāṃ tu yā5valkyāmathāparām //
meaning:
बोध्यां तु प्रथमां शाखां द्वितीयामग्निमातरम् /
पाराशरीं तृतीयां तु या5वल्क्यामथापराम् //
text_mt: the Bodhya recension as the first, the Agnimāṭhara as the second, / the Pārāśarī as the third, and the Yājñavalkyā as the other.

sanskrit_iast:
indrapramatirekāṃ tu saṃhitāmṛṣisattamaḥ /
adhyāpayanmahābhāgaṃ māṇḍūkeyaṃ yaśasvinam //
meaning:
इन्द्रप्रमतिरेकां तु संहितामृषिसत्तमः /
अध्यापयन्महाभागं माण्डूकेयं यशस्विनम् //
text_mt: Indrapramati, the best of sages, taught his single / collection to the highly fortunate and renowned Māṇḍūkeya.

sanskrit_iast:
styasravasamagryaṃ tu putraṃ sa tu mahāyaśāḥ /
satyasravāḥ satyahitaṃ putramadhyāpayadvibhuḥ //
meaning:
स्त्यस्रवसमग्र्यं तु पुत्रं स तु महायशाः /
सत्यस्रवाः सत्यहितं पुत्रमध्यापयद्विभुः //
text_mt: He of great renown [taught] his foremost son Satyaśravas, / and the powerful Satyaśravas taught his son Satyahita.

sanskrit_iast:
so 'pi satyahitaḥ putraṃ punaradhyāpayaddvijāḥ /
satyaśriyaṃ mahātmānaṃ satya dharmaparāyaṇam //
meaning:
सो ऽपि सत्यहितः पुत्रं पुनरध्यापयद्द्विजाः /
सत्यश्रियं महात्मानं सत्य धर्मपरायणम् //
text_mt: That Satyahita, O twice-born, again taught his son, / the great-souled Satyaśrī, devoted to truth and righteousness.

sanskrit_iast:
abhavaṃstasya śiṣyā vai trayastu sumahaujasaḥ /
satyaśriyāśca vidvāṃsaḥ śāstragrahaṇatatparāḥ //
meaning:
अभवंस्तस्य शिष्या वै त्रयस्तु सुमहौजसः /
सत्यश्रियाश्च विद्वांसः शास्त्रग्रहणतत्पराः //
text_mt: He had three disciples of exceedingly great splendour, / and belonging to Satyaśrī were these learned men devoted to receiving the scriptures:

sanskrit_iast:
śākalyaḥ prathamasteṣāṃ tasmādanyo rathītaraḥ /
bāṣkaliśca bharadvāja iti śākhāpravarttakāḥ //
meaning:
शाकल्यः प्रथमस्तेषां तस्मादन्यो रथीतरः /
बाष्कलिश्च भरद्वाज इति शाखाप्रवर्त्तकाः //
text_mt: Śākalya was the first of them, another after him was Rāthītara, / and Bāṣkali, and Bharadvāja: these were the founders of recensions.

sanskrit_iast:
devamitrastu śākalyo jñānāhaṅkāragarvitaḥ /
janakasya sa yajñe vai vināśāmagamaddvijāḥ //
meaning:
देवमित्रस्तु शाकल्यो ज्ञानाहङ्कारगर्वितः /
जनकस्य स यज्ञे वै विनाशामगमद्द्विजाः //
text_mt: Devamitra Śākalya, puffed up with pride in his knowledge, / went to destruction at the sacrifice of Janaka, O twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
śāṃśapāyana uvāca
kathaṃ vināśamagamatsa munirjñānagarvitaḥ /
janakasyāśvamedhe tu katha vādābhyajāyata //
meaning:
शांशपायन उवाच
कथं विनाशमगमत्स मुनिर्ज्ञानगर्वितः /
जनकस्याश्वमेधे तु कथ वादाभ्यजायत //
text_mt: Śāṃśapāyana said: / How did that sage, proud of his knowledge, go to destruction? / And how did the debate arise at the horse sacrifice of Janaka?

sanskrit_iast:
kimarthaṃ vābhavadvādaḥ kena sārddhamathāpi vā /
etatsarvaṃ yathā vṛttamācakṣtra viditaṃ tava //
meaning:
किमर्थं वाभवद्वादः केन सार्द्धमथापि वा /
एतत्सर्वं यथा वृत्तमाचक्ष्त्र विदितं तव //
text_mt: For what purpose did the debate take place, or with whom? / Relate all this as it happened, for it is known to you.

sanskrit_iast:
sūta uvāca
janakasyāśvamedhe tu mahānāsītsamāgamaḥ /
ṛṣīṇāṃ hi sahasrāṇi tatrājagmuranekaśaḥ //
meaning:
सूत उवाच
जनकस्याश्वमेधे तु महानासीत्समागमः /
ऋषीणां हि सहस्राणि तत्राजग्मुरनेकशः //
text_mt: The bard said: / At the horse sacrifice of Janaka there was a great gathering; / thousands of sages arrived there in great numbers.

sanskrit_iast:
rājarṣerjanakasyātha taṃ yajñaṃ hi didṛkṣavaḥ /
āgatānbrāhmaṇāndṛṣṭvā jijñāsāsyābhavattataḥ //
meaning:
राजर्षेर्जनकस्याथ तं यज्ञं हि दिदृक्षवः /
आगतान्ब्राह्मणान्दृष्ट्वा जिज्ञासास्याभवत्ततः //
text_mt: Desiring to see that sacrifice of the royal sage Janaka, / and seeing the brāhmaṇas who had arrived, a desire to know arose in him:

sanskrit_iast:
ko nveṣāṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhaḥ kathaṃ me niścayo bhavet /
iti niścitya manasā buddhiṃ cakre janādhipaḥ //
meaning:
को न्वेषां ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठः कथं मे निश्चयो भवेत् /
इति निश्चित्य मनसा बुद्धिं चक्रे जनाधिपः //
text_mt: ‘Who among these is the foremost brāhmaṇa? How may I be certain?’ / Having considered this in his mind, the lord of men formed a plan.

sanskrit_iast:
gavāṃ sahasramādāya suvarṇamadhikaṃ tataḥ /
grāmānratnāni dāsīscha munīnprāha narādhipaḥ //
meaning:
गवां सहस्रमादाय सुवर्णमधिकं ततः /
ग्रामान्रत्नानि दासीस्छ मुनीन्प्राह नराधिपः //
text_mt: Gathering a thousand cows, and gold beyond that, / villages, jewels, and female slaves, the king said to the sages:

sanskrit_iast:
sarvānahaṃ prapanno vaḥ śirasā śreṣṭhabhāginaḥ /
yadetadāhṛtaṃ vittaṃ yo vā śreṣṭhatamo bhavet //
meaning:
सर्वानहं प्रपन्नो वः शिरसा श्रेष्ठभागिनः /
यदेतदाहृतं वित्तं यो वा श्रेष्ठतमो भवेत् //
text_mt: ‘I bow with my head to all of you, who possess the highest merit. / Whoever is the foremost, this wealth that has been brought—

sanskrit_iast:
tasmai tadupanītaṃ me vitta vittaṃ dvijottamāḥ /
janakasya vacaḥ śrutvā ṛṣayaste śrutikṣamāḥ //
meaning:
तस्मै तदुपनीतं मे वित्त वित्तं द्विजोत्तमाः /
जनकस्य वचः श्रुत्वा ऋषयस्ते श्रुतिक्षमाः //
text_mt: know, O best of the twice-born, that this wealth has been brought for him.’ / Hearing the words of Janaka, those sages capable of [hearing] the revealed scriptures,

sanskrit_iast:
dṛṣṭvā dhanaṃ mahāsāraṃ dhanagṛdhnā jighṛkṣavaḥ /
āhvayāñcakrire 'nyonyaṃ vedajñānamadolbaṇān //
meaning:
दृष्ट्वा धनं महासारं धनगृध्ना जिघृक्षवः /
आह्वयाञ्चक्रिरे ऽन्योन्यं वेदज्ञानमदोल्बणान् //
text_mt: seeing the wealth of great value, being greedy for wealth and wishing to seize it, / challenged one another, swollen with pride in their knowledge of the Vedas.

sanskrit_iast:
manasā gatavittāste mamaitaddhanamityuta /
mamaitanna tavetyanyo brūhi vā kiṃ vikatthase //
meaning:
मनसा गतवित्तास्ते ममैतद्धनमित्युत /
ममैतन्न तवेत्यन्यो ब्रूहि वा किं विकत्थसे //
text_mt: With minds fixed on the wealth, [they cried,] ‘This wealth is mine!’ / ‘It is mine, not yours!’ [shouted] another; ‘Speak, why do you boast?’

sanskrit_iast:
ityevaṃ dhanadoṣeṇa vādāṃścakuranekaśaḥ /
athānyastatravai vidvānbrahmaṇastu sutaḥ kaviḥ //
meaning:
इत्येवं धनदोषेण वादांश्चकुरनेकशः /
अथान्यस्तत्रवै विद्वान्ब्रह्मणस्तु सुतः कविः //
text_mt: Thus, through the fault of wealth, they engaged in many debates. / Then another wise sage was there, a poet, son of Brahmā,

sanskrit_iast:
yājñavalkyo mahātejāstapasvī brahmavittamaḥ /
brahmaṇoṃ'śasamutpanno vākyaṃ provāca susvaram //
meaning:
याज्ञवल्क्यो महातेजास्तपस्वी ब्रह्मवित्तमः /
ब्रह्मणोंऽशसमुत्पन्नो वाक्यं प्रोवाच सुस्वरम् //
text_mt: Yājñavalkya, of great splendour, an ascetic, the foremost of knowers of Brahman, / born from a portion of Brahmā; he spoke in a clear voice

sanskrit_iast:
śiṣyaṃ brahmavidāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dhanametadgṛhāṇa vai /
nayasva ca gṛhaṃvatsa mamaitannātra saṃśayaḥ //
meaning:
शिष्यं ब्रह्मविदां श्रेष्ठं धनमेतद्गृहाण वै /
नयस्व च गृहंवत्स ममैतन्नात्र संशयः //
text_mt: to his disciple, the best of knowers of Brahman: ‘Take this wealth, / and bring it home, child; it is mine, there is no doubt about this.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvavādeṣvahaṃ vaktā nānyaḥ kaścittu matsamaḥ /
yo vā na prīyate vidvānsamāhvayatu māciram //
meaning:
सर्ववादेष्वहं वक्ता नान्यः कश्चित्तु मत्समः /
यो वा न प्रीयते विद्वान्समाह्वयतु माचिरम् //
text_mt: In all debates I will speak; no other is equal to me. / Or whichever scholar is not pleased, let him challenge me without delay.’

sanskrit_iast:
tato brahmārṇavaḥ kṣubdaḥ samudra iva saṃplave /
tānuvāca tataḥ svastho yājñavalkyo hasanniva //
meaning:
ततो ब्रह्मार्णवः क्षुब्दः समुद्र इव संप्लवे /
तानुवाच ततः स्वस्थो याज्ञवल्क्यो हसन्निव //
text_mt: Then the ocean of sacred lore became agitated, like the ocean at the dissolution of the world. / Then, undisturbed, Yājñavalkya said to them, as if smiling:

sanskrit_iast:
krodhaṃ mā kārṣṭa vidvāṃso bhavantaḥ satyavādinaḥ /
vadāmahe yathāśakti jijñāsaṃtaḥ parasparam //
meaning:
क्रोधं मा कार्ष्ट विद्वांसो भवन्तः सत्यवादिनः /
वदामहे यथाशक्ति जिज्ञासंतः परस्परम् //
text_mt: ‘Do not be angry, O learned ones, you who speak the truth. / We shall speak according to our ability, inquiring into each other [’s knowledge].’

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'bhyupagatāsteṣāṃ vādāḥ śabdairanekaśaḥ /
sahasradhā śubhairarthaiḥ sukṣmadarśanasaṃbhavaiḥ //
meaning:
ततो ऽभ्युपगतास्तेषां वादाः शब्दैरनेकशः /
सहस्रधा शुभैरर्थैः सुक्ष्मदर्शनसंभवैः //
text_mt: Then debates among them began with many words, / in a thousand ways, with noble meanings born of subtle perception,

sanskrit_iast:
loke vede tathādhyātmavidyāsthānairalaṅkṛtaiḥ /
saṃtyuttamaguṇairyuktā nṛpasyāpi parīkṣakāḥ //
meaning:
लोके वेदे तथाध्यात्मविद्यास्थानैरलङ्कृतैः /
संत्युत्तमगुणैर्युक्ता नृपस्यापि परीक्षकाः //
text_mt: in worldly lore, in the Veda, and adorned with the seats of knowledge of the supreme Self, / endowed with the highest qualities, tested even by the king.

sanskrit_iast:
vādāḥ samabhavaṃstatra dhanahetormahātmanām /
ṛṣayastvekataḥ sarve yājñavalkyastathaikataḥ //
meaning:
वादाः समभवंस्तत्र धनहेतोर्महात्मनाम् /
ऋषयस्त्वेकतः सर्वे याज्ञवल्क्यस्तथैकतः //
text_mt: Debates arose there for the sake of wealth among the great-souled ones; / all the sages were on one side, and Yājñavalkya on the other.

sanskrit_iast:
sarve te munayastena yājñavalkyena dhīmatā /
ekaikaśastataḥ pṛṣṭā naivottaramathābruvan //
meaning:
सर्वे ते मुनयस्तेन याज्ञवल्क्येन धीमता /
एकैकशस्ततः पृष्टा नैवोत्तरमथाब्रुवन् //
text_mt: All those sages, questioned one by one / by that wise Yājñavalkya, could give no answer at all.

sanskrit_iast:
sa vijitya munīnsarvān brahmarāśirmahāmatiḥ /
śākalyamiti hovāca vādakarttāramañjasā //
meaning:
स विजित्य मुनीन्सर्वान् ब्रह्मराशिर्महामतिः /
शाकल्यमिति होवाच वादकर्त्तारमञ्जसा //
text_mt: Having conquered all the sages, that great-minded heap of sacred knowledge / directly addressed Śākalya, the challenger in debate:

sanskrit_iast:
śākalya vada vaktavyaṃ kiṃ dhyāyannavatiṣṭhase /
paṇastu yajamānena baddho nīto yathā dhṛtaḥ //
meaning:
शाकल्य वद वक्तव्यं किं ध्यायन्नवतिष्ठसे /
पणस्तु यजमानेन बद्धो नीतो यथा धृतः //
text_mt: ‘Śākalya, speak what is to be spoken! Why do you stand meditating? / The wager set by the sacrificer has been taken, held as it was.’

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ sa dharṣitastena roṣāttāmrāsyalocanaḥ /
provāca yājñavalkyaṃ sapuruṣaṃ munisannidhau //
meaning:
एवं स धर्षितस्तेन रोषात्ताम्रास्यलोचनः /
प्रोवाच याज्ञवल्क्यं सपुरुषं मुनिसन्निधौ //
text_mt: Thus assailed by him, with eyes and face red with rage, / he spoke harshly to Yājñavalkya in the presence of the sages:

sanskrit_iast:
tvamasmāstṛṇavatkṛtvā tathaivānyāndvijottamān /
vidyādhanaṃ mahāsāraṃ svayaṅgrāhaṃ jighṛkṣasi //
meaning:
त्वमस्मास्तृणवत्कृत्वा तथैवान्यान्द्विजोत्तमान् /
विद्याधनं महासारं स्वयङ्ग्राहं जिघृक्षसि //
text_mt: ‘Treating us and other best twice-born as mere straw, / do you wish to seize the wealth of learning, this great prize, by self-selection?’

sanskrit_iast:
śākalyenaivamuktastu yājñavalkyastamabravīt /
brahmiṣṭhānāṃ balaṃ viddhi vidyātattvārthadarśanam //
meaning:
शाकल्येनैवमुक्तस्तु याज्ञवल्क्यस्तमब्रवीत् /
ब्रह्मिष्ठानां बलं विद्धि विद्यातत्त्वार्थदर्शनम् //
text_mt: Thus addressed by Śākalya, Yājñavalkya said to him: / ‘Know that the strength of those who are most grounded in Brahman is insight into the true meaning of knowledge.

sanskrit_iast:
kāmasyārthena saṃbandhastenārthaṃ kāmayāmahe /
kāmaprarśnadhanā viprāḥ kāmapraśnaṃ vadāmahe //
meaning:
कामस्यार्थेन संबन्धस्तेनार्थं कामयामहे /
कामप्रर्श्नधना विप्राः कामप्रश्नं वदामहे //
text_mt: Desire is linked with wealth; therefore we desire wealth. / The brāhmaṇas have the wealth of answering questions at will; we will answer questions at will.

sanskrit_iast:
paṇaścaivāsya rājarṣestasmānnītaṃ dhanaṃ mayā /
etacchrutvā vacastasya śākalyaḥ krodhamūrcchitaḥ //
meaning:
पणश्चैवास्य राजर्षेस्तस्मान्नीतं धनं मया /
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य शाकल्यः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः //
text_mt: And it was the wager of this royal sage; therefore the wealth was taken by me.’ / Hearing these words of his, Śākalya was overcome with anger.

sanskrit_iast:
yā5valkyamathovāca kāmapraśnārthakṛdvacaḥ /
brūhīdānīṃ mayoddiṣṭānkāmapraśnānyathārthataḥ //
meaning:
या5वल्क्यमथोवाच कामप्रश्नार्थकृद्वचः /
ब्रूहीदानीं मयोद्दिष्टान्कामप्रश्नान्यथार्थतः //
text_mt: Then he spoke words aimed at questioning him at will to Yājñavalkya: / ‘Answer now, in accordance with the truth, the questions at will posed by me.’

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ samabhavadvādastayorbrahmavidormahān /
sāgraṃ praśnasahasraṃ tu śākalyaḥ so 'karottadā //
meaning:
ततः समभवद्वादस्तयोर्ब्रह्मविदोर्महान् /
साग्रं प्रश्नसहस्रं तु शाकल्यः सो ऽकरोत्तदा //
text_mt: Then a great debate arose between those two knowers of Brahman; / Śākalya then posed more than a thousand questions.

sanskrit_iast:
yājñavalkyo 'bravītsarvamṛṣīṇāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ tadā /
śākalyastvāsa nirvādo yājñavalkyastamabravīt //
meaning:
याज्ञवल्क्यो ऽब्रवीत्सर्वमृषीणां शृण्वतां तदा /
शाकल्यस्त्वास निर्वादो याज्ञवल्क्यस्तमब्रवीत् //
text_mt: Yājñavalkya explained everything while the sages listened. / Śākalya was left without an argument, and Yājñavalkya said to him:

sanskrit_iast:
praśnamekaṃ mamāpi tvaṃ śākalya vada kāmikam /
paṇaprāpyasya vādasya bruvatormṛtyuratra vai //
meaning:
प्रश्नमेकं ममापि त्वं शाकल्य वद कामिकम् /
पणप्राप्यस्य वादस्य ब्रुवतोर्मृत्युरत्र वै //
text_mt: ‘Answer, Śākalya, also one optional question of mine; / in this debate where a wager is to be gained, for the one who speaks [falsely] there is death here:

sanskrit_iast:
susūkṣmajñānasaṃyuktaṃ sāṃkhyaṃyogamathāpi vā /
adhyātmasya gatiṃ mukhyāṃ dhyānamārgamathāpi vā //
meaning:
सुसूक्ष्मज्ञानसंयुक्तं सांख्यंयोगमथापि वा /
अध्यात्मस्य गतिं मुख्यां ध्यानमार्गमथापि वा //
text_mt: joined with very subtle knowledge, whether Sāṅkhya or Yoga, / or the principal path of the inner Self, or the way of meditation.’

sanskrit_iast:
atha saṃcoditaḥ praśno yājñavalkyena dhīmatā /
śākalyastamavijñāya tathā mṛtyumavāptavān //
meaning:
अथ संचोदितः प्रश्नो याज्ञवल्क्येन धीमता /
शाकल्यस्तमविज्ञाय तथा मृत्युमवाप्तवान् //
text_mt: Then the question was urged by the wise Yājñavalkya; / Śākalya, unable to understand it, met with death in that manner.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ smṛtaḥ sa śākalyaḥ praśnavyākhyānapīḍitaḥ /
evaṃ vivādaḥ sumahānāsītteṣāṃ dhanārthinām //
meaning:
एवं स्मृतः स शाकल्यः प्रश्नव्याख्यानपीडितः /
एवं विवादः सुमहानासीत्तेषां धनार्थिनाम् //
text_mt: Thus is Śākalya remembered, afflicted by the explanation of the question. / Such was the great dispute of those seekers of wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣīṇāmṛṣibhiḥ sārddhaṃ yājñavalkyasya caiva hi /
yājñavalkyo dhanaṃ gṛhya yaśo vikhyāya cātmanaḥ /
jagāma vai gṛhaṃ svacchaṃ śiṣyaiḥ parivṛto vaśī //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte pūrvabhāge dvitīye 'nuṣaṅgapāde vyāsaśiṣyotpattivarṇanaṃ nāma catustriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
ऋषीणामृषिभिः सार्द्धं याज्ञवल्क्यस्य चैव हि /
याज्ञवल्क्यो धनं गृह्य यशो विख्याय चात्मनः /
जगाम वै गृहं स्वच्छं शिष्यैः परिवृतो वशी //
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते पूर्वभागे द्वितीये ऽनुषङ्गपादे व्यासशिष्योत्पत्तिवर्णनं नाम चतुस्त्रिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
text_mt:
between the sages with the sages, and also indeed with Yājñavalkya. / Taking the wealth and proclaiming his own renown, / Yājñavalkya, master of his senses, went to his own pure abode surrounded by his disciples.

Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter, called 'Description of the Origin of the Disciples of Vyāsa', in the second part, the Anuṣaṅgapāda, of the first half of the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa, spoken by Vāyu.

sanskrit_iast:
sūta uvāca
devamitraśca śākalyo mahātmā dvijapuṅgavaḥ /
cakāra saṃhitāḥ pañca buddhimānvedavittamaḥ //
meaning:
सूत उवाच
देवमित्रश्च शाकल्यो महात्मा द्विजपुङ्गवः /
चकार संहिताः पञ्च बुद्धिमान्वेदवित्तमः //
text_mt: The Sūta said: / Devamitra Śākalya, that great soul and bull among the twice-born, / intelligent and foremost among knowers of the Veda, created five Saṃhitās.

sanskrit_iast:
pañca tasyābhavañchiṣyā mudgalo gokhalastathā /
khalīyānsutapā vatsaḥ śaiśireyaśca pañcamaḥ //
meaning:
पञ्च तस्याभवञ्छिष्या मुद्गलो गोखलस्तथा /
खलीयान्सुतपा वत्सः शैशिरेयश्च पञ्चमः //
text_mt: His disciples were five: Mudgala and Gokhhala, / Khalīya, Sutapas, Vatsa, and Śaiśireya was the fifth.

sanskrit_iast:
provāca saṃhitāstisraḥ śāko vaiṇo rathītaraḥ /
niruktaṃ ca punaścakre caturthaṃ dvijasattamaḥ //
meaning:
प्रोवाच संहितास्तिस्रः शाको वैणो रथीतरः /
निरुक्तं च पुनश्चक्रे चतुर्थं द्विजसत्तमः //
text_mt: Śākapūrṇa Rathītara taught three Saṃhitās, / and again, that best of the twice-born made a fourth work, the Nirukta.

sanskrit_iast:
tasya śiṣyāstu catvāraḥ pailaścekṣalakastathā /
dhīmāñcha tabalākaśca gajaścaiva dvijottamāḥ //
meaning:
तस्य शिष्यास्तु चत्वारः पैलश्चेक्षलकस्तथा /
धीमाञ्छ तबलाकश्च गजश्चैव द्विजोत्तमाः //
text_mt: His disciples were four, O best of the twice-born: / Paila, Ikṣalaka, / the wise Śatabalāka, and Gaja.

sanskrit_iast:
bāṣkalistu bharadvājastisraḥ provāca saṃhitāḥ /
trayastasyābhavañcchiṣyā mahātmāno guṇānvitāḥ //
meaning:
बाष्कलिस्तु भरद्वाजस्तिस्रः प्रोवाच संहिताः /
त्रयस्तस्याभवञ्च्छिष्या महात्मानो गुणान्विताः //
text_mt: Bāṣkali, son of Bharadvāja, taught three Saṃhitās; / he had three noble and virtuous disciples:

sanskrit_iast:
dhīmāṃśca tvāpanāpaśca pānnagāriśca buddhimān /
tṛtīyaścārjavaste ca tapasā śaṃsitavratāḥ //
meaning:
धीमांश्च त्वापनापश्च पान्नगारिश्च बुद्धिमान् /
तृतीयश्चार्जवस्ते च तपसा शंसितव्रताः //
text_mt: the wise Tāpanāpa, the intelligent Pānnagāri, / and the third was Ārjava; they were steadfast in their vows through austerity,

sanskrit_iast:
vītarāgā mahātejāḥ saṃhitājñānapāragāḥ /
ityete bahūvṛcāḥ proktāḥ saṃhitā yaiḥ pravartitāḥ //
meaning:
वीतरागा महातेजाः संहिताज्ञानपारगाः /
इत्येते बहूवृचाः प्रोक्ताः संहिता यैः प्रवर्तिताः //
text_mt: free from passion, endowed with great splendor, having mastered the knowledge of the Saṃhitās. / Thus these Bahvṛcas have been proclaimed, by whom the Saṃhitās were set forth.

sanskrit_iast:
vaiśaṃpāyanaśiṣyo 'sau yajurvedamakalpayat /
ṣaḍaśītistu tenoktāḥ saṃhitā yajuṣāṃ śubhāḥ //
meaning:
वैशंपायनशिष्यो ऽसौ यजुर्वेदमकल्पयत् /
षडशीतिस्तु तेनोक्ताः संहिता यजुषां शुभाः //
text_mt: That disciple of Vaiśampāyana arranged the Yajurveda; / eighty-six auspicious Saṃhitās of the Yajus were taught by him.

sanskrit_iast:
śiṣyebhyaḥ pradadau tāśca jagūhuste vidhānataḥ /
ekastatra parityakto yā5valkyo mahātapāḥ //
meaning:
शिष्येभ्यः प्रददौ ताश्च जगूहुस्ते विधानतः /
एकस्तत्र परित्यक्तो या5वल्क्यो महातपाः //
text_mt: He gave them to his disciples, and they received them according to rule; / one disciple was abandoned there: the great ascetic Yājñavalkya.

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaḍaśītistathā śiṣyāḥ saṃhitānāṃ vikalpakāḥ /
sarveṣāmeva teṣāṃ vai tridhā bhedāḥ prakīrttitāḥ //
meaning:
षडशीतिस्तथा शिष्याः संहितानां विकल्पकाः /
सर्वेषामेव तेषां वै त्रिधा भेदाः प्रकीर्त्तिताः //
text_mt: Thus eighty-six disciples were arrangers of the Saṃhitās; / of all of them, indeed, threefold divisions are proclaimed.

sanskrit_iast:
tridhā bhedāstu te vedabhede 'sminnavame śubhe /
udīcyā madhyadeśyāśca prācyaścaiva pṛthagvidhāḥ //
meaning:
त्रिधा भेदास्तु ते वेदभेदे ऽस्मिन्नवमे शुभे /
उदीच्या मध्यदेश्याश्च प्राच्यश्चैव पृथग्विधाः //
text_mt: The divisions are threefold in this auspicious ninth Vedic division: / northern, central-country, and eastern, of various kinds.

sanskrit_iast:
śyāmāyanirudīcyānāṃ pradhānaḥ saṃbabhūva ha /
madhyadeśapratiṣṭhātā cāsuriḥ prathamaḥ smṛtaḥ //
meaning:
श्यामायनिरुदीच्यानां प्रधानः संबभूव ह /
मध्यदेशप्रतिष्ठाता चासुरिः प्रथमः स्मृतः //
text_mt: Śyāmāyani was the foremost of the northerners; / Āsuri is remembered as the primary founder of the central country;

sanskrit_iast:
ālaṃbirādiḥ prācyānāṃ trayodeśyādayastu te /
ityete carakāḥ proktāḥ saṃhitā vādino dvijāḥ //
meaning:
आलंबिरादिः प्राच्यानां त्रयोदेश्यादयस्तु ते /
इत्येते चरकाः प्रोक्ताः संहिता वादिनो द्विजाः //
text_mt: Ālambir was the first of the easterners, followed by Trayodaśya and others. / Thus these twice-born Carakas are proclaimed, who profess the Saṃhitās.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
carakādhvaryavaḥ kena kāraṇaṃ brūhi tattvataḥ /
kiṃ cīrṇaṃ kasya vā hetoścarakatvaṃ hi bhejire //
meaning:
ऋषय ऊचुः
चरकाध्वर्यवः केन कारणं ब्रूहि तत्त्वतः /
किं चीर्णं कस्य वा हेतोश्चरकत्वं हि भेजिरे //
text_mt: The sages said: / Why are they called the Caraka Adhvaryus? Tell [us] the reason truly. / What did they practice, or for what purpose did they acquire the status of Carakas?

sanskrit_iast:
sūta uvāca
kāryamāsīdṛṣīṇāṃ ca kiñcidbrāhmaṇasattamāḥ /
merupṛṣṭhaṃ samāsādya taistadā tviti mantritam //
meaning:
सूत उवाच
कार्यमासीदृषीणां च किञ्चिद्ब्राह्मणसत्तमाः /
मेरुपृष्ठं समासाद्य तैस्तदा त्विति मन्त्रितम् //
text_mt: The Sūta said: / The sages had some business to perform, O best of Brahmins; / reaching the top of Mount Meru, they held this agreement at that time:

sanskrit_iast:
yo vātra saptarātreṇa nāgaccheddvijasattamaḥ /
sa kuryādbrahmahatyāṃ vai samayo naḥ prakīrtitaḥ //
meaning:
यो वात्र सप्तरात्रेण नागच्छेद्द्विजसत्तमः /
स कुर्याद्ब्रह्महत्यां वै समयो नः प्रकीर्तितः //
text_mt: 'Whichever best of the twice-born does not arrive here within seven nights, / he will indeed commit the killing of a Brahmin; this is our declared compact.'

sanskrit_iast:
tataste sagaṇāḥ sarve vaiśaṃpāyanavarjitāḥ /
prayayuḥ saptarātreṇa yatra saṃdhiḥ kṛto 'bhavat //
meaning:
ततस्ते सगणाः सर्वे वैशंपायनवर्जिताः /
प्रययुः सप्तरात्रेण यत्र संधिः कृतो ऽभवत् //
text_mt: Then all of them with their retinues, except Vaiśampāyana, / set out within seven nights to where the agreement had been made.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmaṇānāṃ tu vacanādbrahmahatyāṃ cakāra saḥ /
śiṣyānatha samānīya sa vaiśaṃpāyano 'bravīt //
meaning:
ब्रह्मणानां तु वचनाद्ब्रह्महत्यां चकार सः /
शिष्यानथ समानीय स वैशंपायनो ऽब्रवीत् //
text_mt: By the word of the Brahmins, he committed [the sin of] Brahmin-killing. / Then, having gathered his disciples, Vaiśampāyana said:

sanskrit_iast:
brahmahatyāṃ caradhvaṃ vai matkṛte dvijasattamāḥ /
sarve yūyaṃ samāgamya brūta kāmaṃ hitaṃ vacaḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्महत्यां चरध्वं वै मत्कृते द्विजसत्तमाः /
सर्वे यूयं समागम्य ब्रूत कामं हितं वचः //
text_mt: 'Practice [expiation for] the killing of a Brahmin on my behalf, O best of the twice-born! / All of you assemble and speak words that are pleasing and beneficial.'

sanskrit_iast:
yājñavalkya uvāca
ahamekaścariṣyāmi tiṣṭhantu munayastvime /
balenotthāpayiṣyāmi tapasā svena bhāvitaḥ //
meaning:
याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच
अहमेकश्चरिष्यामि तिष्ठन्तु मुनयस्त्विमे /
बलेनोत्थापयिष्यामि तपसा स्वेन भावितः //
text_mt: Yājñavalkya said: / 'I alone will perform it; let these munis remain [at ease]. / Endowed with my own austerity, I will raise [you] up by my power.'

sanskrit_iast:
eva muktastataḥ kruddho yā5valkyama thātyajat /
uvāca yattvayādhītaṃ sarvaṃ pratyarpayasva me //
meaning:
एव मुक्तस्ततः क्रुद्धो या5वल्क्यम थात्यजत् /
उवाच यत्त्वयाधीतं सर्वं प्रत्यर्पयस्व मे //
text_mt: Addressed thus, enraged, [the teacher] then cast off Yājñavalkya. / He said, 'Everything that has been studied by you, return it all to me!'

sanskrit_iast:
evamuktaḥ sarūpāṇi yajūṃṣi gurave dadau /
rudhireṇa tathāktāni ccharditvā brahmavittamāḥ //
meaning:
एवमुक्तः सरूपाणि यजूंषि गुरवे ददौ /
रुधिरेण तथाक्तानि च्छर्दित्वा ब्रह्मवित्तमाः //
text_mt: Thus addressed, having vomited the Yajus formulas endowed with bodily form / and smeared with blood, he gave them to his teacher, O knowers of Brahman!

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ sa dhyānamāsthāya saryamārādhayaddvijaḥ /
sūrye brahma yadutpannaṃ taṃ gatvā pratitiṣṭhati //
meaning:
ततः स ध्यानमास्थाय सर्यमाराधयद्द्विजः /
सूर्ये ब्रह्म यदुत्पन्नं तं गत्वा प्रतितिष्ठति //
text_mt: Then, having taken refuge in meditation, the twice-born [sage] worshipped the sun. / The sacred knowledge that arose in the sun goes and becomes established in him.

sanskrit_iast:
tato yāni gatānyūrdhvaṃ yajūṣyādityamaḍalam /
tāni tasmai dadau tuṣṭaḥ sūryo vai brahmarātaye //
meaning:
ततो यानि गतान्यूर्ध्वं यजूष्यादित्यमडलम् /
तानि तस्मै ददौ तुष्टः सूर्यो वै ब्रह्मरातये //
text_mt: Then, pleased, the Sun indeed gave to Brahmarāti / those Yajus formulas that had risen up into the solar disc.

sanskrit_iast:
aśvarūpāya mārttaṇḍo yājñavaklyāya dhīmate /
yajūṃṣyadhīyate tāni brāhmaṇā yena kenacit //
meaning:
अश्वरूपाय मार्त्तण्डो याज्ञवक्ल्याय धीमते /
यजूंष्यधीयते तानि ब्राह्मणा येन केनचित् //
text_mt: Mārtaṇḍa [gave them] to the wise Yājñavalkya, who had assumed the form of a horse. / Brahmins study those Yajus formulas in whatever way possible.

sanskrit_iast:
aśvarūpāya dattāni tataste vājino 'mavan /
brahmahatyā tu yaiścīrṇā caraṇāccarakāḥ smṛtāḥ //
meaning:
अश्वरूपाय दत्तानि ततस्ते वाजिनो ऽमवन् /
ब्रह्महत्या तु यैश्चीर्णा चरणाच्चरकाः स्मृताः //
text_mt: Because they were given to him who had assumed the form of a horse, they became the Vājins; / and because [the expiation for] Brahmin-killing was practiced by them, they are called Carakas from their wandering (caraṇa).

sanskrit_iast:
vaiśaṃpāyanaśiṣyāste carakāḥ samudāhṛtāḥ /
ityete carakāḥ proktā vājinastu nibodhata //
meaning:
वैशंपायनशिष्यास्ते चरकाः समुदाहृताः /
इत्येते चरकाः प्रोक्ता वाजिनस्तु निबोधत //
text_mt: Those disciples of Vaiśampāyana are declared to be the Carakas. / Thus these Carakas have been spoken of; now learn of the Vājins.

sanskrit_iast:
yā5valkyasya śiṣyāste kaṇvo baudheya eva ca /
madhyandinastu sāpatyo vaidheyaścāddhabauddhakau //
meaning:
या5वल्क्यस्य शिष्यास्ते कण्वो बौधेय एव च /
मध्यन्दिनस्तु सापत्यो वैधेयश्चाद्धबौद्धकौ //
text_mt: Those disciples of Yājñavalkya are Kaṇva and Baudheya, / Mādhyandina, Sāpatya, Vaidheya, and the two Addhabauddhas;

sanskrit_iast:
tāpanīyaśca vatsāśca tathā jābālakevalau /
āvaṭī ca tathā puṇḍro vaiṇoyaḥ saparāśaraḥ //
meaning:
तापनीयश्च वत्साश्च तथा जाबालकेवलौ /
आवटी च तथा पुण्ड्रो वैणोयः सपराशरः //
text_mt: Tāpanīya, the Vatsas, and likewise Jābāla and Kevala, / Āvaṭī, and likewise Puṇḍra, and Vaiṇoya together with Parāśara.

sanskrit_iast:
ityete vājinaḥ proktā daśapañca ca sattamāḥ /
śatamekādhikaṃ jñeyaṃ yajuṣāṃ ye vikalpakāḥ //
meaning:
इत्येते वाजिनः प्रोक्ता दशपञ्च च सत्तमाः /
शतमेकाधिकं ज्ञेयं यजुषां ये विकल्पकाः //
text_mt: Thus these fifteen Vājins are declared to be the best; / one hundred and one are to be known as the arrangers of the Yajus formulas.

sanskrit_iast:
putramadhyāpayāmāsa sumantumatha jaiminiḥ /
sumantuścāpi sutvānaṃ putramadhyāpayatpunaḥ //
meaning:
पुत्रमध्यापयामास सुमन्तुमथ जैमिनिः /
सुमन्तुश्चापि सुत्वानं पुत्रमध्यापयत्पुनः //
text_mt: Then Jaimini taught his son Sumantu, / and Sumantu again taught his son Sutvan.

sanskrit_iast:
sukarmāṇaṃ tataḥ sunvānputramadhyāpayatpunaḥ /
sa sahasramadhītyāśu sukarmāpyatha saṃhitāḥ //
meaning:
सुकर्माणं ततः सुन्वान्पुत्रमध्यापयत्पुनः /
स सहस्रमधीत्याशु सुकर्माप्यथ संहिताः //
text_mt: Sunvān then taught his son Sukarman; / and that Sukarman, having quickly studied a thousand Saṃhitās,

sanskrit_iast:
provācātha sahasrasya sukarmā sūryavarcasaḥ /
anadhyāyeṣvadhīyānāṃstañjaghāna śatakratuḥ //
meaning:
प्रोवाचाथ सहस्रस्य सुकर्मा सूर्यवर्चसः /
अनध्यायेष्वधीयानांस्तञ्जघान शतक्रतुः //
text_mt: Sukarman, possessing the splendor of the sun, taught the thousand [disciples]. / Śatakratu struck them down as they were studying on forbidden study days (anadhyāya).

sanskrit_iast:
prāyopaveśamakarottato 'sau śiṣyakāramāt /
kruddhaṃ dṛṣṭvā tataḥ śakrovaraṃ so 'tha punardadau //
meaning:
प्रायोपवेशमकरोत्ततो ऽसौ शिष्यकारमात् /
क्रुद्धं दृष्ट्वा ततः शक्रोवरं सो ऽथ पुनर्ददौ //
text_mt: Then, on account of his disciples, he resolved to fast unto death; / seeing him enraged, Śakra then granted him a boon again:

sanskrit_iast:
bhaviṣyato mahāvīryauṃ śiṣyau te 'tulavarcasau /
adhīyātāṃ mahāprājñau sahasraṃ saṃhitā ubhau //
meaning:
भविष्यतो महावीर्यौं शिष्यौ ते ऽतुलवर्चसौ /
अधीयातां महाप्राज्ञौ सहस्रं संहिता उभौ //
text_mt: 'Your two disciples will be of great prowess and peerless splendor; / both highly intelligent, they will study the thousand Saṃhitās.'

sanskrit_iast:
ete surā mahābhāgāḥ saṃkruddhā dvijasattama /
ityuktvā vāsavaḥ śrīmānsukarmāṇaṃ yaśasvinam //
meaning:
एते सुरा महाभागाः संक्रुद्धा द्विजसत्तम /
इत्युक्त्वा वासवः श्रीमान्सुकर्माणं यशस्विनम् //
text_mt: 'These gods, O best of the twice-born, were deeply angered.' / Having said this to the renowned Sukarman, the glorious Vāsava,

sanskrit_iast:
śāntakrodhaṃ dvijaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣipramantara dhātprabhuḥ /
tasya śiṣyo 'bhavaddhīmān pauṣyañjirdvijasattamāḥ //
meaning:
शान्तक्रोधं द्विजं दृष्ट्वा क्षिप्रमन्तर धात्प्रभुः /
तस्य शिष्यो ऽभवद्धीमान् पौष्यञ्जिर्द्विजसत्तमाः //
text_mt: seeing the anger of the twice-born [sage] calmed, the lord immediately disappeared. / His wise disciple was Pauṣyañji, O best of the twice-born;

sanskrit_iast:
hiraṇyanābhaḥ kauśalyo dvitīyo 'bhūnnarādhipaḥ /
adhyāpayata pauṣyāñjiḥ sahasrārddhaṃ tusaṃhitāḥ //
meaning:
हिरण्यनाभः कौशल्यो द्वितीयो ऽभून्नराधिपः /
अध्यापयत पौष्याञ्जिः सहस्रार्द्धं तुसंहिताः //
text_mt: the second was Hiraṇyanābha Kauśalya, the king of men. / Pauṣyañji taught half of the thousand Saṃhitās.

sanskrit_iast:
te nāmnodīcyasāmānaḥ śiṣyāḥ pauṣyañjinaḥ śubhāḥ /
sattvāni pañca kauśilyaḥ saṃhitānā madhītavān //
meaning:
ते नाम्नोदीच्यसामानः शिष्याः पौष्यञ्जिनः शुभाः /
सत्त्वानि पञ्च कौशिल्यः संहिताना मधीतवान् //
text_mt: By name, the auspicious disciples of Pauṣyañji were Northern Sāman-chanters; / the Kauśilya studied five hundred Saṃhitās.

sanskrit_iast:
śiṣyā hiraṇyanābhasya smṛtāstu prācyasāmagāḥ /
laugākṣiḥ kuśumiścaiva kuśīdirlāṅgalistathā /
pauṣyañji śiṣyāścatvārasteṣāṃ bhedānnibodhata //
meaning:
शिष्या हिरण्यनाभस्य स्मृतास्तु प्राच्यसामगाः /
लौगाक्षिः कुशुमिश्चैव कुशीदिर्लाङ्गलिस्तथा /
पौष्यञ्जि शिष्याश्चत्वारस्तेषां भेदान्निबोधत //
text_mt: The disciples of Hiraṇyanābha are remembered as Eastern Sāman-chanters. / Laugākṣi, Kuśumi, Kuśīdin, and Lāṅgali: / these are the four disciples of Pauṣyañji; hear their divisions!

sanskrit_iast:
nāḍāyanīyaḥ sahataṇḍiputrastasmādanovainanāmā suvidvān /
sakotiputraḥ susahāḥ sunāmā caitānbhedānvittalaugākṣiṇastu //
meaning:
नाडायनीयः सहतण्डिपुत्रस्तस्मादनोवैननामा सुविद्वान् /
सकोतिपुत्रः सुसहाः सुनामा चैतान्भेदान्वित्तलौगाक्षिणस्तु //
text_mt: The Nāḍāyanīya, together with the Taṇḍiputra, and after him the highly learned one named Anovaina, / and Kotiputra, Susaha, and Sunāman: know these to be the branches of Laugākṣi.

sanskrit_iast: trayastu kuśumeḥ śiṣyā aurasaḥ sa parāśaraḥ //
meaning: त्रयस्तु कुशुमेः शिष्या औरसः स पराशरः //
text_mt: The disciples of Kuśumi were three: Aurasa, Parāśara,

sanskrit_iast:
nābhirvittastu tejasvī trividhā kauśumāḥ smṛtāḥ /
śauriṣuḥ śṛṅgiputraśca dvāvetau tu ciravratau //
meaning:
नाभिर्वित्तस्तु तेजस्वी त्रिविधा कौशुमाः स्मृताः /
शौरिषुः शृङ्गिपुत्रश्च द्वावेतौ तु चिरव्रतौ //
text_mt: and the splendid Nābhi; the Kauśumas are recorded as threefold. / Śauriṣu and Śṛṅgiputra, these two of lasting vows,

sanskrit_iast:
rāṇāyanīyiḥ saumitriḥ sāmavedaviśāradau /
provāca saṃhitāsti sraḥ śṛṅgiputrau mahātpāḥ //
meaning:
राणायनीयिः सौमित्रिः सामवेदविशारदौ /
प्रोवाच संहितास्ति स्रः शृङ्गिपुत्रौ महात्पाः //
text_mt: Rāṇāyanīya and Saumitri, were experts in the Sāmaveda; / the noble Śṛṅgiputra taught three Saṃhitās.

sanskrit_iast:
vainaḥ prājīnayogaśca surālaśca dvijauttamaḥ /
provāca saṃhitāḥ ṣaṭtu pārāśaryastu kauthumaḥ //
meaning:
वैनः प्राजीनयोगश्च सुरालश्च द्विजौत्तमः /
प्रोवाच संहिताः षट्तु पाराशर्यस्तु कौथुमः //
text_mt: Vaina, Prācīnayoga, and Surāla, the best of the twice-born; / and Pārāśarya Kauthuma proclaimed six collections.

sanskrit_iast:
āsurāyaṇavaiśākhyau vedavṛddhaparāyaṇau /
prācīnayogaputraśca buddhimāṃśca patañjaliḥ //
meaning:
आसुरायणवैशाख्यौ वेदवृद्धपरायणौ /
प्राचीनयोगपुत्रश्च बुद्धिमांश्च पतञ्जलिः //
text_mt: Āsurāyaṇi and Vaiśākhya, devoted to the elders of the Veda, / and the son of Prācīnayoga, and the wise Patañjali—

sanskrit_iast:
kauthumasya tu bhedāśca pārāśaryasya paṭ samṛtāḥ /
lāṅgalaḥ śālihotraśca ṣaḍuvācātha saṃhitāḥ //
meaning:
कौथुमस्य तु भेदाश्च पाराशर्यस्य पट् समृताः /
लाङ्गलः शालिहोत्रश्च षडुवाचाथ संहिताः //
text_mt: these six divisions of Kauthuma Pārāśarya are remembered. / Then Lāṅgala and Śālihotra taught six collections:

sanskrit_iast:
hālinirjyāmahāniśca jaiminirlomagāyaniḥ /
kaṇḍuśca kohalaścaiva ṣaḍe te lāṅgalāḥ smṛtāḥ //
meaning:
हालिनिर्ज्यामहानिश्च जैमिनिर्लोमगायनिः /
कण्डुश्च कोहलश्चैव षडे ते लाङ्गलाः स्मृताः //
text_mt: Hālini, Jāmahāni, Jaimini, Lomagāyani, / Kaṇḍu, and Kohala: these six are remembered as the Lāṅgalas.

sanskrit_iast:
ete lāṅgalinaḥ śiṣyāḥ saṃhitā yaiḥ pravarttitāḥ /
eko hiraṇyanābhasya kṛtaḥ śiṣyo nṛpātmajaḥ //
meaning:
एते लाङ्गलिनः शिष्याः संहिता यैः प्रवर्त्तिताः /
एको हिरण्यनाभस्य कृतः शिष्यो नृपात्मजः //
text_mt: These are the disciples of Lāṅgali, by whom the collections were propagated. / There was one disciple of Hiraṇyanābha, a prince, [named] Kṛta.

sanskrit_iast:
so 'karottu caturviśasaṃhitā dvipadāṃ varaḥ /
provāca caiva śiṣyebhyo yebhyastāśca nibodhata //
meaning:
सो ऽकरोत्तु चतुर्विशसंहिता द्विपदां वरः /
प्रोवाच चैव शिष्येभ्यो येभ्यस्ताश्च निबोधत //
text_mt: That best of two-footed beings made twenty-four collections, / and he taught them to his disciples; learn who they were:

sanskrit_iast:
rāḍiśca rāḍavīyaśca pañjamau vāhanastathā /
talako māṇḍukaścaiva kāliko rājikaṃstathā //
meaning:
राडिश्च राडवीयश्च पञ्जमौ वाहनस्तथा /
तलको माण्डुकश्चैव कालिको राजिकंस्तथा //
text_mt: Rāḍi, Rāḍavīya, Pañcama, Vāhana, / Talaka, Māṇḍūka, Kālika, Rājika,

sanskrit_iast:
gautamaścājabastaśca somarājāyanastataḥ /
puṣṭiśca parikṛṣṭaśca ulūkhalaka eva ca //
meaning:
गौतमश्चाजबस्तश्च सोमराजायनस्ततः /
पुष्टिश्च परिकृष्टश्च उलूखलक एव च //
text_mt: Gautama, Ajabasta, and then Somarājāyana, / Puṣṭi, Parikṛṣṭa, and Ulūkhalaka,

sanskrit_iast:
yavīyasastu vai śālīraṅgulīyaśca kauśikaḥ /
śālimañjaripākaśca śadhīyaḥ kāniniśca yaḥ //
meaning:
यवीयसस्तु वै शालीरङ्गुलीयश्च कौशिकः /
शालिमञ्जरिपाकश्च शधीयः कानिनिश्च यः //
text_mt: Yavīyas, the virtuous Śālīraṅguli, Kauśika, / Śālimañjaripāka, Śādhīya, and Kānini.

sanskrit_iast:
pārāśaryastu dharmātmā iti krāntāstu sāmagāḥ /
sāmagānāṃ tu sarveṣāṃ śreṣṭhau dvau parikīrttitau //
meaning:
पाराशर्यस्तु धर्मात्मा इति क्रान्तास्तु सामगाः /
सामगानां तु सर्वेषां श्रेष्ठौ द्वौ परिकीर्त्तितौ //
text_mt: And the righteous Pārāśarya. Thus the chanters of the Sāman have departed. / Among all the chanters of the Sāman, two have been declared the greatest:

sanskrit_iast:
pauṣyañjiśca kṛtaścaiva saṃhitānāṃ vikalpakau /
atharvāṇaṃ dvidhā kṛtvā sumanturadadāddvijāḥ //
meaning:
पौष्यञ्जिश्च कृतश्चैव संहितानां विकल्पकौ /
अथर्वाणं द्विधा कृत्वा सुमन्तुरददाद्द्विजाः //
text_mt: Pauṣyañji and Kṛta, the arrangers of the collections. / Having divided the Atharvaveda into two, O twice-born, Sumantu gave it

sanskrit_iast:
kabandhāya punaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ sa ca vidvānyathāśrutam /
kabandhastu dvidhā kṛtvā pathyāyaikaṃ punardadau //
meaning:
कबन्धाय पुनः कृष्णं स च विद्वान्यथाश्रुतम् /
कबन्धस्तु द्विधा कृत्वा पथ्यायैकं पुनर्ददौ //
text_mt: again, in its entirety, to Kabandha; and that learned one [taught it] as he had heard it. / Kabandha, having divided it into two, gave one [part] to Pathya,

sanskrit_iast:
dvitīyaṃ devadarśāyasa caturdhākarotprabhuḥ /
modo brahmabalaścaiva pippalādastathaiva ca //
meaning:
द्वितीयं देवदर्शायस चतुर्धाकरोत्प्रभुः /
मोदो ब्रह्मबलश्चैव पिप्पलादस्तथैव च //
text_mt: and the second to Devadarśa; that lord divided it into four: / Moda, Brahmabala, and likewise Pippalāda,

sanskrit_iast:
śaulkāyaniśca dharmajñaścaturthastapasi sthitaḥ /
devadarśasya catvāraḥ śiṣyā hyete dṛḍhavratāḥ //
meaning:
शौल्कायनिश्च धर्मज्ञश्चतुर्थस्तपसि स्थितः /
देवदर्शस्य चत्वारः शिष्या ह्येते दृढव्रताः //
text_mt: and the fourth was Śaulkāyani, knower of dharma, established in asceticism. / These four, of firm vows, were the disciples of Devadarśa.

sanskrit_iast:
punaśca trividhaṃ viddhi pathyānāṃ bhedamuttamam /
jājaliḥ kumudādiśca tṛtīyaḥ śaunakaḥ smṛtaḥ //
meaning:
पुनश्च त्रिविधं विद्धि पथ्यानां भेदमुत्तमम् /
जाजलिः कुमुदादिश्च तृतीयः शौनकः स्मृतः //
text_mt: Know, further, the excellent three-fold division of the Pathyas: / Jājali, Kumudādi, and the third is recorded as Śaunaka.

sanskrit_iast:
śaunakastu dvidhā kṛtvā dadāvekāntu babhrave /
ddvitīyāṃ saṃhitāṃ dhīmānsaindhavāyanasaṃjñi te //
meaning:
शौनकस्तु द्विधा कृत्वा ददावेकान्तु बभ्रवे /
द्द्वितीयां संहितां धीमान्सैन्धवायनसंज्ञि ते //
text_mt: Śaunaka, having divided it into two, gave one to Babhru, / and the wise one gave the second collection to the one named Saindhavāyana.

sanskrit_iast:
saindhavo muñjakeśyaśca bhinnāmādhāddvidhā punaḥ /
nakṣatrakalpo vaitānastṛtīyaḥ saṃhitāvidhiḥ //
meaning:
सैन्धवो मुञ्जकेश्यश्च भिन्नामाधाद्द्विधा पुनः /
नक्षत्रकल्पो वैतानस्तृतीयः संहिताविधिः //
text_mt: Saindhava and Muñjakeśya divided it again into two. / The Nakṣatrakalpa and the Vaitāna [kalpa], the third being the Saṃhitāvidhi,

sanskrit_iast:
caturthoṃ'girasaḥ kalpaḥ śāntikalpaśca pañcamaḥ /
śreṣṭhāstvatharvaṇāmete saṃhitānāṃ vikalpakāḥ //
meaning:
चतुर्थोंऽगिरसः कल्पः शान्तिकल्पश्च पञ्चमः /
श्रेष्ठास्त्वथर्वणामेते संहितानां विकल्पकाः //
text_mt: the fourth the Āṅgirasa kalpa, and the Śāntikalpa is the fifth. / These are the foremost Atharvaṇa arrangers of the collections.

sanskrit_iast:
khaḍgaḥ kṛtvā mayā yuktaṃ purāṇamṛṣisattamāḥ /
ātreyaḥ sumatirdhīmānkāśyapo hyakṛtavraṇaḥ //
meaning:
खड्गः कृत्वा मया युक्तं पुराणमृषिसत्तमाः /
आत्रेयः सुमतिर्धीमान्काश्यपो ह्यकृतव्रणः //
text_mt: Having composed the Purāṇa connected with me, O best of sages: / the wise Ātreya Sumati, the Kāśyapa Akṛtavraṇa,

sanskrit_iast:
bhāradvājo 'gnivarcāśca vāsiṣṭhā mitrayuśca yaḥ /
sāvarṇiḥ somadattiśca suśarmā śāṃśapāyanaḥ //
meaning:
भारद्वाजो ऽग्निवर्चाश्च वासिष्ठा मित्रयुश्च यः /
सावर्णिः सोमदत्तिश्च सुशर्मा शांशपायनः //
text_mt: the Bhāradvāja Agnivarcas, and he who is the Vāsiṣṭha Mitrayu, / Sāvarṇi, Somadatti, and Suśarman Śāṃśapāyana—

sanskrit_iast:
ete śiṣyā mama proktāḥ purāṇeṣu dhṛtavratāḥ /
tribhistatra kṛtāstisraḥ saṃhitāḥ punareva hi //
meaning:
एते शिष्या मम प्रोक्ताः पुराणेषु धृतव्रताः /
त्रिभिस्तत्र कृतास्तिस्रः संहिताः पुनरेव हि //
text_mt: these are declared to be my disciples, constant in their vows regarding the Purāṇas. / Among them, three made three collections again:

sanskrit_iast:
kāśyapaḥ saṃhitā karttā sāvarṇiḥ śāṃśapāyanaḥ /
māmikā tu caturthī syāccatasro mūlasaṃhitāḥ //
meaning:
काश्यपः संहिता कर्त्ता सावर्णिः शांशपायनः /
मामिका तु चतुर्थी स्याच्चतस्रो मूलसंहिताः //
text_mt: Kāśyapa is an author of a collection, [as are] Sāvarṇi and Śāṃśapāyana; / mine would be the fourth: [thus] there are four primary collections.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvāstā hi catuṣpādāḥ sarvāścaikārthavācikāḥ /
pāṭhāntare vṛthābhūtā vedaśākhā yathā tathā //
meaning:
सर्वास्ता हि चतुष्पादाः सर्वाश्चैकार्थवाचिकाः /
पाठान्तरे वृथाभूता वेदशाखा यथा तथा //
text_mt: All of them consist of four parts, and all express the same meaning; / the variations in their readings are natural, just as in the Vedic branches.

sanskrit_iast:
catuḥ sāhasrikāḥ sarvāḥ śāṃśapāyanikāmṛte /
laumaharṣaṇikā mūlā tataḥ kāśyapikā parā //
meaning:
चतुः साहस्रिकाः सर्वाः शांशपायनिकामृते /
लौमहर्षणिका मूला ततः काश्यपिका परा //
text_mt: All consist of four thousand verses, except that of Śāṃśapāyana. / The original is that of Lomaharṣaṇa; after that, the next is of Kāśyapa;

sanskrit_iast:
sāvarṇikā tṛtīyāsāvṛjuvākyārthamaṇḍitā /
śāṃśapāyanikā cānyā nodanārthavibhūṣitā //
meaning:
सावर्णिका तृतीयासावृजुवाक्यार्थमण्डिता /
शांशपायनिका चान्या नोदनार्थविभूषिता //
text_mt: that of Sāvarṇi is the third, adorned with straightforward expression of meaning; / and the other, of Śāṃśapāyana, is embellished with incitement and purpose.

sanskrit_iast:
sahasrāṇi ṛcāṃ cāṣṭau ṣaṭśatāni tathaiva ca /
etāḥ pañcadaśānyāśca daśānyā daśabhistathā //
meaning:
सहस्राणि ऋचां चाष्टौ षट्शतानि तथैव च /
एताः पञ्चदशान्याश्च दशान्या दशभिस्तथा //
text_mt: There are eight thousand verses, and six hundred likewise; / these, along with fifteen others, and ten others, and ten—

sanskrit_iast:
savālakhilyāḥ saptaitāḥ sasuparṇāḥ prakīrttitāḥ /
aṣṭau sāmasahasrāṇi sāmāni ca caturddaśa //
meaning:
सवालखिल्याः सप्तैताः ससुपर्णाः प्रकीर्त्तिताः /
अष्टौ सामसहस्राणि सामानि च चतुर्द्दश //
text_mt: together with the Vālakhilyas, these seven are proclaimed together with the Suparṇas. / There are eight thousand Sāmans, and fourteen Sāmans,

sanskrit_iast:
sāraṇyakaṃ sahohaṃ ca etadgāyanti sāmagāḥ /
dvādaśaiva sahasrāṇi cchanda ādhvaryavaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
सारण्यकं सहोहं च एतद्गायन्ति सामगाः /
द्वादशैव सहस्राणि च्छन्द आध्वर्यवं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: along with the Āraṇyaka and the Ūha; this the chanters of the Sāman sing. / Twelve thousand metres are remembered as belonging to the Adhvaryu.

sanskrit_iast:
yajuṣāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ ca tathā vyāso vyakalpayat /
sagrāmyāraṇyakaṃ tasmātsamantrakaraṇaṃ tathā //
meaning:
यजुषां ब्राह्मणानां च तथा व्यासो व्यकल्पयत् /
सग्राम्यारण्यकं तस्मात्समन्त्रकरणं तथा //
text_mt: Thus Vyāsa arranged the Yajuses and the Brāhmaṇas, / with the common and the wilderness [recitations], together with the performance of mantras.

sanskrit_iast:
ataḥ paraṃ kathānaṃ tu pūrvā iti viśeṣaṇam /
grāmyāraṇyaṃ samantraṃ tadṛgbrāhmaṇayajuḥ smṛtam //
meaning:
अतः परं कथानं तु पूर्वा इति विशेषणम् /
ग्राम्यारण्यं समन्त्रं तदृग्ब्राह्मणयजुः स्मृतम् //
text_mt: Beyond this, the designation 'ancient' applies to the narrations; / that combined with village and forest mantras is remembered as the Ṛg, Brāhmaṇa, and Yajus.

sanskrit_iast:
tathā hāridravīryāṇāṃ khilānyupakhilānitu /
tathaiva taittirīyāṇāṃ parakṣudrā iti smṛtam //
meaning:
तथा हारिद्रवीर्याणां खिलान्युपखिलानितु /
तथैव तैत्तिरीयाणां परक्षुद्रा इति स्मृतम् //
text_mt: Likewise, for the Hāridravīyas there are supplements and minor supplements; / similarly, for the Taittirīyas they are remembered as the other minor [texts].

sanskrit_iast:
dve sahasre śatanyūne vede vājasaneyake /
ṛggamaḥ parisaṃkhyāto brāhmaṇaṃ tu caturguṇam //
meaning:
द्वे सहस्रे शतन्यूने वेदे वाजसनेयके /
ऋग्गमः परिसंख्यातो ब्राह्मणं तु चतुर्गुणम् //
text_mt: In the Vājasaneyaka Veda, the verse portions are reckoned / as two thousand less one hundred, while the Brāhmaṇa is four times that.

sanskrit_iast:
aṣṭau sahasrāṇi śatāni vāṣṭāvaśītiranyānyadhikāni vā ca /
etatpramāṇaṃ yajuṣāmṛcāṃ ca saśukriyaṃ sakhilaṃ yājñavalkyam //
meaning:
अष्टौ सहस्राणि शतानि वाष्टावशीतिरन्यान्यधिकानि वा च /
एतत्प्रमाणं यजुषामृचां च सशुक्रियं सखिलं याज्ञवल्क्यम् //
text_mt: Eight thousand, or eight hundred, or eighty more, or [still] more— / such is the extent of the Yajuses and the verses of the Yājñavalkya text, with its Śukriya and Khila.

sanskrit_iast:
tathā cāraṇavidyānāṃ pramāṇasahitaṃ śṛṇu /
ṣaṭsahasramṛcāmuktamṛcaḥ ṣaḍviṃśatiṃ punaḥ //
meaning:
तथा चारणविद्यानां प्रमाणसहितं शृणु /
षट्सहस्रमृचामुक्तमृचः षड्विंशतिं पुनः //
text_mt: Hear also the extent of the Cāraṇavidyās: / six thousand verses are stated, and twenty-six verses besides.

sanskrit_iast:
etāvadadhikaṃ teṣāṃ yajuḥ ki mapi vakṣyate /
ekādaśasahasrāṇi ṛcaścānyā daśottarāḥ //
meaning:
एतावदधिकं तेषां यजुः कि मपि वक्ष्यते /
एकादशसहस्राणि ऋचश्चान्या दशोत्तराः //
text_mt: So much more of their Yajus will be mentioned in some measure: / eleven thousand verses, and ten more verses.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛcāṃ daśasahasrāṇi hyaśītistriṃśadeva tu /
sahasramekaṃ mantrāṇāmṛcāmuktaṃ pramāṇataḥ //
meaning:
ऋचां दशसहस्राणि ह्यशीतिस्त्रिंशदेव तु /
सहस्रमेकं मन्त्राणामृचामुक्तं प्रमाणतः //
text_mt: Ten thousand verses, and eighty, and thirty; / one thousand mantras of the verses are stated by measure.

sanskrit_iast:
etāvānṛci vistāro hyanyaccātharvikaṃ bahu /
ṛcāmatharvaṇāṃ pañcasahasrāṇīti niścayaḥ //
meaning:
एतावानृचि विस्तारो ह्यन्यच्चाथर्विकं बहु /
ऋचामथर्वणां पञ्चसहस्राणीति निश्चयः //
text_mt: Such is the extent of the verses; and there is much other Atharvaṇa material. / It is determined that there are five thousand verses of the Atharvans.

sanskrit_iast:
sahasramanyadvijñeyamṛṣi bhirviśatiṃ vinā /
etadaṅgirasāṃ proktaṃ teṣāmāraṇyakaṃ punaḥ //
meaning:
सहस्रमन्यद्विज्ञेयमृषि भिर्विशतिं विना /
एतदङ्गिरसां प्रोक्तं तेषामारण्यकं पुनः //
text_mt: Another thousand, less twenty, is understood by the sages; / this is declared for the Āṅgirases, and their Āraṇyaka besides.

sanskrit_iast:
iti saṃkhyā prasaṃkhyātā śākhābhedāstathaiva tu /
kartāraśacaiva śākhānāṃ bhedahetūṃstathaiva ca //
meaning:
इति संख्या प्रसंख्याता शाखाभेदास्तथैव तु /
कर्तारशचैव शाखानां भेदहेतूंस्तथैव च //
text_mt: Thus the number has been fully counted, and likewise the divisions of the branches, / the makers of the branches, and the causes of division.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvamanvantareṣvevaṃ śākhābhedāḥ samāśritāḥ /
prājāpatyā śrutirnityā tadvikalpāstvime smṛtāḥ //
meaning:
सर्वमन्वन्तरेष्वेवं शाखाभेदाः समाश्रिताः /
प्राजापत्या श्रुतिर्नित्या तद्विकल्पास्त्विमे स्मृताः //
text_mt: In all manvantaras, the divisions of the branches are settled in this way. / The revelation of Prajāpati is eternal, but these variations of it are remembered.

sanskrit_iast:
anityabhāvāddevānāṃ mantrotpattiḥ punaḥ punaḥ /
dvāpareṣu punarbhedāḥ śrutīnāṃ parikīrttitāḥ //
meaning:
अनित्यभावाद्देवानां मन्त्रोत्पत्तिः पुनः पुनः /
द्वापरेषु पुनर्भेदाः श्रुतीनां परिकीर्त्तिताः //
