एवमुक्तास्तदा विश्वे ब्रह्मणा विश्वकर्मणा /
ऊचुस्ते सहिताः सर्वे ब्रह्माणां लोकभावनम् //
text_mt: Addressed thus at that time by Brahmā, the maker of the universe, / all the Viśvas together said to Brahmā, the creator of the worlds:

sanskrit_iast:
śrāddhe 'smākaṃ bhavedaṃśo hyeṣa naḥ kāṅkṣito varaḥ /
pratyuvāca tato brahmā tānvai tridaśapūjitaḥ //
meaning:
श्राद्धे ऽस्माकं भवेदंशो ह्येष नः काङ्क्षितो वरः /
प्रत्युवाच ततो ब्रह्मा तान्वै त्रिदशपूजितः //
text_mt: “May there be a share for us in the śrāddha; this is the boon we desire.” / Then Brahmā, worshipped by the gods, replied to them:

sanskrit_iast:
bhaviṣyatyevamevaṃ tu kāṅkṣito vo varastu yaḥ /
pitṛbhiśca tathetyuktamevametanna saṃśayaḥ //
meaning:
भविष्यत्येवमेवं तु काङ्क्षितो वो वरस्तु यः /
पितृभिश्च तथेत्युक्तमेवमेतन्न संशयः //
text_mt: “It shall be just so, this boon desired by you.” / And by the ancestors it was said, “So be it; thus it is, without doubt.”

sanskrit_iast:
sahasmābhistu bhoktavyaṃ yatkiṃ ciddṛśyate tviha /
asmākaṃ kalpite śrāddhe yuṣmānaprāśanaṃ hi vai //
bhaviṣyati manuṣyeṣu satyame tadbruvāmahe /
mālyairgandhaistathānnena yuṣmānagre 'rccayiṣyati /1 12.12//
meaning:
सहस्माभिस्तु भोक्तव्यं यत्किं चिद्दृश्यते त्विह /
अस्माकं कल्पिते श्राद्धे युष्मानप्राशनं हि वै //
भविष्यति मनुष्येषु सत्यमे तद्ब्रुवामहे /
माल्यैर्गन्धैस्तथान्नेन युष्मानग्रे ऽर्च्चयिष्यति /1 12.12//
text_mt:
[The ancestors said:] “Whatever is seen here must be enjoyed together with us. / In the śrāddha arranged for us, your non-eating [is impossible].

This will happen among men; we speak this truth: / with garlands, perfumes, and food, one will worship you first.

sanskrit_iast:
agre dattvā tu yuṣmākamasmākaṃ dāsyate tataḥ /
visarjanamathāsmākaṃ pūrvaṃ paścāttu daivatam //
meaning:
अग्रे दत्त्वा तु युष्माकमस्माकं दास्यते ततः /
विसर्जनमथास्माकं पूर्वं पश्चात्तु दैवतम् //
text_mt: Having given to you first, it will then be given to us. / Then the dismissal will be ours first, and the divine one afterwards.

sanskrit_iast:
rakṣaṇaṃ caiva śrāddhasya ātithyasya vidhidvayam /
bhūtānāṃ devatānāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ caiva karmaṇi //
meaning:
रक्षणं चैव श्राद्धस्य आतिथ्यस्य विधिद्वयम् /
भूतानां देवतानां च पितॄणां चैव कर्मणि //
text_mt: Protection of the śrāddha and the two-fold rule of hospitality / [are established] in the rite for living beings, deities, and ancestors.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ kṛte samyagetatsarvameva bhaviṣyati /
evaṃ dattvā varaṃ teṣāṃ brahmā pitṛgaṇaiḥ saha //
meaning:
एवं कृते सम्यगेतत्सर्वमेव भविष्यति /
एवं दत्त्वा वरं तेषां ब्रह्मा पितृगणैः सह //
text_mt: When this is performed thus properly, everything will come to pass.” / Having thus granted a boon to them, Brahmā, along with the groups of ancestors,

sanskrit_iast:
kṣamānugrahakṛddevaḥ saṃcakāra yathoditam /
vede pañca mahāyajñā narāṇāṃ samudāhṛtāḥ //
meaning:
क्षमानुग्रहकृद्देवः संचकार यथोदितम् /
वेदे पञ्च महायज्ञा नराणां समुदाहृताः //
text_mt: the god who bestows forbearance and grace, concluded as prescribed. / In the Veda, five great sacrifices are proclaimed for men.

sanskrit_iast:
etānpañca mahāyajñānnirvapetsatataṃ naraḥ /
yatra sthāsyanti dātārastatsthānaṃ vai nibodhata //
meaning:
एतान्पञ्च महायज्ञान्निर्वपेत्सततं नरः /
यत्र स्थास्यन्ति दातारस्तत्स्थानं वै निबोधत //
text_mt: A man should constantly offer these five great sacrifices. / Understand that abode where the givers will dwell:

sanskrit_iast:
nirbhayaṃ virajaskaṃ ca niḥśokaṃ nirvyathaklamam /
brāhmaṃ sthānamavāpnoti sarvalokapuraskṛtam //
meaning:
निर्भयं विरजस्कं च निःशोकं निर्व्यथक्लमम् /
ब्राह्मं स्थानमवाप्नोति सर्वलोकपुरस्कृतम् //
text_mt: free from fear, free from rajas, sorrowless, free from pain and exhaustion, / he attains the realm of Brahmā, honored by all the worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
śūdreṇāpi ca karttavyāḥ pañcaite mantravarjitāḥ /
ato 'nyathā tu yo bhuṅkte sa ṛṇaṃ nityamaśnute //
meaning:
शूद्रेणापि च कर्त्तव्याः पञ्चैते मन्त्रवर्जिताः /
अतो ऽन्यथा तु यो भुङ्क्ते स ऋणं नित्यमश्नुते //
text_mt: These five must also be performed by a Śūdra, [though] devoid of mantras. / He who eats otherwise always incurs a debt.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṇaṃ bhuṅkte sa pāpātmā yaḥ pacedātmakāraṇāt /
tasmānnirvartayetpañca mahāyajñānsadā budhaḥ //
meaning:
ऋणं भुङ्क्ते स पापात्मा यः पचेदात्मकारणात् /
तस्मान्निर्वर्तयेत्पञ्च महायज्ञान्सदा बुधः //
text_mt: That evil-minded person eats debt who cooks for his own sake; / therefore a wise man should always perform the five great sacrifices.

sanskrit_iast:
udakpūrve baliṃ kuryādudakānte tathaiva ca /
baliṃ suvihitaṃ kuryā duccairuccataraṃ kṣipet //
meaning:
उदक्पूर्वे बलिं कुर्यादुदकान्ते तथैव च /
बलिं सुविहितं कुर्या दुच्चैरुच्चतरं क्षिपेत् //
text_mt: One should offer a bali in the north-east, and likewise near water; / one should present the bali well-prepared, casting it higher and higher.

sanskrit_iast:
paraśṛṅgaṃ gavāṃ mūtraṃ baliṃ sūtraṃ samutkṣipet /
tannivedyo bhavetpiṇḍaḥ pitṝṇāṃ yastu jīvati //
meaning:
परशृङ्गं गवां मूत्रं बलिं सूत्रं समुत्क्षिपेत् /
तन्निवेद्यो भवेत्पिण्डः पितॄणां यस्तु जीवति //
text_mt: He should throw out an animal's horn, cow urine, the bali offering, and the sacred thread. / For the ancestors, that food ball may be offered to one who is alive.

sanskrit_iast:
iṣṭenānnena bhakṣyaiśca bhojayecca yathāvidhi /
nivedyaṃ kecidicchanti jīvantyapi hi yatnataḥ //
meaning:
इष्टेनान्नेन भक्ष्यैश्च भोजयेच्च यथाविधि /
निवेद्यं केचिदिच्छन्ति जीवन्त्यपि हि यत्नतः //
text_mt: He should feed [the brāhmaṇas] with desired foods and edibles according to rule. / Some desire an offering with diligence even while [the father] is alive.

sanskrit_iast:
devadevā mahātmāno hyete pitara ityuta /
icchanti kecidācāryaḥ paścātpiṇḍanivedanam //
meaning:
देवदेवा महात्मानो ह्येते पितर इत्युत /
इच्छन्ति केचिदाचार्यः पश्चात्पिण्डनिवेदनम् //
text_mt: Indeed, these ancestors are great-souled gods of gods. / Some teachers desire the offering of the food balls [to be performed] afterwards,

sanskrit_iast:
pūjanaṃ caiva vipraṇāṃ pūrvameveha nityaśaḥ /
taddhidharmārthakuśalo netyuvāca bṛhasmatiḥ //
meaning:
पूजनं चैव विप्रणां पूर्वमेवेह नित्यशः /
तद्धिधर्मार्थकुशलो नेत्युवाच बृहस्मतिः //
text_mt: and the worshipping of the brāhmaṇas always first in this world. / But Bṛhaspati, skilled in dharma and artha, said, “No;

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvaṃ nivedayetpiṇḍānpaścādviprāṃśca bhojayet /
yogātmāno mahātmānaḥ pitaro yoga saṃbhavāḥ //
meaning:
पूर्वं निवेदयेत्पिण्डान्पश्चाद्विप्रांश्च भोजयेत् /
योगात्मानो महात्मानः पितरो योग संभवाः //
text_mt: one should offer the food balls first, and afterwards feed the brāhmaṇas. / The ancestors are great souls consisting of yoga, born of yoga.

sanskrit_iast:
somamāpyāyayantyete pitaro yogasaṃsthitāḥ /
tasmāddadyācchuciḥ piṇḍānyogebhyastatparāyaṇaḥ //
meaning:
सोममाप्याययन्त्येते पितरो योगसंस्थिताः /
तस्माद्दद्याच्छुचिः पिण्डान्योगेभ्यस्तत्परायणः //
text_mt: Established in yoga, these ancestors cause Soma to swell; / therefore, pure [and] devoted to them, one should give the food balls to the yogins.

sanskrit_iast:
pitṝṇāṃ hi bhavedetatsākṣādiva hutaṃ haviḥ /
brahmaṇānāṃ sahasrasya yogasthaṃ grāsayedyadi //
meaning:
पितॄणां हि भवेदेतत्साक्षादिव हुतं हविः /
ब्रह्मणानां सहस्रस्य योगस्थं ग्रासयेद्यदि //
text_mt: For this becomes directly like an offering of oblation poured into fire for the ancestors. / If, of a thousand brāhmaṇas, one feeds one who is established in yoga,

sanskrit_iast:
yajamānaṃ ca bhoktṝṃś ca naurivāmbhasi tārayet /
asatāṃ pragraho yatra satāṃ caiva vimānatā //
meaning:
यजमानं च भोक्तॄंश् च नौरिवाम्भसि तारयेत् /
असतां प्रग्रहो यत्र सतां चैव विमानता //
text_mt: he delivers the sacrificer and the eaters like a boat on the water. / Where the wicked are honored and the virtuous are disrespected,

sanskrit_iast:
daṇḍo daivakṛtastatra sadyaḥ patati dāruṇaḥ /
itvā mama sadharmāṇaṃ bāliśaṃ yastu bhojayet //
meaning:
दण्डो दैवकृतस्तत्र सद्यः पतति दारुणः /
इत्वा मम सधर्माणं बालिशं यस्तु भोजयेत् //
text_mt: there severe divine punishment falls immediately. / But one who feeds a fool merely because he observes the same dharma as oneself,

sanskrit_iast:
ādikarma samutsṛjya dātā tatra vinaśyati /
piṇḍamagnau sadā dadyadbhogārthī prathamaṃ naraḥ //
meaning:
आदिकर्म समुत्सृज्य दाता तत्र विनश्यति /
पिण्डमग्नौ सदा दद्यद्भोगार्थी प्रथमं नरः //
text_mt: having abandoned the primary ritual, the giver is ruined in that act. / A man seeking enjoyment should always offer the first food ball into the fire;

sanskrit_iast:
dadyātprajārthī yatnena madhyamaṃ mantrapūrvakam /
uttamāṃ kāntimanvicchangoṣu nityaṃ prayacchati //
meaning:
दद्यात्प्रजार्थी यत्नेन मध्यमं मन्त्रपूर्वकम् /
उत्तमां कान्तिमन्विच्छन्गोषु नित्यं प्रयच्छति //
text_mt: one seeking offspring should diligently give the middle one preceded by mantras. / Seeking supreme beauty, he constantly gives it to cows;

sanskrit_iast:
prajñāṃ caiva yaśaḥ kīrttimapsu vai saṃprayacchati /
prārthayandīrghāmāyuśca vāyasebhyaḥ prayacchati //
meaning:
प्रज्ञां चैव यशः कीर्त्तिमप्सु वै संप्रयच्छति /
प्रार्थयन्दीर्घामायुश्च वायसेभ्यः प्रयच्छति //
text_mt: he gives it into the waters [seeking] wisdom, renown, and fame; / praying for a long lifespan, he gives it to crows;

sanskrit_iast:
sokumāryamathānvicchankukkuṭebhyaḥ prayacchati /
evametatsamuddiṣṭaṃ piṇḍanirvapaṇe phalam //
meaning:
सोकुमार्यमथान्विच्छन्कुक्कुटेभ्यः प्रयच्छति /
एवमेतत्समुद्दिष्टं पिण्डनिर्वपणे फलम् //
text_mt: and desiring tenderness of youth, he gives it to cocks. / In this way, this fruit has been declared regarding the offering of the food ball.

sanskrit_iast:
ākāśe gamayedvāpi apsu vā dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ /
pitṝṇāṃ sthānamākāśaṃ dakṣiṇā caiva digbhevet //
meaning:
आकाशे गमयेद्वापि अप्सु वा दक्षिणामुखः /
पितॄणां स्थानमाकाशं दक्षिणा चैव दिग्भेवेत् //
text_mt: Or facing south, he should cast it into the air or into the waters; / for the place of the ancestors is the air and the southern direction.

sanskrit_iast:
eke viprāḥ punaḥ prāhuḥ piṇḍoddharaṇamagrataḥ /
anujñātastu tairvipraiḥ kāmasuddhriyatāmit //
meaning:
एके विप्राः पुनः प्राहुः पिण्डोद्धरणमग्रतः /
अनुज्ञातस्तु तैर्विप्रैः कामसुद्ध्रियतामित् //
text_mt: Other brāhmaṇas, however, say that the raising of the food ball [is done] in front; / and permitted by those brāhmaṇas with the words, ‘Let it be raised at will,’

sanskrit_iast:
puṣpāṇāṃ ca phalānāṃ ca bhakṣyāṇāmannatastathā /
agramuddhṛtya sarveṣāṃ juhuyāddhavyavāhane //
meaning:
पुष्पाणां च फलानां च भक्ष्याणामन्नतस्तथा /
अग्रमुद्धृत्य सर्वेषां जुहुयाद्धव्यवाहने //
text_mt: having taken the choice portion from all the flowers, fruits, and edible foods, / he should offer it into the fire-bearer [Agni].

sanskrit_iast:
bhaṅyamannaṃ tathā peyaṃ mūlāni ca phalāni ca /
hutvāgnau ca tataḥ piṇḍānnirvapeddakṣiṇā mukhaḥ //
meaning:
भङ्यमन्नं तथा पेयं मूलानि च फलानि च /
हुत्वाग्नौ च ततः पिण्डान्निर्वपेद्दक्षिणा मुखः //
text_mt: Having offered into the fire edible food, drink, roots, and fruits, / he should then, facing south, offer the food balls.

sanskrit_iast:
vaivasvatāya somāya hutvā piṇḍānnivedya ca /
udakānnayanaṃ kṛtvā paścādviprāṃśca bhojayet //
meaning:
वैवस्वताय सोमाय हुत्वा पिण्डान्निवेद्य च /
उदकान्नयनं कृत्वा पश्चाद्विप्रांश्च भोजयेत् //
text_mt: Having offered to Vaivasvata and to Soma, and having presented the food balls, / and having carried out the rinsing with water, he should feed the brāhmaṇas afterwards.

sanskrit_iast:
anupūrvaṃ tato viprānbhakṣyairannaiśca śaktitaḥ /
snigdhairuṣṇaiḥ sugandhaiśca tarpayettānrasairapi //
meaning:
अनुपूर्वं ततो विप्रान्भक्ष्यैरन्नैश्च शक्तितः /
स्निग्धैरुष्णैः सुगन्धैश्च तर्पयेत्तान्रसैरपि //
text_mt: Then, according to order and to his ability, with foods and edibles / that are unctuous, hot, and fragrant, and with savory liquids, he should gratify those brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit_iast:
ekāgraḥ paryupāsīnaḥ prayataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitaḥ /
tatparaḥ śraddadhānaśca kāmānāpnoti mānavaḥ //
meaning:
एकाग्रः पर्युपासीनः प्रयतः प्राञ्जलिः स्थितः /
तत्परः श्रद्दधानश्च कामानाप्नोति मानवः //
text_mt: Attentive, sitting nearby, restrained, standing with folded hands, / devoted to them and full of faith, a man attains his desires.

sanskrit_iast:
akṣudratvaṃ kṛtajñatvaṃ dākṣiṇyaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ vacaḥ /
tapo yajñāṃśca dānaṃ ca prayacchanti pitāmahāḥ //
meaning:
अक्षुद्रत्वं कृतज्ञत्वं दाक्षिण्यं संस्कृतं वचः /
तपो यज्ञांश्च दानं च प्रयच्छन्ति पितामहाः //
text_mt: Freedom from meanness, gratitude, courtesy, refined speech, / ascetic practice, sacrifices, and charity—the grandfathers bestow [all these].

sanskrit_iast:
ataḥ paraṃ vidhiṃ saumyaṃ bhuktavatsu dvijātiṣu /
ānupūrvyeṇa vihitaṃ tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu //
meaning:
अतः परं विधिं सौम्यं भुक्तवत्सु द्विजातिषु /
आनुपूर्व्येण विहितं तन्मे निगदतः शृणु //
text_mt: After this, hear from me as I proclaim the gentle rule laid down in order / when the twice-born have finished eating.

sanskrit_iast:
prokṣya bhūmimathoddhṛtya pūrvaṃ pitṛparāyaṇaḥ /
tato 'nnivikiraṃ kuryādvidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā //
meaning:
प्रोक्ष्य भूमिमथोद्धृत्य पूर्वं पितृपरायणः /
ततो ऽन्निविकिरं कुर्याद्विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा //
text_mt: Having sprinkled the ground and previously swept it, devoted to the ancestors, / he should then scatter the food according to the rite observed in the rules.

sanskrit_iast:
svadhā vācya tato viprān vidhivadbhūritakṣiṇān /
annaśeṣamanujñāpya satkṛtya dvijasattamān //
meaning:
स्वधा वाच्य ततो विप्रान् विधिवद्भूरितक्षिणान् /
अन्नशेषमनुज्ञाप्य सत्कृत्य द्विजसत्तमान् //
text_mt: Having recited ‘svadhā’, and having honored the excellent twice-born with abundant sacrificial gifts according to rule, / having asked permission concerning the remnant of the food,

sanskrit_iast:
prāñjaliḥ prayataścaiva anugamya visarjayet //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyabhāge tṛtīye
upoddhātapāde śrāddhakalpe dvādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ // 12//
meaning:
प्राञ्जलिः प्रयतश्चैव अनुगम्य विसर्जयेत् //
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यभागे तृतीये
उपोद्धातपादे श्राद्धकल्पे द्वादशो ऽध्यायः // 12//
text_mt:
with folded hands and self-restrained, he should accompany them and dismiss them.

Thus ends the twelfth chapter on the rules of śrāddha in the Upoddhātapāda, the third middle section, of the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa spoken by Vāyu. // 12

sanskrit_iast:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
sakṛdabhyarcitāḥ prītā bhavanti pitaro 'vyayāḥ /
yogātmāno mahātmāno vipāpmāno mahaujasaḥ //
meaning:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
सकृदभ्यर्चिताः प्रीता भवन्ति पितरो ऽव्ययाः /
योगात्मानो महात्मानो विपाप्मानो महौजसः //
text_mt: Bṛhaspati said: / Worshipped but once, the imperishable ancestors are pleased— / those great souls consisting of yoga, free from sin, possessing great splendor.

sanskrit_iast:
pretya ca svargalokāya kāmaiśca bahulaṃ bhuvi /
yeṣu vāpyanugṛhṇanti mokṣaprāptiḥ krameṇa tu //
meaning:
प्रेत्य च स्वर्गलोकाय कामैश्च बहुलं भुवि /
येषु वाप्यनुगृह्णन्ति मोक्षप्राप्तिः क्रमेण तु //
text_mt: And after dying, [they go] to the heavenly world; and with abundant desires on earth, / or upon whom they bestow grace, there is attainment of liberation in due course.

sanskrit_iast:
tāni vakṣyāmyahaṃ saumya sarāṃsi saritastathā /
tīrthāni caiva puṇyāni deśāṃśchailāṃstathāśramān //
meaning:
तानि वक्ष्याम्यहं सौम्य सरांसि सरितस्तथा /
तीर्थानि चैव पुण्यानि देशांश्छैलांस्तथाश्रमान् //
text_mt: I shall tell of them, gentle one—the lakes as well as the rivers, / the holy tīrthas, regions, mountains, and hermitages.

sanskrit_iast:
puṇyo hi triṣu lokeṣu sadaivāmarakaṇṭakaḥ /
parvatapravaraḥ puṇyaḥ siddhayāraṇasevitaḥ //
meaning:
पुण्यो हि त्रिषु लोकेषु सदैवामरकण्टकः /
पर्वतप्रवरः पुण्यः सिद्धयारणसेवितः //
text_mt: Amarkaṇṭaka is indeed holy in the three worlds at all times, / an eminent and holy mountain visited by Siddhas and Cāraṇas,

sanskrit_iast:
yatra varṣasahasrāṇi prayutānyarbudāni ca /
tapaḥ suduścaraṃ tepe bhagavānaṅgirāḥ purā //
meaning:
यत्र वर्षसहस्राणि प्रयुतान्यर्बुदानि च /
तपः सुदुश्चरं तेपे भगवानङ्गिराः पुरा //
text_mt: where the blessed Aṅgiras of old performed austerity very hard to practice / for thousands, hundreds of thousands, and hundreds of millions of years;

sanskrit_iast:
yatra mṛtyorgatirnnāsti tathaivāsurarakṣasām /
na bhayaṃ naiva cālakṣmīryāvadbhūmirddhariṣyati //
meaning:
यत्र मृत्योर्गतिर्न्नास्ति तथैवासुररक्षसाम् /
न भयं नैव चालक्ष्मीर्यावद्भूमिर्द्धरिष्यति //
text_mt: where death has no access, nor do asuras and rākṣasas; / there is neither fear nor misfortune as long as the earth endures.

sanskrit_iast:
tapasā tejasā tasya bhrajate sa nagottamaḥ /
śṛṅge mālyavato nityaṃ vahniḥ saṃvarttako yathā //
meaning:
तपसा तेजसा तस्य भ्रजते स नगोत्तमः /
शृङ्गे माल्यवतो नित्यं वह्निः संवर्त्तको यथा //
text_mt: By his austerity and splendor, that best of mountains shines / like the fire of dissolution constantly on the peak of Mālyavat.

sanskrit_iast:
mṛdavastu sugandhāśca hemābhāḥ priyadarśanāḥ /
śāntāḥkuśā iti khyātāḥ paridakṣiṇanarmadām //
meaning:
मृदवस्तु सुगन्धाश्च हेमाभाः प्रियदर्शनाः /
शान्ताःकुशा इति ख्याताः परिदक्षिणनर्मदाम् //
text_mt: The kuśa grasses known to be soft, fragrant, golden-hued, pleasant to behold, / and tranquil surround the Narmadā to the right.

sanskrit_iast:
dṛṣṭavānsvargasopānaṃ bhagavānaṅgirāḥ purā /
agnihotre mahātejāḥ prastārārthaṃ kuśottamān //
meaning:
दृष्टवान्स्वर्गसोपानं भगवानङ्गिराः पुरा /
अग्निहोत्रे महातेजाः प्रस्तारार्थं कुशोत्तमान् //
text_mt: The blessed Aṅgiras of great splendor formerly saw [them as] a stairway to heaven, / [being] the best kuśa grasses for the sacrificial seat in the agnihotra.

sanskrit_iast:
teṣu darbheṣu yaḥ piṇḍānmarakaṇṭaṭakaparvate /
dadyātsakṛdapi prājñastasya vakṣyāmi yatphalam //
meaning:
तेषु दर्भेषु यः पिण्डान्मरकण्टटकपर्वते /
दद्यात्सकृदपि प्राज्ञस्तस्य वक्ष्यामि यत्फलम् //
text_mt: The wise man who offers food balls upon those darbha grasses on Mount Amarakaṇṭaka / even once—I shall tell of his fruit:

sanskrit_iast:
tadbhavatyakṣayaṃ śrāddhaṃ pitṝṇāṃ prītivardhanam /
antarddhānaṃ ca gacchanti kṣetramāsādya tatsadā //
meaning:
तद्भवत्यक्षयं श्राद्धं पितॄणां प्रीतिवर्धनम् /
अन्तर्द्धानं च गच्छन्ति क्षेत्रमासाद्य तत्सदा //
text_mt: That śrāddha becomes imperishable, increasing the delight of the ancestors; / and having reached that sacred place, they always attain invisibility.

sanskrit_iast:
tatra jvālāsaraḥ puṇyaṃ dṛśyate cāpi parvasu /
saśalyānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ viśalyakaraṇī nadī //
meaning:
तत्र ज्वालासरः पुण्यं दृश्यते चापि पर्वसु /
सशल्यानां च सत्त्वानां विशल्यकरणी नदी //
text_mt: The holy Jvālāsaras is seen there on conjunction days, / and the river that removes arrow-heads from living beings with darts [in them],

sanskrit_iast:
prāgdakṣiṇāyatāvarttā vāpī sā sunagottame /
kaliṅgadeśapaścārddhe śṛṅge mālyavato vibhoḥ //
meaning:
प्राग्दक्षिणायतावर्त्ता वापी सा सुनगोत्तमे /
कलिङ्गदेशपश्चार्द्धे शृङ्गे माल्यवतो विभोः //
text_mt: that pool having an eddy extending towards the southeast on that excellent mountain / on the western half of the Kaliṅga country, on the peak of Mālyavat of the lord.

sanskrit_iast:
siddhikṣetramṛṣiśreṣṭhā yaduktaṃ paramaṃ bhuvi /
saṃmataṃ devadaityānāṃ ślokaṃ cāpyuśanā jagau //
meaning:
सिद्धिक्षेत्रमृषिश्रेष्ठा यदुक्तं परमं भुवि /
संमतं देवदैत्यानां श्लोकं चाप्युशना जगौ //
text_mt: O best of ṛṣis, it is declared the supreme field of accomplishment on earth, / agreed upon by gods and daityas; and Uśanas sang a verse [about it]:

sanskrit_iast:
dhanyāste puruṣā loke ye prāpyāmarakaṇṭakam /
pitṝnsaṃtarpayiṣyantiśrāddhe pitṛparāyaṇāḥ //
meaning:
धन्यास्ते पुरुषा लोके ये प्राप्यामरकण्टकम् /
पितॄन्संतर्पयिष्यन्तिश्राद्धे पितृपरायणाः //
text_mt: ‘Blessed are those men in the world who, having reached Amarakaṇṭaka, / satisfy their ancestors in a śrāddha, wholly devoted to their ancestors.

sanskrit_iast:
alpena tapasā siddhiṃ gamiṣyanti na saṃśayaḥ /
sakṛdevārcitāstatra svargamāmarakaṇṭake //
meaning:
अल्पेन तपसा सिद्धिं गमिष्यन्ति न संशयः /
सकृदेवार्चितास्तत्र स्वर्गमामरकण्टके //
text_mt: By little austerity, they will attain perfection, there is no doubt; / worshipped but once there at Amarakaṇṭaka, [the ancestors go to] heaven.’

sanskrit_iast:
mahendraḥparvataḥ puṇyo ramyaḥ śakraniṣevitaḥ /
tatrāruhya bhavetpūtaḥ śrāddhaṃ caiva mahāphalam //
meaning:
महेन्द्रःपर्वतः पुण्यो रम्यः शक्रनिषेवितः /
तत्रारुह्य भवेत्पूतः श्राद्धं चैव महाफलम् //
text_mt: Mount Mahendra is holy, delightful, and resorted to by Śakra; / having climbed it, one becomes purified, and a śrāddha [performed there] bears great fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
vailāṭaśikhare yuktvā divyaṃ cakṣuḥ pravartate /
adhṛṣyaścaiva bhūtānāṃ devavaccarate mahīm //
meaning:
वैलाटशिखरे युक्त्वा दिव्यं चक्षुः प्रवर्तते /
अधृष्यश्चैव भूतानां देववच्चरते महीम् //
text_mt: Engaging in yoga on the summit of Vailāṭa, divine vision arises; / unassailable by living beings, he wanders the earth like a god.

sanskrit_iast:
saptagodāvare caiva gokarṇe ca tapovane /
aśvamedhaphalaṃ snātvā tatra dattvā bhavettataḥ //
meaning:
सप्तगोदावरे चैव गोकर्णे च तपोवने /
अश्वमेधफलं स्नात्वा तत्र दत्त्वा भवेत्ततः //
text_mt: At Saptagodāvara and in the hermitage at Gokarṇa, / having bathed and given [gifts] there, the fruit of an aśvamedha arises from that.

sanskrit_iast:
dhūtapāpasthalaṃ prāpya pūtaḥ snātvā bhavennaraḥ /
rudrastatra tapastepe devadevo maheśvaraḥ //
meaning:
धूतपापस्थलं प्राप्य पूतः स्नात्वा भवेन्नरः /
रुद्रस्तत्र तपस्तेपे देवदेवो महेश्वरः //
text_mt: Having reached the place called Dhūtapāpa, a man, having bathed, becomes purified; / Rudra, the god of gods, Maheśvara, performed austerities there.

sanskrit_iast:
gokarṇe nihitaṃ devair nāstikānāṃ nidarśanam /
abrāhmaṇasya sāvitrīṃ paṭhatastu praṇaśyati //
meaning:
गोकर्णे निहितं देवैर् नास्तिकानां निदर्शनम् /
अब्राह्मणस्य सावित्रीं पठतस्तु प्रणश्यति //
text_mt: At Gokarṇa an example for non-believers was set by the gods: / for a non-brāhmaṇa reciting the Sāvitrī, it perishes.

sanskrit_iast:
devarṣibhavane śṛṅge siddhacāraṇasevite /
āruhyataṃ niya mavāṃstato yāti triviṣṭapam //
meaning:
देवर्षिभवने शृङ्गे सिद्धचारणसेविते /
आरुह्यतं निय मवांस्ततो याति त्रिविष्टपम् //
text_mt:
Ascending that peak, the dwelling of divine seers, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas,
one who is self-restrained goes from there to heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
divyaiścandanavṛkṣaiśca pādapairupaśobhitam /
āpaścandanasaṃyuktāḥ spandeti satataṃ tataḥ //
meaning:
दिव्यैश्चन्दनवृक्षैश्च पादपैरुपशोभितम् /
आपश्चन्दनसंयुक्ताः स्पन्देति सततं ततः //
text_mt:
Adorned with heavenly sandalwood trees and various plants,
waters mixed with sandalwood flow constantly from there.

sanskrit_iast:
nadī pravartate tābhyastāmraparṇīti nāmataḥ /
yā candanamahākhaṇḍāddakṣiṇaṃ yāti sāgaram //
meaning:
नदी प्रवर्तते ताभ्यस्ताम्रपर्णीति नामतः /
या चन्दनमहाखण्डाद्दक्षिणं याति सागरम् //
text_mt:
From those [waters] issues a river named Tāmraparṇī,
which flows from the great sandalwood grove to the southern sea.

sanskrit_iast:
nadyāstasyāśca tāmrāyāstūhyamānā mahodadhau /
śaṅkhā bhavanti śuktyaśca jāyate yāsu mauktikam //
meaning:
नद्यास्तस्याश्च ताम्रायास्तूह्यमाना महोदधौ /
शङ्खा भवन्ति शुक्त्यश्च जायते यासु मौक्तिकम् //
text_mt:
Borne by that river Tāmrā into the great ocean,
there are conches and oysters within which pearls are born.

sanskrit_iast:
udakānayanaṃ kṛtvā śaṅkhamauktikasaṃyutam /
ādhibhirvyādhibhiścaiva muktā yāntyamarāvatīm //
meaning:
उदकानयनं कृत्वा शङ्खमौक्तिकसंयुतम् /
आधिभिर्व्याधिभिश्चैव मुक्ता यान्त्यमरावतीम् //
text_mt:
Having offered water accompanied by conches and pearls,
freed from mental agonies and physical diseases, they go to Amarāvatī.

sanskrit_iast:
candanebhyaḥ prasūtānāṃ śaṅkhānāṃ mauktikasya vā /
pāpakarttṝnapi pitṝṃstārayanti yathāśruti //
meaning:
चन्दनेभ्यः प्रसूतानां शङ्खानां मौक्तिकस्य वा /
पापकर्त्तॄनपि पितॄंस्तारयन्ति यथाश्रुति //
text_mt:
[By means] of the conches or the pearls produced from the sandalwood [grove],
they deliver even fathers who have committed sins, according to the sacred tradition.

sanskrit_iast:
candratīrthe kumāryāṃ ca kāverīprabhave kṣaye /
śrīparvatasya tīrtheṣu vaikṛte ca tathā girau //
meaning:
चन्द्रतीर्थे कुमार्यां च कावेरीप्रभवे क्षये /
श्रीपर्वतस्य तीर्थेषु वैकृते च तथा गिरौ //
text_mt:
At Candratīrtha and Kumārī, at the source of the Kāverī, at Kṣaya,
at the holy sites of Śrīparvata and on the mountain Vaikṛta,

sanskrit_iast:
ekasthā yatra dṛśyante vṛkṣāhyauśīraparvate /
palāśāḥ khadirā bilvāḥ plakṣāśvatthavikaṅkatāḥ //
meaning:
एकस्था यत्र दृश्यन्ते वृक्षाह्यौशीरपर्वते /
पलाशाः खदिरा बिल्वाः प्लक्षाश्वत्थविकङ्कताः //
text_mt:
where trees are seen standing together on the Auśīra mountain—
palāśas, khadiras, bilvas, plakṣas, aśvatthas, and vikaṅkatas—

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ dvimaṇḍalāviddhaṃ vijñeyaṃ dvijasattamāḥ /
asmiṃstyaktvā janoṃ'gāti kṣipraṃ yātyamarāvatīm //
meaning:
एवं द्विमण्डलाविद्धं विज्ञेयं द्विजसत्तमाः /
अस्मिंस्त्यक्त्वा जनोंऽगाति क्षिप्रं यात्यमरावतीम् //
text_mt:
thus should it be known as encompassed by two circles, O best of the twice-born;
leaving one's body here, a person goes swiftly to Amarāvatī.

sanskrit_iast:
śrīparvatasya tīrthe tu vaikṛte ca tathā girau /
karmāṇi tu prayuktā ni siddhyanti prabhavāpyaye //
meaning:
श्रीपर्वतस्य तीर्थे तु वैकृते च तथा गिरौ /
कर्माणि तु प्रयुक्ता नि सिद्ध्यन्ति प्रभवाप्यये //
text_mt:
At the holy site of Śrīparvata and likewise on mount Vaikṛta,
rituals performed at the origin and destruction [of the world] succeed.

sanskrit_iast:
duṣprayuktā hi pitṛṣu suprayogā bhavantyuta /
pitṝṇāṃ duhitā puṇyā narmadā saritāṃ varā //
meaning:
दुष्प्रयुक्ता हि पितृषु सुप्रयोगा भवन्त्युत /
पितॄणां दुहिता पुण्या नर्मदा सरितां वरा //
text_mt:
Indeed, even ill-performed [offerings] to the ancestors become well-performed;
moreover, the sacred Narmadā, daughter of the ancestors, is the best of rivers,

sanskrit_iast:
yatra śrāddhāni dattāṃni hyakṣayāṇi bhavantyuta /
māṭharasya vane puṇye siddhacāraṇasevite //
meaning:
यत्र श्राद्धानि दत्तांनि ह्यक्षयाणि भवन्त्युत /
माठरस्य वने पुण्ये सिद्धचारणसेविते //
text_mt:
where indeed śrāddhas that are offered become imperishable,
in the holy forest of Māṭhara, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas.

sanskrit_iast:
antarddhānena gacchanti yuktvā tasminmahā girau /
vindhye caiva girau puṇye dharmādharmanidarśanīm //
meaning:
अन्तर्द्धानेन गच्छन्ति युक्त्वा तस्मिन्महा गिरौ /
विन्ध्ये चैव गिरौ पुण्ये धर्माधर्मनिदर्शनीम् //
text_mt:
Fixing [their minds] on that great mountain, they depart by becoming invisible;
and on the holy Vindhya mountain, [there is a stream] revealing dharma and adharma,

sanskrit_iast:
dhārāṃ pāpā na paśyanti dhārāṃ paśyanti sādhavaḥ /
tatra taddṛśyate pāpaṃ keṣāṃ citpāpakarmaṇām //
meaning:
धारां पापा न पश्यन्ति धारां पश्यन्ति साधवः /
तत्र तद्दृश्यते पापं केषां चित्पापकर्मणाम् //
text_mt:
a stream which the wicked do not see, [but] the virtuous do see;
there that sin of certain evildoers becomes visible.

sanskrit_iast:
kailāse yā mataṅgasya vāpī pāpaniṣūdanī /
snātvā tasyā divaṃ yānti kāmacārā vihaṅgamāḥ //
meaning:
कैलासे या मतङ्गस्य वापी पापनिषूदनी /
स्नात्वा तस्या दिवं यान्ति कामचारा विहङ्गमाः //
text_mt:
The pool of Mataṅga on Kailāsa destroys sin;
having bathed in it, birds that move at will go to heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
śaurpārake tathā tīrthe parvate pālamañjare /
pāṇḍukūpe samudrānte piṇḍārakataṭe tathā //
meaning:
शौर्पारके तथा तीर्थे पर्वते पालमञ्जरे /
पाण्डुकूपे समुद्रान्ते पिण्डारकतटे तथा //
text_mt:
Likewise at the holy site in Śūrpāraka, on Mount Pālamañjara,
at Pāṇḍukūpa on the edge of the sea, and on the shore of Piṇḍāraka,

sanskrit_iast:
vimale ca vipāpe ca saṃkalpaṃ prāpya cākṣayam /
śrīvṛkṣe citrakūṭe ca jaṃbūmārge ca nityaśaḥ //
meaning:
विमले च विपापे च संकल्पं प्राप्य चाक्षयम् /
श्रीवृक्षे चित्रकूटे च जंबूमार्गे च नित्यशः //
text_mt:
and at Vimala and Vipāpa, attaining an imperishable resolve,
at Śrīvṛkṣa, Citrakūṭa, and constantly at Jaṃbūmārga,

sanskrit_iast:
asitasya girau puṇye yogācāryasya dhīmataḥ /
tatrāpi śrāddhamānantyamasitāyāṃ ca nityaśaḥ //
meaning:
असितस्य गिरौ पुण्ये योगाचार्यस्य धीमतः /
तत्रापि श्राद्धमानन्त्यमसितायां च नित्यशः //
text_mt:
on the holy mountain of the wise yoga master Asita—
there too a śrāddha [brings] endless [fruits], and constantly at the Asitā river.

sanskrit_iast:
puṣkareṣvakṣayaṃ śrāddhaṃ tapaścaiva mahāphalamā /
mahodadhau prabhāse ca tadvadeva vinirdiśet //
meaning:
पुष्करेष्वक्षयं श्राद्धं तपश्चैव महाफलमा /
महोदधौ प्रभासे च तद्वदेव विनिर्दिशेत् //
text_mt:
At Puṣkara a śrāddha is imperishable, and austerity bears great fruit;
one should declare the very same regarding the great ocean and Prabhāsa.

sanskrit_iast:
devikāyāṃ vṛṣo nāma kūpaḥ siddhaniṣevitaḥ /
samutpatanti tasyāpo gavāṃ śabdena nityaśaḥ //
meaning:
देविकायां वृषो नाम कूपः सिद्धनिषेवितः /
समुत्पतन्ति तस्यापो गवां शब्देन नित्यशः //
text_mt:
On the Devikā [river] there is a well named Vṛṣa frequented by Siddhas;
its waters constantly surge up at the bellowing of cows.

sanskrit_iast:
yogeśvaraiḥ sadā juṣṭaḥ sarvapāpabahiṣkṛtaḥ /
dadyācchrāddhaṃ tu yastasmiṃstasya vakṣyāmi yatphalam //
meaning:
योगेश्वरैः सदा जुष्टः सर्वपापबहिष्कृतः /
दद्याच्छ्राद्धं तु यस्तस्मिंस्तस्य वक्ष्यामि यत्फलम् //
text_mt:
Always visited by lords of yoga, it is free from all sins;
whoever offers a śrāddha there, I shall describe the fruit for him.

sanskrit_iast:
akṣayaṃ sarvakāmīyaṃ śrāddhaṃ prīṇāti vai pitṝn /
jātavedaḥ śilā tatra sākṣādagneḥ sanātanāt //
meaning:
अक्षयं सर्वकामीयं श्राद्धं प्रीणाति वै पितॄन् /
जातवेदः शिला तत्र साक्षादग्नेः सनातनात् //
text_mt:
An imperishable śrāddha fulfilling all desires truly pleases the ancestors;
there is the stone of Jātavedas, [manifested] directly from the eternal Fire.

sanskrit_iast:
śrāddhāni cāgnikāryaṃ ca tatra kuryātsadā kṣayam /
yastvagniṃ praviśettatra nākapṛṣṭhe sa modate //
meaning:
श्राद्धानि चाग्निकार्यं च तत्र कुर्यात्सदा क्षयम् /
यस्त्वग्निं प्रविशेत्तत्र नाकपृष्ठे स मोदते //
text_mt:
One should always perform śrāddhas and rituals to fire there at the time of the waning moon;
and he who enters the fire there rejoices in the highest heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
agniśāntaḥ punarjātastatra dattaṃ tato 'kṣayam /
daśāśvamedhike tīrthe tīrthe pañcāśvamedhike //
meaning:
अग्निशान्तः पुनर्जातस्तत्र दत्तं ततो ऽक्षयम् /
दशाश्वमेधिके तीर्थे तीर्थे पञ्चाश्वमेधिके //
text_mt:
When the fire is extinguished, he is reborn; what is given there is therefore imperishable.
At the holy site Daśāśvamedhika and at the holy site Pañcāśvamedhika,

sanskrit_iast:
yathoddiṣṭaphalaṃ teṣāṃ kratūnāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ /
khyātaṃ hayaśiro nāma tīrthaṃ sadyo varapradam //
meaning:
यथोद्दिष्टफलं तेषां क्रतूनां नात्र संशयः /
ख्यातं हयशिरो नाम तीर्थं सद्यो वरप्रदम् //
text_mt:
the fruit of those sacrifices is as prescribed, there is no doubt of this;
the well-known holy site named Hayaśiras immediately grants boons.

sanskrit_iast:
śrāddhaṃ tatra sadākṣayyaṃ dātā svarge ca modate /
śrāddhaṃ suṃdanisuṃde ca deyaṃ pāpaniṣū danam //
meaning:
श्राद्धं तत्र सदाक्षय्यं दाता स्वर्गे च मोदते /
श्राद्धं सुंदनिसुंदे च देयं पापनिषू दनम् //
text_mt:
A śrāddha there is always imperishable, and the giver rejoices in heaven;
a śrāddha should be offered at Sundanīsunda, destroying sins.

sanskrit_iast:
śrāddhaṃ tatrākṣayaṃ proktaṃ japahomatapāṃsi ca /
jatuṅge śubhe tīrthe tarpayetsatataṃ pitṝn //
meaning:
श्राद्धं तत्राक्षयं प्रोक्तं जपहोमतपांसि च /
जतुङ्गे शुभे तीर्थे तर्पयेत्सततं पितॄन् //
text_mt:
A śrāddha there is declared imperishable, as are recitation, oblation, and austerities;
at the auspicious holy site Jatuṅga one should continually gratify the ancestors.

sanskrit_iast:
dṛśyate parvasu cchāyā yatra nityaṃ divaukasām /
pṛthivyāmakṣayaṃ dattaṃ virajā yatra pādapaḥ //
meaning:
दृश्यते पर्वसु च्छाया यत्र नित्यं दिवौकसाम् /
पृथिव्यामक्षयं दत्तं विरजा यत्र पादपः //
text_mt:
Where the shadow of the gods is always visible on the sacred days,
what is given on earth where the Virajā tree [stands] is imperishable.

sanskrit_iast:
yogeśvaraiḥ sadā juṣṭaḥ sarvapāpabahiṣkṛtaḥ /
dadyācchrāddhaṃ tu yastasmiṃstasya vakṣyāmi yatphalam //
meaning:
योगेश्वरैः सदा जुष्टः सर्वपापबहिष्कृतः /
दद्याच्छ्राद्धं तु यस्तस्मिंस्तस्य वक्ष्यामि यत्फलम् //
text_mt:
Always visited by lords of yoga, it is free from all sins;
whoever offers a śrāddha there, I shall describe the fruit for him:

sanskrit_iast:
arcitāstena vai sākṣādbhavanti pitaraḥ sadā /
asmiṃlloke vaśī ca syātpretya svarge mahī yate //
meaning:
अर्चितास्तेन वै साक्षाद्भवन्ति पितरः सदा /
अस्मिंल्लोके वशी च स्यात्प्रेत्य स्वर्गे मही यते //
text_mt:
by him the ancestors are indeed worshipped directly at all times;
he would become a master in this world, and after dying, he is honored in heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
prāyaśo madravā puṇyā śivo nāma hradastathā /
tatra vyāsasaraḥ puṇyaṃ divyo brahmahradastathā //
meaning:
प्रायशो मद्रवा पुण्या शिवो नाम ह्रदस्तथा /
तत्र व्याससरः पुण्यं दिव्यो ब्रह्मह्रदस्तथा //
text_mt:
For the most part, the Madravā is holy, and likewise the pool named Śiva;
there is the holy lake of Vyāsa and the divine Brahmahrada,

sanskrit_iast:
ūrjjantaḥ parvataḥ puṇyo yatra yogeśvarālayaḥ /
atraiva cāśramaḥ puṇyo vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ //
meaning:
ऊर्ज्जन्तः पर्वतः पुण्यो यत्र योगेश्वरालयः /
अत्रैव चाश्रमः पुण्यो वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः //
text_mt:
and the holy mountain Ūrjjanta, where the abode of the lords of yoga is;
and right here is the holy hermitage of the great-souled Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛgyajuḥ sāmaśirasaḥ kapotāḥ puṣpasāhvayāḥ /
ākhyāna pañcamā vedāḥ sṛṣṭā hyete svayaṃbhuvā //
meaning:
ऋग्यजुः सामशिरसः कपोताः पुष्पसाह्वयाः /
आख्यान पञ्चमा वेदाः सृष्टा ह्येते स्वयंभुवा //
text_mt:
Those named Kapota and Puṣpa, headed by the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma,
and the Vedas with the histories as the fifth, were created by Svayambhū.

sanskrit_iast:
gatvaitānmucyate pāpaddvijo vahniṃ samāśrayan /
śrāddhaṃ cānantyameteṣu japahomatapāṃsi ca //
meaning:
गत्वैतान्मुच्यते पापद्द्विजो वह्निं समाश्रयन् /
श्राद्धं चानन्त्यमेतेषु जपहोमतपांसि च //
text_mt:
Going to these, a twice-born, taking refuge in the fire, is freed from sin;
and a śrāddha performed at these, as well as recitation, oblations, and austerities, brings endless [reward].

sanskrit_iast:
puṇḍarīke mahātīrthe puṇḍarīkasamaṃ phalam /
brahmatīrthe mahāprājña sarvayajñasamaṃ phalam //
meaning:
पुण्डरीके महातीर्थे पुण्डरीकसमं फलम् /
ब्रह्मतीर्थे महाप्राज्ञ सर्वयज्ञसमं फलम् //
text_mt:
At the great holy site Puṇḍarīka, the fruit equals [that of] a Puṇḍarīka sacrifice;
at Brahmatīrtha, O very wise one, the fruit equals [that of] all sacrifices.

sanskrit_iast:
siṃdhusāgarasaṃbhede tathā pañcanade kṣayam /
virajāyāṃ tathā puṇyaṃ madravāyāṃ ca parvate //
meaning:
सिंधुसागरसंभेदे तथा पञ्चनदे क्षयम् /
विरजायां तथा पुण्यं मद्रवायां च पर्वते //
text_mt:
At the confluence of the Sindhu and the ocean, and likewise at Pañcanada on the new moon,
and on the holy Virajā, and on Mount Madravā,

sanskrit_iast:
deyaṃ saptanade śrāddhaṃ mānase vā viśeṣataḥ /
mahākūṭe hyanante ca girau trikakude tathā //
meaning:
देयं सप्तनदे श्राद्धं मानसे वा विशेषतः /
महाकूटे ह्यनन्ते च गिरौ त्रिककुदे तथा //
text_mt:
a śrāddha should be offered at Saptanada, or especially at Mānasa,
on Mahākūṭa, on Ananta, and likewise on Mount Trikakud.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃdhyāyāṃ ca mahānadyāṃ dṛśyate mahādadbhutam /
aśraddadhānaṃ nābhyeti sā cābhyeti dhṛtavratam //
meaning:
संध्यायां च महानद्यां दृश्यते महादद्भुतम् /
अश्रद्दधानं नाभ्येति सा चाभ्येति धृतव्रतम् //
text_mt:
At twilight on the great river, a great wonder is seen:
it does not approach one who lacks faith, but it approaches one who keeps his vows.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃśrayitvaikamekena sāyāhnaṃ prati nityaśaḥ /
tasmindeyaṃ sadā śrāddhaṃ pitṝṇāmakṣayārthinām //
meaning:
संश्रयित्वैकमेकेन सायाह्नं प्रति नित्यशः /
तस्मिन्देयं सदा श्राद्धं पितॄणामक्षयार्थिनाम् //
text_mt:
Approaching one by one constantly toward evening,
one should always offer a śrāddha there, desiring imperishability for the ancestors.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtātmā vākṛtātmā ca yatra vijñāyate naraḥ /
svargamārgapradaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ sadyo varapradam //
meaning:
कृतात्मा वाकृतात्मा च यत्र विज्ञायते नरः /
स्वर्गमार्गप्रदं नाम तीर्थं सद्यो वरप्रदम् //
text_mt:
Where a person is recognized as either cultivated in self or uncultivated in self,
that holy site named Svargamārgaprada immediately grants boons,

sanskrit_iast:
cīrāṇyutsṛjya yasmiṃstu divaṃ saptarṣayo gātāḥ /
adyāpi tāni dṛśyante cīrāṇyaṃbhogatāni tu //
meaning:
चीराण्युत्सृज्य यस्मिंस्तु दिवं सप्तर्षयो गाताः /
अद्यापि तानि दृश्यन्ते चीराण्यंभोगतानि तु //
text_mt:
where the seven seers, having cast off their bark garments, went to heaven;
even today those bark garments are seen submerged in the waters.

sanskrit_iast:
snātvā svargamavāpnoti tasmiṃstīrthettame naraḥ /
khyātamāyatanaṃ tatra nandinaḥ siddhasevitam //
meaning:
स्नात्वा स्वर्गमवाप्नोति तस्मिंस्तीर्थेत्तमे नरः /
ख्यातमायतनं तत्र नन्दिनः सिद्धसेवितम् //
text_mt:
Having bathed at that best of holy sites, a man attains heaven;
there is the renowned sanctuary of Nandin, frequented by Siddhas.

sanskrit_iast:
nandīśvarasya sā mūrttirnirācārairnadṛśyate /
dṛśyante kāñcanā yupāstvarciṣo bhāskarodaye //
meaning:
नन्दीश्वरस्य सा मूर्त्तिर्निराचारैर्नदृश्यते /
दृश्यन्ते काञ्चना युपास्त्वर्चिषो भास्करोदये //
text_mt:
That form of Nandīśvara is not seen by those lacking proper conduct;
golden sacrificial posts and rays of light are seen at sunrise.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ tāṃstu gacchantyānanditā divam /
sarvataśca kurukṣetraṃ sutīrthaṃ tu viśeṣataḥ //
meaning:
कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणं तांस्तु गच्छन्त्यानन्दिता दिवम् /
सर्वतश्च कुरुक्षेत्रं सुतीर्थं तु विशेषतः //
text_mt:
Having circumambulated them, they go to heaven rejoiced;
Kurukṣetra is good throughout, but especially as an excellent holy site.

sanskrit_iast:
puṇyaṃ sanatkumārasya yogeśasya mahātmanaḥ /
kīrtyate ca tilāndattvā pitṛbhyovai sadākṣayam //
meaning:
पुण्यं सनत्कुमारस्य योगेशस्य महात्मनः /
कीर्त्यते च तिलान्दत्त्वा पितृभ्योवै सदाक्षयम् //
text_mt:
The holy [site] of the great-souled Sanatkumāra, the lord of yoga,
is renowned; offering sesame seeds to the ancestors there [is] truly ever imperishable.

sanskrit_iast:
uktamevākṣayaṃ śrāddhaṃ dharmarājaniṣevitam /
śrāddhaṃ dattamamāvāsyāṃ vidhinā ca yathākramam //
meaning:
उक्तमेवाक्षयं श्राद्धं धर्मराजनिषेवितम् /
श्राद्धं दत्तममावास्यां विधिना च यथाक्रमम् //
text_mt:
An imperishable śrāddha frequented by the King of Dharma has been declared;
a śrāddha offered on the new-moon day in accordance with the rule and in due order,

sanskrit_iast:
puṃsaḥ sannihitāyāṃ tu kurūkṣetre viśeṣataḥ /
arcayitvā pitṝṃstatra sa putrastvanṛṇo bhavet //
meaning:
पुंसः सन्निहितायां तु कुरूक्षेत्रे विशेषतः /
अर्चयित्वा पितॄंस्तत्र स पुत्रस्त्वनृणो भवेत् //
text_mt:
especially at the Sannihitā pool in Kurukṣetra,
by worshipping the ancestors there, that man, a son, becomes free from debt.

sanskrit_iast:
sarasvatyāṃ vinaśane plakṣapraśravaṇe tathā /
vyāsatīrthe dṛṣadvatyāṃ triplakṣe ca viśeṣataḥ //
meaning:
सरस्वत्यां विनशने प्लक्षप्रश्रवणे तथा /
व्यासतीर्थे दृषद्वत्यां त्रिप्लक्षे च विशेषतः //
text_mt: On the Sarasvatī at Vinaśana, and likewise at Plakṣapraśravaṇa, / at Vyāsatīrtha, on the Dṛṣadvatī, and especially at Triplakṣa;

sanskrit_iast:
deyamoṅkārapavane śrāddhamakṣayamicchatā /
śakrāvatāre gaṅgāyāṃ maināke ca nagottame //
meaning:
देयमोङ्कारपवने श्राद्धमक्षयमिच्छता /
शक्रावतारे गङ्गायां मैनाके च नगोत्तमे //
text_mt: śrāddha should be offered at Oṅkārapavana by one desiring inexhaustible fruit, / at Śakrāvatāra on the Gaṅgā, and on Maināka, the best of mountains;

sanskrit_iast:
yamunāprabhave caiva sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate /
atyuṣṇāścātiśītāśca āpastasminnidarśanam //
meaning:
यमुनाप्रभवे चैव सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते /
अत्युष्णाश्चातिशीताश्च आपस्तस्मिन्निदर्शनम् //
text_mt: and at the source of the Yamunā, one is freed from all sins. / The waters there are extremely hot and extremely cold—a visible proof;

sanskrit_iast:
yamasya bhaginī puṣyā mārttaṇḍaduhitā śubhā /
tatrākṣayaṃ sadā śrāddhaṃ pitṛbhiḥ pūrvakīrttitam //
meaning:
यमस्य भगिनी पुष्या मार्त्तण्डदुहिता शुभा /
तत्राक्षयं सदा श्राद्धं पितृभिः पूर्वकीर्त्तितम् //
text_mt: she is the sister of Yama, the auspicious, bright daughter of the sun. / The ancestors formerly declared that a śrāddha offered there is ever inexhaustible.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmatuṇḍahrade snātvā saddayo bhavati brāhmaṇaḥ /
tasmiṃstu śrāddhamānantyaṃ japahomatapāṃsi ca //
meaning:
ब्रह्मतुण्डह्रदे स्नात्वा सद्दयो भवति ब्राह्मणः /
तस्मिंस्तु श्राद्धमानन्त्यं जपहोमतपांसि च //
text_mt: Having bathed in the lake Brahmatuṇḍahrada, a brāhmaṇa instantly becomes pure; / and śrāddha, recitation, burnt offerings, and austerities performed there are unending.

sanskrit_iast:
sthāṇubhūto 'carattatra vasiṣṭo vai mahātapāḥ /
adyāpi tatra dṛśyante pādapā maṇibarhaṇāḥ //
meaning:
स्थाणुभूतो ऽचरत्तत्र वसिष्टो वै महातपाः /
अद्यापि तत्र दृश्यन्ते पादपा मणिबर्हणाः //
text_mt: Vasiṣṭha of great asceticism wandered there, having become motionless as a tree trunk. / Even today, trees with jewels on their crests are seen there.

sanskrit_iast:
tulā tu dṛśyate tatra dharmāndharmanidharśinī /
yathā vai tolitaṃ vipraistīrthānāṃ phalamuttamam //
meaning:
तुला तु दृश्यते तत्र धर्मान्धर्मनिधर्शिनी /
यथा वै तोलितं विप्रैस्तीर्थानां फलमुत्तमम् //
text_mt: A balance is seen there, demonstrating righteousness and unrighteousness, / just as the supreme fruit of sacred places was weighed by the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit_iast:
pitṝṇāṃ duhitā yogā gandhakālīti viśrutā /
caturtho brahmaṇastvaṃśaḥ parāśarakulodbhavaḥ //
meaning:
पितॄणां दुहिता योगा गन्धकालीति विश्रुता /
चतुर्थो ब्रह्मणस्त्वंशः पराशरकुलोद्भवः //
text_mt: The daughter of the ancestors, known through yoga as Gandhakālī, / [bore] the fourth part of Brahmā born in the family of Parāśara;

sanskrit_iast:
vyasiṣyati caturddhā vai vedaṃ dhīmānmahāmuniḥ /
mahāyogaṃ mahātmānaṃ yā vyāsaṃ janayiṣyati //
meaning:
व्यसिष्यति चतुर्द्धा वै वेदं धीमान्महामुनिः /
महायोगं महात्मानं या व्यासं जनयिष्यति //
text_mt: the wise great sage divided the Veda fourfold— / she who gave birth to Vyāsa of great yoga and great soul.

sanskrit_iast:
acchodakaṃ nāmasarastatrācchodāsamudbhavaḥ /
matsyayonau punarjātā niyogātkāraṇena tu //
meaning:
अच्छोदकं नामसरस्तत्राच्छोदासमुद्भवः /
मत्स्ययोनौ पुनर्जाता नियोगात्कारणेन तु //
text_mt: There was a lake named Acchodaka, where Acchodā arose; / she was born again in the womb of a fish by ordinance and for a reason.

sanskrit_iast:
tasyāstvādyāśrame puṇye puṇyakṛdbhirniṣevite /
dattaṃ sakṛdapi śrāddhamakṣayaṃ samudāhṛtam //
meaning:
तस्यास्त्वाद्याश्रमे पुण्ये पुण्यकृद्भिर्निषेविते /
दत्तं सकृदपि श्राद्धमक्षयं समुदाहृतम् //
text_mt: At her original holy hermitage, frequented by performers of meritorious deeds, / a śrāddha offered even once is declared to be inexhaustible.

sanskrit_iast:
nadyāṃ yogasamādhānaṃ dattaṃ yugapadudbhavet /
kuberatuṅge pāpaghnaṃ vyāsatīrthetathaiva ca //
meaning:
नद्यां योगसमाधानं दत्तं युगपदुद्भवेत् /
कुबेरतुङ्गे पापघ्नं व्यासतीर्थेतथैव च //
text_mt: Composure of mind [attained] through yoga at the river arises simultaneously with the offering; / and likewise, it destroys sins at Kuberatuṅga and at Vyāsatīrtha.

sanskrit_iast:
puṇyāyāṃ brahmaṇo vedyāṃ śrāddhamānantyamiṣyate /
siddhaistu sevitā nityaṃ dṛśyate tu kṛtātmabhiḥ //
meaning:
पुण्यायां ब्रह्मणो वेद्यां श्राद्धमानन्त्यमिष्यते /
सिद्धैस्तु सेविता नित्यं दृश्यते तु कृतात्मभिः //
text_mt: Śrāddha offered on the holy altar of Brahmā is held to be unending; / always frequented by the Siddhas, it is seen by those whose minds are purified.

sanskrit_iast:
anivartanaṃ tu nandāyāṃ vedyāḥ prāguttaradiśi /
siddhikṣetraṃ surairjuṣṭaṃ yatprāpya na nivarttate //
meaning:
अनिवर्तनं तु नन्दायां वेद्याः प्रागुत्तरदिशि /
सिद्धिक्षेत्रं सुरैर्जुष्टं यत्प्राप्य न निवर्त्तते //
text_mt: Anivartana is at the Nandā, in the north-eastern direction from the altar; / it is a field of perfection frequented by gods, reaching which one does not return.

sanskrit_iast:
mahālaye padaṃ nyastaṃ mahādevena dhīmatā /
bhūtānāmanukaṃpārthaṃ nāstikānāṃ nidarśanam //
meaning:
महालये पदं न्यस्तं महादेवेन धीमता /
भूतानामनुकंपार्थं नास्तिकानां निदर्शनम् //
text_mt: At Mahālaya, a footprint was placed by wise Mahādeva, / for the sake of compassion toward beings and as a sign to unbelievers.

sanskrit_iast:
viraje tvakṣayaṃ śrāddhaṃ pūrvameva mahālaye /
nandāyāṃ viraje caiva tathaiva ca mahālaye //
meaning:
विरजे त्वक्षयं श्राद्धं पूर्वमेव महालये /
नन्दायां विरजे चैव तथैव च महालये //
text_mt: A śrāddha at Viraja is indeed inexhaustible, previously [declared] at Mahālaya; / on the Nandā, and at Viraja, and likewise at Mahālaya,

sanskrit_iast:
ātmānaṃ tārayantīha daśapūrvāndaśāparān /
kākahrade jātismaryaṃ suvarṇamamitaujasam //
meaning:
आत्मानं तारयन्तीह दशपूर्वान्दशापरान् /
काकह्रदे जातिस्मर्यं सुवर्णममितौजसम् //
text_mt: they save themselves, ten ancestors and ten descendants. / At Kākahrada there is memory of past births and gold of boundless splendor.

sanskrit_iast:
kaumāraṃ ca saraḥ puṇyaṃ nāgabhogābhirakṣitam /
kumāratīrthe snātvā tu tridivaṃ yāti mānavaḥ //
meaning:
कौमारं च सरः पुण्यं नागभोगाभिरक्षितम् /
कुमारतीर्थे स्नात्वा तु त्रिदिवं याति मानवः //
text_mt: And the holy lake Kaumāra is protected by the coils of serpents; / having bathed at Kumāratīrtha, a man goes to heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
devālaye tapastasvā ekapādena duścaram /
nirāhāro yugaṃ divyamumātuṅgo sthito jvalan //
meaning:
देवालये तपस्तस्वा एकपादेन दुश्चरम् /
निराहारो युगं दिव्यमुमातुङ्गो स्थितो ज्वलन् //
text_mt: Performing severe asceticism on one foot in the abode of the gods, / without food for a divine yuga, standing blazing at Umātuṅga,

sanskrit_iast:
umātuṅge bhṛgostuṅge brahmatuṅge mahālaye /
tatra śrāddhāni deyāni nityamakṣayamicchatā //
meaning:
उमातुङ्गे भृगोस्तुङ्गे ब्रह्मतुङ्गे महालये /
तत्र श्राद्धानि देयानि नित्यमक्षयमिच्छता //
text_mt: at Umātuṅga, at Bhṛgutuṅga, at Brahmatuṅga, and at Mahālaya— / there śrāddhas should be offered constantly by one desiring inexhaustible fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
akṣayaṃ tu sadā śrāddhaṃ śālagrāme samantataḥ /
duṣkṛtaṃ dṛśyate tatra pratyakṣamakṛtātmanām //
meaning:
अक्षयं तु सदा श्राद्धं शालग्रामे समन्ततः /
दुष्कृतं दृश्यते तत्र प्रत्यक्षमकृतात्मनाम् //
text_mt: A śrāddha is ever inexhaustible everywhere at Śālagrāma; / the evil deeds of the undisciplined are visibly seen there.

sanskrit_iast:
pratyadeśo hyaśiṣṭānāṃ śiṣṭānāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ /
tatra devahradaḥ puṇyo brahmaṇo nāgarāṭ śuciḥ //
meaning:
प्रत्यदेशो ह्यशिष्टानां शिष्टानां च विशेषतः /
तत्र देवह्रदः पुण्यो ब्रह्मणो नागराट् शुचिः //
text_mt: Indeed, it is a refutation of the undisciplined and especially [a test] of the disciplined. / There is the holy, pure Devahrada of Brahmā, the king of nāgas;

sanskrit_iast:
piṇḍaṃ gṛhṇati hi satāṃ na gṛhṇātyasatāṃ sadā /
atipradīptairbhujagairbhoktumannaṃ na śakyate //
meaning:
पिण्डं गृह्णति हि सतां न गृह्णात्यसतां सदा /
अतिप्रदीप्तैर्भुजगैर्भोक्तुमन्नं न शक्यते //
text_mt: it takes the funeral ball of the virtuous, but never takes that of the unvirtuous. / The food cannot be consumed by the fiercely blazing serpents.

sanskrit_iast:
pratyakṣaṃ dṛśyate dharmastīrthayornatayordvayoḥ /
kāravatyāṃ ca śāṇḍilyāṃ guhāyāṃ vāmanasya ca //
meaning:
प्रत्यक्षं दृश्यते धर्मस्तीर्थयोर्नतयोर्द्वयोः /
कारवत्यां च शाण्डिल्यां गुहायां वामनस्य च //
text_mt: Righteousness is visibly seen at the two bowed sacred places: / at the Kāravatī and at the Śāṇḍilī, and at the cave of Vāmana.

sanskrit_iast:
gatvā caitāni pūtaḥsyācchradaddhamakṣayameva ca /
japo homastapo dhyānaṃ yatkiñcitsukṛtaṃ bhavet //
meaning:
गत्वा चैतानि पूतःस्याच्छ्रदद्धमक्षयमेव च /
जपो होमस्तपो ध्यानं यत्किञ्चित्सुकृतं भवेत् //
text_mt: Having gone to these, one becomes purified, and śrāddha is truly inexhaustible; / [as also are] recitation, burnt offerings, austerity, meditation, and whatever good deed there may be.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmacaryaṃ ca yau dhatte gurubhaktiṃ śataṃ samāḥ /
evamādyāssaricchreṣṭhā yatsnānādaghamokṣaṇam /
kumāradhārā tatraiva dṛṣṭā pāpaṃ praṇaśyati //
meaning:
ब्रह्मचर्यं च यौ धत्ते गुरुभक्तिं शतं समाः /
एवमाद्यास्सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा यत्स्नानादघमोक्षणम् /
कुमारधारा तत्रैव दृष्टा पापं प्रणश्यति //
text_mt: And whoever maintains celibacy and devotion to the guru for a hundred years— / such are the foremost rivers, by bathing in which release from sin [is attained]; / and there, merely on seeing Kumāradhārā, sin is destroyed.

sanskrit_iast:
dhyānāsanaṃ tu tatraiva vyāsasyādyāpi dṛśyate /
śailaḥ kāntipurābhyāśe prāgudīcyāṃ diśi sthitaḥ //
meaning:
ध्यानासनं तु तत्रैव व्यासस्याद्यापि दृश्यते /
शैलः कान्तिपुराभ्याशे प्रागुदीच्यां दिशि स्थितः //
text_mt: Even today, the meditation seat of Vyāsa is seen right there, / on a mountain near Kāntipura, situated in the north-eastern direction.

sanskrit_iast:
puṇya puṣkariṇī tatra kirātagaṇarakṣitā /
yasyāṃ snātvā sakṛdvipraḥ kāmānāpnoti śāśvatān //
meaning:
पुण्य पुष्करिणी तत्र किरातगणरक्षिता /
यस्यां स्नात्वा सकृद्विप्रः कामानाप्नोति शाश्वतान् //
text_mt: There is a holy lotus pond there, guarded by troops of Kirātas, / bathing in which once, a brāhmaṇa attains eternal desires;

sanskrit_iast: adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ devavaccarate mahīm //
meaning: अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानां देववच्चरते महीम् //
text_mt: invisible to all beings, he wanders the earth like a god.

sanskrit_iast:
kāśyapasya mahātīrthaṃ kālasarpiriti śrutam /
tatra śrāddhāni deyāni nityamakṣayamicchatā //
meaning:
काश्यपस्य महातीर्थं कालसर्पिरिति श्रुतम् /
तत्र श्राद्धानि देयानि नित्यमक्षयमिच्छता //
text_mt: The great sacred place of Kaśyapa is known as Kālasarpi; / there śrāddhas should be offered constantly by one desiring inexhaustible fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
devadāruvane vāpi dhārāyāstu nidarśanam /
nirdhūtāni tu pāpāni dṛśyante sukṛtātmanām //
meaning:
देवदारुवने वापि धारायास्तु निदर्शनम् /
निर्धूतानि तु पापानि दृश्यन्ते सुकृतात्मनाम् //
text_mt: Or in the Devadāruvana, where there is the manifestation of the waterfall, / the cleansed sins of those of good deeds are visibly seen.

sanskrit_iast:
bhāgīrathyāṃ prayāge tu nityamakṣayamucyate /
kālañjare daśārṇāyāṃ naimiṣe kurujāṅgale //
meaning:
भागीरथ्यां प्रयागे तु नित्यमक्षयमुच्यते /
कालञ्जरे दशार्णायां नैमिषे कुरुजाङ्गले //
text_mt: On the Bhāgīrathī at Prayāga, [a śrāddha] is said to be constantly inexhaustible; / at Kālañjara, on the Daśārṇā, in Naimiṣa, in Kurujāṅgala,

sanskrit_iast:
vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ ca deyaṃ śrāddhaṃ prayatnataḥ /
tatra yogeśvaro nityaṃ tasyāṃ dattamathākṣayam //
meaning:
वाराणस्यां नगर्यां च देयं श्राद्धं प्रयत्नतः /
तत्र योगेश्वरो नित्यं तस्यां दत्तमथाक्षयम् //
text_mt: and in the city of Vārāṇasī, śrāddha should be offered with effort; / Yogeśvara is constantly there; what is offered in it is inexhaustible.

sanskrit_iast:
gatvā caitāni pūrtaḥ syācchrāddhamakṣayyameva ca /
jabo homastathā dhyānaṃ yatkiñcitsukṛtaṃ bhavet //
meaning:
गत्वा चैतानि पूर्तः स्याच्छ्राद्धमक्षय्यमेव च /
जबो होमस्तथा ध्यानं यत्किञ्चित्सुकृतं भवेत् //
text_mt: Having gone to these, one becomes filled [with merit], and śrāddha is inexhaustible; / [as also are] recitation, burnt offerings, meditation, and whatever good deed there may be.

sanskrit_iast:
lauhitye vaitaraṇyāṃ casvargavedyāṃ tathaiva ca /
sā tu devī samudrānte dṛśyate caiva nāmabhiḥ //
meaning:
लौहित्ये वैतरण्यां चस्वर्गवेद्यां तथैव च /
सा तु देवी समुद्रान्ते दृश्यते चैव नामभिः //
text_mt: At the Lauhitya, at the Vaitaraṇī, and likewise at Svargavedī; / that goddess is seen at the edge of the ocean under those names.

sanskrit_iast:
gayāyāṃ dharmavṛṣṭhe tu sarasi brahmaṇastathā /
gayāṃ gṛdhravaṭe caiva śrāddhaṃ dattaṃ mahāphalam //
meaning:
गयायां धर्मवृष्ठे तु सरसि ब्रह्मणस्तथा /
गयां गृध्रवटे चैव श्राद्धं दत्तं महाफलम् //
text_mt: At Gayā on Dharmapṛṣṭha, and likewise at the lake of Brahmā, / at Gayā and at Gṛdhravaṭa, śrāddha offered bears great fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
himaṃ ca patate tatra samantātpañcayo janam /
bharatasyāśrame puṇye 'raṇyaṃ puṇyatamaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
हिमं च पतते तत्र समन्तात्पञ्चयो जनम् /
भरतस्याश्रमे पुण्ये ऽरण्यं पुण्यतमं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: And snow falls there all around for five yojanas. / At the holy hermitage of Bharata is the forest considered most holy;

sanskrit_iast:
mataṅgasya vanaṃ tatra dṛśyate sarvamānuṣaiḥ /
sthāpitaṃ dharmasarvasvaṃ lokasyāsya nidarśanam //
meaning:
मतङ्गस्य वनं तत्र दृश्यते सर्वमानुषैः /
स्थापितं धर्मसर्वस्वं लोकस्यास्य निदर्शनम् //
text_mt: the forest of Mataṅga is seen there by all humans, / established as the entirety of righteousness, an example for this world.

sanskrit_iast:
yaddaṇḍakavanaṃ puṇyaṃ puṇyakṛdbhirniṣevitam /
yasminprāhurviśalyeti tīrthaṃ sadyo nidarśanam //
meaning:
यद्दण्डकवनं पुण्यं पुण्यकृद्भिर्निषेवितम् /
यस्मिन्प्राहुर्विशल्येति तीर्थं सद्यो निदर्शनम् //
text_mt: The Daṇḍaka forest is holy, frequented by performers of meritorious deeds; / in it, they speak of the sacred place called Viśalyā, an immediate proof;

sanskrit_iast:
tulāmānaistathā cāpi śāstraiśca vividhaistathā /
unmaccanti tathā lagna ye vai pāpakṛto janāḥ //
meaning:
तुलामानैस्तथा चापि शास्त्रैश्च विविधैस्तथा /
उन्मच्चन्ति तथा लग्न ये वै पापकृतो जनाः //
text_mt: by measures on a balance and in diverse scriptures, / those people who commit sins emerge while stuck [there].

sanskrit_iast:
tṛtīyāyāṃ tathā pāde nirādhāyāṃ tu maṇḍale /
mahāhrade ca kauśikyāṃ dattaṃ śrāddhaṃ mahāphalam //
meaning:
तृतीयायां तथा पादे निराधायां तु मण्डले /
महाह्रदे च कौशिक्यां दत्तं श्राद्धं महाफलम् //
text_mt: And on the third pāda, in the unsupportive region, / and at the great pool on the Kauśikī, a śrāddha offered bears great fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
muṇḍapṛṣṭe padaṃ nyastaṃ mahādevena dhīmatā /
bahudevayugāṃstaptvā tapastīvraṃ sudaścaram //
meaning:
मुण्डपृष्टे पदं न्यस्तं महादेवेन धीमता /
बहुदेवयुगांस्तप्त्वा तपस्तीव्रं सुदश्चरम् //
text_mt: On Muṇḍapṛṣṭha, a footprint was placed by wise Mahādeva, / after performing severe and very difficult asceticism for many divine yugas.

sanskrit_iast:
alpenāpyatra kālena naro dharmaparāyaṇaḥ /
pāpmānamutsṛjatyāśu jīrṇāṃ tvacamivoragaḥ //
meaning:
अल्पेनाप्यत्र कालेन नरो धर्मपरायणः /
पाप्मानमुत्सृजत्याशु जीर्णां त्वचमिवोरगः //
text_mt: Even in a short time here, a man devoted to righteousness / quickly casts off sin, like a snake its worn-out skin.

sanskrit_iast:
siddhānāṃ prītijananaṃ papānāṃ ca bhayaṅkaram /
lelihānairmahāghorai rakṣyate sumahoragaiḥ //
meaning:
सिद्धानां प्रीतिजननं पपानां च भयङ्करम् /
लेलिहानैर्महाघोरै रक्ष्यते सुमहोरगैः //
text_mt: Causing joy to the Siddhas and fear to the sinful, / it is protected by very great serpents, fiercely licking with their tongues.

sanskrit_iast:
nāmnā kanakanandīti tīrthaṃ jagati viśrutam /
udīcyāṃ muṇḍapṛṣṭasya brahmarṣigaṇasevitam //
meaning:
नाम्ना कनकनन्दीति तीर्थं जगति विश्रुतम् /
उदीच्यां मुण्डपृष्टस्य ब्रह्मर्षिगणसेवितम् //
text_mt: The sacred place known in the world by the name Kanakanandī, / to the north of Muṇḍapṛṣṭha, is frequented by hosts of Brahmarṣis.

sanskrit_iast:
tatra snātvā divaṃyānti svaśarīreṇa mānavāḥ /
dattaṃ vāpi sadā śrāddhamakṣayyaṃ samudāhṛtam //
meaning:
तत्र स्नात्वा दिवंयान्ति स्वशरीरेण मानवाः /
दत्तं वापि सदा श्राद्धमक्षय्यं समुदाहृतम् //
text_mt: Having bathed there, men go to heaven in their own bodies; / and a śrāddha offered [there] is ever declared to be inexhaustible.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṇaistribhistataḥ snātvā niṣkrīṇāti narastanum /
mānase sarasi snātvā śrāddhaṃnirvarttayettataḥ //
meaning:
ऋणैस्त्रिभिस्ततः स्नात्वा निष्क्रीणाति नरस्तनुम् /
मानसे सरसि स्नात्वा श्राद्धंनिर्वर्त्तयेत्ततः //
text_mt: Having bathed there, a man redeems his body from the three debts; / having bathed in the Mānasa lake, he should then perform the śrāddha.

sanskrit_iast:
tīre tu sarasastasya devasyā yatanaṃ mahat /
āruhya tu japaṃstatra siddho yāti divaṃ tataḥ //
meaning:
तीरे तु सरसस्तस्य देवस्या यतनं महत् /
आरुह्य तु जपंस्तत्र सिद्धो याति दिवं ततः //
text_mt: On the shore of that lake is a great sanctuary of the god. / Ascending [it] while muttering prayers, perfected, he then goes to heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
uttaraṃ mānasaṃ gatvāsiddhiṃ prāpnotyanuttamām /
snātvā tasminsaraśreṣṭhe dṛśyate mahādadbhutam //
meaning:
उत्तरं मानसं गत्वासिद्धिं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् /
स्नात्वा तस्मिन्सरश्रेष्ठे दृश्यते महादद्भुतम् //
text_mt: Having gone to the northern Mānasa [lake], he attains unsurpassed perfection. / After bathing in that best of lakes, a great wonder is seen:

sanskrit_iast:
divaścyutā mahābhāgā hyantarikṣe virājate /
gaṅgā tripathagā devī viṣṇupādāccyutā satī //
meaning:
दिवश्च्युता महाभागा ह्यन्तरिक्षे विराजते /
गङ्गा त्रिपथगा देवी विष्णुपादाच्च्युता सती //
text_mt: having fallen from heaven, the highly fortunate goddess Gaṅgā shines in the mid-region; / traversing three paths, she is the virtuous woman fallen from the foot of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
ākāśe dṛśyate tatra toraṇaṃ sūryasannibham /
jāṃbūnadamayaṃ puṇyaṃ svagadvāramivāyatam //
meaning:
आकाशे दृश्यते तत्र तोरणं सूर्यसन्निभम् /
जांबूनदमयं पुण्यं स्वगद्वारमिवायतम् //
text_mt: There an archway resembling the sun is seen in the sky, / made of gold, sacred, like an extended gateway to heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ pravarttate bhūyaḥ sarvasāgaramaṇḍikā /
pāvanī sarvabhūtānāṃ dharmajñānāṃ viśeṣataḥ //
meaning:
ततः प्रवर्त्तते भूयः सर्वसागरमण्डिका /
पावनी सर्वभूतानां धर्मज्ञानां विशेषतः //
text_mt: From there flows forth once more the adornment of all oceans, / purifying all creatures, especially those who know dharma.

sanskrit_iast:
candrabhāgā ca siddhuśca śubhe mānasasaṃbhave /
sāgaraṃ paścimaṃ yāto divyaḥ siṃdhunado varaḥ //
meaning:
चन्द्रभागा च सिद्धुश्च शुभे मानससंभवे /
सागरं पश्चिमं यातो दिव्यः सिंधुनदो वरः //
text_mt: The Candrabhāgā and the Sindhu, both auspicious, originate from Mānasa. / The celestial, excellent Sindhu river flows to the western sea.

sanskrit_iast:
parvato himavānnāma nānādhātuvibhūṣitaḥ /
āyato vai sahasrāṇi yojanānāṃ bahuni tu //
meaning:
पर्वतो हिमवान्नाम नानाधातुविभूषितः /
आयतो वै सहस्राणि योजनानां बहुनि तु //
text_mt: The mountain named Himavat is adorned with various minerals, / extended indeed over many thousands of yojanas.

sanskrit_iast:
siddhacāraṇasaṃkīrṇā devarṣigaṇasevitā /
tatra puṣkariṇī ramyā suṣumṇā nāma nāmataḥ //
meaning:
सिद्धचारणसंकीर्णा देवर्षिगणसेविता /
तत्र पुष्करिणी रम्या सुषुम्णा नाम नामतः //
text_mt: Crowded with Siddhas and Cāraṇas, attended by hosts of divine seers, / there is a charming lotus pool named Suṣumṇā.

sanskrit_iast:
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi tasyāṃ snātastu jīvati /
śrāddhaṃ bhavati cānantaṃ tatra dattaṃ mahodayam //
meaning:
दशवर्षसहस्राणि तस्यां स्नातस्तु जीवति /
श्राद्धं भवति चानन्तं तत्र दत्तं महोदयम् //
text_mt: One who bathes in it lives for ten thousand years, / and a śrāddha offered there becomes imperishable and brings great elevation.

sanskrit_iast:
tārayecca sadā śrāddhe daśapūrvāndaśāparān /
sarvatra himavānpuṇyo gaṅgā puṇyā samantataḥ //
meaning:
तारयेच्च सदा श्राद्धे दशपूर्वान्दशापरान् /
सर्वत्र हिमवान्पुण्यो गङ्गा पुण्या समन्ततः //
text_mt: At a śrāddha he always delivers ten ancestors before him and ten after him. / Everywhere the Himavat is holy, and everywhere the Gaṅgā is holy;

sanskrit_iast:
samudragāḥ samudrāśca sarve puṇyāḥ samantataḥ /
evamādiṣu cānyeṣu śrāddhaṃ nirvartayedbudhaḥ //
meaning:
समुद्रगाः समुद्राश्च सर्वे पुण्याः समन्ततः /
एवमादिषु चान्येषु श्राद्धं निर्वर्तयेद्बुधः //
text_mt: all ocean-going [rivers] and oceans are holy on every side. / In such and other [places] the wise person should perform a śrāddha.

sanskrit_iast:
puto bhavati vai snātvā hutvā dattvā tathaiva ca /
śelasānuṣu śṛṅgeṣu kandareṣu guhāsu ca //
meaning:
पुतो भवति वै स्नात्वा हुत्वा दत्त्वा तथैव च /
शेलसानुषु शृङ्गेषु कन्दरेषु गुहासु च //
text_mt: He becomes purified indeed after bathing, offering oblations, and making gifts / on mountain ridges, peaks, crevices, and caves,

sanskrit_iast:
upahvaranitaṃbeṣu tathā prasravaṇeṣu ca /
pulineṣvāpagānāṃ ca tathaiva prabhaveṣu ca //
meaning:
उपह्वरनितंबेषु तथा प्रस्रवणेषु च /
पुलिनेष्वापगानां च तथैव प्रभवेषु च //
text_mt: on slopes and declivities, and at waterfalls, / on the sandy banks of rivers, and likewise at their sources,

sanskrit_iast:
mahodadhau gavāṃ goṣṭe saṃgameṣu vaneṣu ca /
susaṃmṛṣṭopalipteṣu tdṛdyeṣu surabhiṣvatha //
meaning:
महोदधौ गवां गोष्टे संगमेषु वनेषु च /
सुसंमृष्टोपलिप्तेषु त्दृद्येषु सुरभिष्वथ //
text_mt: at the ocean, in a cow-pen, at confluences, and in forests, / and in pleasant and fragrant places thoroughly swept and smeared;

sanskrit_iast:
gomayenopalipteṣu vivikteṣu gṛheṣu ca /
kuryācchrāddhamathaiteṣu nityameva yathāvidhi //
meaning:
गोमयेनोपलिप्तेषु विविक्तेषु गृहेषु च /
कुर्याच्छ्राद्धमथैतेषु नित्यमेव यथाविधि //
text_mt: and in secluded houses smeared with cow-dung / he should always perform the śrāddha in these according to rule,

sanskrit_iast:
prāgdakṣiṇāṃ diśaṃ gatvā sarvakāmacikīrṣayā /
evameteṣu sarveṣu śrāddhaṃ kuryādatandritaḥ //
meaning:
प्राग्दक्षिणां दिशं गत्वा सर्वकामचिकीर्षया /
एवमेतेषु सर्वेषु श्राद्धं कुर्यादतन्द्रितः //
text_mt: facing the south-east with the desire to accomplish all wishes. / Thus in all these [places] he should perform a śrāddha without sloth.

sanskrit_iast:
eteṣveva tu medhāvī brāhmīṃ siddhimavāpnuyāt /
traivarṇavihitaiḥ sthāne dharme varṇāśrame rataiḥ //
meaning:
एतेष्वेव तु मेधावी ब्राह्मीं सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् /
त्रैवर्णविहितैः स्थाने धर्मे वर्णाश्रमे रतैः //
text_mt: In these very places the wise man would attain Brahman-like perfection / through the sites prescribed for the three twice-born classes, devoted to the duty of caste and stage of life.

sanskrit_iast:
kaupasthānaṃ ca saṃtyāgātprāpyate pitṛpūjanam /
tīrthānyanusaranvīraḥ śraddadhānaḥ samāhitaḥ //
meaning:
कौपस्थानं च संत्यागात्प्राप्यते पितृपूजनम् /
तीर्थान्यनुसरन्वीरः श्रद्दधानः समाहितः //
text_mt: And by renunciation a place by a well is obtained for the worship of the ancestors. / Visiting sacred places, heroic, faithful, and concentrated,

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtapāpo 'pi śudhyeta kiṃ punaḥ śubhakarmakṛt /
tiryagyoniṃ na gacchecca kudeśe ca na jāyate //
meaning:
कृतपापो ऽपि शुध्येत किं पुनः शुभकर्मकृत् /
तिर्यग्योनिं न गच्छेच्च कुदेशे च न जायते //
text_mt: even one who has committed sins would be purified, how much more so one who does good deeds! / He would not go into an animal womb, nor is he born in a bad land;

sanskrit_iast:
svargī bhavati vipro vai mokṣopāyaṃ ca vindati /
aśraddadhānaḥ pāpāyurnāstiko 'cchinnasaṃśayaḥ //
meaning:
स्वर्गी भवति विप्रो वै मोक्षोपायं च विन्दति /
अश्रद्दधानः पापायुर्नास्तिको ऽच्छिन्नसंशयः //
text_mt: the Brahmin indeed attains heaven and finds the means to liberation. / One without faith, of sinful life, an atheist, one whose doubts are unsevered,

sanskrit_iast:
hetuniṣṭhaśca pañcaite na tīrthe phalabhāginaḥ /
gurutīrthe parā siddhistīrthānāṃ paramaṃ padam //
meaning:
हेतुनिष्ठश्च पञ्चैते न तीर्थे फलभागिनः /
गुरुतीर्थे परा सिद्धिस्तीर्थानां परमं पदम् //
text_mt: and one devoted to sophistry—these five do not partake of the fruit in a sacred place. / The highest perfection is in the sacred place of the guru; it is the supreme abode of sacred places.

sanskrit_iast:
dhyānaṃ tīrthaṃ paraṃ tasmādbrahmatīrthaṃ sanātanam /
upavāsātparaṃ dhyānamindriyāṇāṃ nivarttanam //
meaning:
ध्यानं तीर्थं परं तस्माद्ब्रह्मतीर्थं सनातनम् /
उपवासात्परं ध्यानमिन्द्रियाणां निवर्त्तनम् //
text_mt: Meditation is a higher sacred place than that; it is the eternal sacred place of Brahman. / Meditation is higher than fasting; it is the turning back of the senses.

sanskrit_iast:
upavāsanibaddhairhi prāṇaireva punaḥ punaḥ /
prāṇāpānau vaśe kṛtvā vaśagānīndiyāṇi ca //
meaning:
उपवासनिबद्धैर्हि प्राणैरेव पुनः पुनः /
प्राणापानौ वशे कृत्वा वशगानीन्दियाणि च //
text_mt: With the vital breaths bound indeed by fasting again and again, / having brought the prāṇa and apāna under control and made the senses obedient,

sanskrit_iast:
buddhiṃ manasi saṃyamya sarveṣāṃ tu nivarttanam /
pratyāhāraṃ kṛtaṃ viddhi mokṣopāyamasaṃśayam //
meaning:
बुद्धिं मनसि संयम्य सर्वेषां तु निवर्त्तनम् /
प्रत्याहारं कृतं विद्धि मोक्षोपायमसंशयम् //
text_mt: restraining the intellect in the mind and withdrawing all [senses]— / know that withdrawal has been accomplished, undoubtedly the means to liberation.

sanskrit_iast:
indriyāṇāṃ mano ghoraṃ buddhyādīnāṃ vivarttanam /
anā hāro kṣayaṃ yāti vidyādanaśanaṃ tapaḥ //
meaning:
इन्द्रियाणां मनो घोरं बुद्ध्यादीनां विवर्त्तनम् /
अना हारो क्षयं याति विद्यादनशनं तपः //
text_mt: The terrible mind is the sensory faculty [directing] the turning away of the intellect and other [faculties]. / Fasting goes to ruin [if seen merely as abstention]; one should know that abstention from food is austerity [only when accompanied by control].

sanskrit_iast:
nigrahe buddhimansoranyabuddhirna jāyate /
kṣīṇeṣu sarvadoṣeṣu kṣīṇeṣvevendriyeṣu ca //
meaning:
निग्रहे बुद्धिमन्सोरन्यबुद्धिर्न जायते /
क्षीणेषु सर्वदोषेषु क्षीणेष्वेवेन्द्रियेषु च //
text_mt: When the mind and intellect are restrained, no other intellect arises. / When all faults have waned and the senses have also waned,

sanskrit_iast:
parinirvāti śuddhātmā yathā vahniranidhanaḥ /
kāraṇebhyo guṇebhyaśca vyaktāvyaktācca kutsnaśaḥ //
meaning:
परिनिर्वाति शुद्धात्मा यथा वह्निरनिधनः /
कारणेभ्यो गुणेभ्यश्च व्यक्ताव्यक्ताच्च कुत्स्नशः //
text_mt: the purified self completely attains extinction, like a fire without fuel. / From the causes, from the qualities, and from the manifest and unmanifest in their entirety,

sanskrit_iast:
niyojayati kṣetrajñaṃ tebhyoyogena yogavit /
tasya nāsti gatiḥ sthānaṃ vyaktāvyakte ca sarvaśaḥ /
na sannāsanna sadasannaiva kiñcidavasthitaḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhyabhāge tṛtīya upoddhātapāde śrāddhakalpe puṇyadeśānukīrttanaṃ nāma trayodaśo 'dhyāyaḥ // 13//
meaning:
नियोजयति क्षेत्रज्ञं तेभ्योयोगेन योगवित् /
तस्य नास्ति गतिः स्थानं व्यक्ताव्यक्ते च सर्वशः /
न सन्नासन्न सदसन्नैव किञ्चिदवस्थितः //
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मध्यभागे तृतीय उपोद्धातपादे श्राद्धकल्पे पुण्यदेशानुकीर्त्तनं नाम त्रयोदशो ऽध्यायः // 13//
text_mt:
the knower of yoga unites the knower of the field through yoga with them. / For him there is no movement or state among the manifest and unmanifest in any way; / he exists neither as existent nor as non-existent, nor as existent and non-existent, nor as anything at all.

Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, named ‘Recitation of Sacred Places’ in the section on the rites of ancestral offerings (śrāddhakalpa), in the third [section], the Upoddhātapāda, in the middle part proclaimed by Vāyu, of the glorious and great Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi sarvadānaphalāni ca /
śrāddhakarmaṇi medhyāni varjanīyāni yāni ca //
meaning:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि सर्वदानफलानि च /
श्राद्धकर्मणि मेध्यानि वर्जनीयानि यानि च //
text_mt: Bṛhaspati said: / After this I shall proclaim the fruits of all gifts, / and those [substances] which are fit for offerings and those to be avoided in the rite of śrāddha.

sanskrit_iast:
himaprapatane kuryādā haredvā himaṃ tataḥ /
agnihotramupāyuṣyaṃ pavitraṃ paramaṃ hitam //
meaning:
हिमप्रपतने कुर्यादा हरेद्वा हिमं ततः /
अग्निहोत्रमुपायुष्यं पवित्रं परमं हितम् //
text_mt: When snow falls, one should perform [it] or bring snow from there; / the fire-sacrifice prolongs life, is pure, supreme, and beneficial.

sanskrit_iast:
naktaṃ tu varjayecchrāddhaṃ rāhoranyatra darśanāt /
sarvasvenāpi karttavyaṅkṣipraṃ vai rāhudarśane //
meaning:
नक्तं तु वर्जयेच्छ्राद्धं राहोरन्यत्र दर्शनात् /
सर्वस्वेनापि कर्त्तव्यङ्क्षिप्रं वै राहुदर्शने //
text_mt: One should avoid a śrāddha at night, except upon the sighting of Rāhu; / at the sight of Rāhu, it should indeed be performed promptly, even at the cost of all one's possessions.

sanskrit_iast:
uparāge na kuryādyaḥ paṅke gauriva sīdati /
kurvāṇastattaretpāpaṃ satī nauriva sāgare //
meaning:
उपरागे न कुर्याद्यः पङ्के गौरिव सीदति /
कुर्वाणस्तत्तरेत्पापं सती नौरिव सागरे //
text_mt: He who does not perform it during an eclipse sinks like a cow in mud; / while performing it, he crosses over sin like a seaworthy boat on the ocean.

sanskrit_iast:
vaiśvadevaṃ ca saumyaṃ ca khaḍgamāṃsaṃ paraṃ haviḥ /
viṣāṇavarjaṃ khaḍgasya mātsaryānnāśayāmahe //
meaning:
वैश्वदेवं च सौम्यं च खड्गमांसं परं हविः /
विषाणवर्जं खड्गस्य मात्सर्यान्नाशयामहे //
text_mt: The vaiśvadeva and the saumya [offerings], and the flesh of a rhinoceros are a supreme oblation; / excluding the horn of the rhinoceros, we do not destroy [it] out of envy.

sanskrit_iast:
tvāṣṭrā vai yajamānena deveśena mahātmanā /
pibañchacīpatiḥ somaṃ pṛthivyāṃ madhyagaḥ purā //
meaning:
त्वाष्ट्रा वै यजमानेन देवेशेन महात्मना /
पिबञ्छचीपतिः सोमं पृथिव्यां मध्यगः पुरा //
text_mt: Formerly, while Śacī's lord [Indra] was drinking the soma as a sacrificer related to Tvaṣṭṛ, standing in the middle of the earth as the great lord of gods,

sanskrit_iast:
śyāmākāstatra utpannāḥ pitrarthamaparajitāḥ /
vipruṣastasya nāsābhyāmāsaktābhyāṃ tathekṣavaḥ //
meaning:
श्यामाकास्तत्र उत्पन्नाः पित्रर्थमपरजिताः /
विप्रुषस्तस्य नासाभ्यामासक्ताभ्यां तथेक्षवः //
text_mt: unconquered śyāmāka grains were produced there for the sake of the ancestors / from the drops clinging to his nostrils, and likewise sugarcanes.

sanskrit_iast:
śreṣmalāḥ śītalāḥ snigdhā madhurāśca tathekṣavaḥ /
śyāmākairikṣubhiścaiva pitṝṇāṃ sarvakāmikam //
meaning:
श्रेष्मलाः शीतलाः स्निग्धा मधुराश्च तथेक्षवः /
श्यामाकैरिक्षुभिश्चैव पितॄणां सर्वकामिकम् //
text_mt: Sugarcanes produce phlegm, are cooling, smooth, and sweet; / through śyāmāka grains and sugarcanes, all wishes of the ancestors are fulfilled.

sanskrit_iast:
kuryādāgrayaṇaṃ yastu sa śīghraṃ siddhimāpnuyāt /
śyāmākāstu dvināmāno vihitā yajanesmṛte //
meaning:
कुर्यादाग्रयणं यस्तु स शीघ्रं सिद्धिमाप्नुयात् /
श्यामाकास्तु द्विनामानो विहिता यजनेस्मृते //
text_mt: He who performs the first-fruits offering (āgrayaṇa) would quickly attain perfection. / The śyāmāka grains, having two names, are prescribed in sacrificial rites according to traditional law.

sanskrit_iast:
yasmāttedevasṛṣṭāstu tasmātte cākṣayāḥ smṛtāḥ /
prasātikāḥ priyaṅguśca mudgāśca haritāstathā //
meaning:
यस्मात्तेदेवसृष्टास्तु तस्मात्ते चाक्षयाः स्मृताः /
प्रसातिकाः प्रियङ्गुश्च मुद्गाश्च हरितास्तथा //
text_mt: Because they were created by the god, they are remembered as imperishable. / Prasātikā wild grains, priyaṅgu panic-seeds, and likewise green beans—

sanskrit_iast:
etānyapi samānāni śyāmākānāṃ guṇaistu taiḥ /
kṛṣṇamāṣāstilāścaiva śreṣṭhāstu yavaśālayaḥ //
meaning:
एतान्यपि समानानि श्यामाकानां गुणैस्तु तैः /
कृष्णमाषास्तिलाश्चैव श्रेष्ठास्तु यवशालयः //
text_mt: these are also equal to śyāmāka grains by virtue of those qualities; / black lentils and sesame seeds indeed, and barley and winter rice are the best,

sanskrit_iast:
mahāyavāśca niṣpāvāstathaiva ca madhūlikāḥ /
kṛṣṇāścaivānnalohāśca garhyāḥ syuḥ śrāddhakarmaṇi //
meaning:
महायवाश्च निष्पावास्तथैव च मधूलिकाः /
कृष्णाश्चैवान्नलोहाश्च गर्ह्याः स्युः श्राद्धकर्मणि //
text_mt: and large barley, kidney-beans, and likewise madhūlikā grains. / Dark and unwholesome grains should be blamed in the rite of śrāddha.

sanskrit_iast:
rājamāṣāstathānye vai varjanīyāḥ prayatnataḥ /
masūrāścaiva puṇyāśca kusuṃbhaṃ śrīniketanam //
meaning:
राजमाषास्तथान्ये वै वर्जनीयाः प्रयत्नतः /
मसूराश्चैव पुण्याश्च कुसुंभं श्रीनिकेतनम् //
text_mt: Likewise, cowpeas and other [forbidden beans] must be avoided with great care; / lentils, though pure, and safflower, the abode of fortune,

sanskrit_iast:
varṣāsvatiyavā nityaṃ tathā vṛṣakavāsakau /
bilvāmalakamṛdvīkāpanasāmrātadāḍimāḥ //
meaning:
वर्षास्वतियवा नित्यं तथा वृषकवासकौ /
बिल्वामलकमृद्वीकापनसाम्रातदाडिमाः //
text_mt: and during the rains, overgrown barley must always [be avoided], as well as the vṛṣaka and vāsaka plants. / Wood-apples, myrobalans, raisins, jackfruits, hog-plums, pomegranates,

sanskrit_iast:
tavaśolaṃyatākṣaudrakharjūrāmralāni ca /
khaśerukovidāryaśca tālakandaṃ tathā visam //
meaning:
तवशोलंयताक्षौद्रखर्जूराम्रलानि च /
खशेरुकोविदार्यश्च तालकन्दं तथा विसम् //
text_mt: tavaśola, honey, dates, mangoes, / rush-nuts, kovidāra, palm roots, and lotus fibers,

sanskrit_iast:
tamālaṃ śatakandaṃ ca madvasūcāntakāndikī /
kāleyaṃ kālaśākaṃ ca bhūripūrṇā suvarcalā //
meaning:
तमालं शतकन्दं च मद्वसूचान्तकान्दिकी /
कालेयं कालशाकं च भूरिपूर्णा सुवर्चला //
text_mt: tamāla, the hundred-rooted plant, madvasū, antakāndikī, / kāleya, black pot-herb, full-leafed suvarcalā,

sanskrit_iast:
māṃsākṣaṃ duviśākaṃ ca bubucetā kurastathā /
kaphālakaṃ kaṇā drākṣā lakucaṃ cocameva ca //
meaning:
मांसाक्षं दुविशाकं च बुबुचेता कुरस्तथा /
कफालकं कणा द्राक्षा लकुचं चोचमेव च //
text_mt: māṃsākṣa, duviśāka, bubucetā, kura, / kaphālaka, long pepper, grapes, monkey-jack, and cinnamon,

sanskrit_iast:
alābuṃ grīvakaṃ vīraṃ karkandhūmadhusāhvayam /
vaikaṅkataṃ nālikeraśṛṅgaja pakarūṣakam //
meaning:
अलाबुं ग्रीवकं वीरं कर्कन्धूमधुसाह्वयम् /
वैकङ्कतं नालिकेरशृङ्गज पकरूषकम् //
text_mt: gourds, grīvaka, vīra, jujubes called honey-sweet, / vaikaṅkata, coconut, trapa bispinosa, and parūṣaka [fruits]—

sanskrit_iast:
pippalī maricaṃ caiva paṭholaṃ bṛhatīphalam /
sugandhamāṃsapīvanti kaṣāyāḥ sarva eva ca //
meaning:
पिप्पली मरिचं चैव पठोलं बृहतीफलम् /
सुगन्धमांसपीवन्ति कषायाः सर्व एव च //
text_mt: Long pepper, black pepper, pointed gourd, and the fruit of the Indian nightshade, / fragrant meat drink, and all astringents;

sanskrit_iast:
evamādīni cānyāni varāṇi madhurāṇi ca /
nāgaraṃ cātra vai deyaṃ dīrghamūlakamava ca //
meaning:
एवमादीनि चान्यानि वराणि मधुराणि च /
नागरं चात्र वै देयं दीर्घमूलकमव च //
text_mt: these and other choice, sweet things, / as well as dry ginger and long radish, should indeed be offered here.

sanskrit_iast:
vaṃśaḥ karīraḥ surasaḥ sarjakaṃ bhūstṛṇāni ca /
varjanīyāni vakṣyāmi śrāddhakarmaṇi nityaśaḥ //
meaning:
वंशः करीरः सुरसः सर्जकं भूस्तृणानि च /
वर्जनीयानि वक्ष्यामि श्राद्धकर्मणि नित्यशः //
text_mt: Bamboo shoots, karīra, holy basil, sarjaka, and bhūstṛṇa— / I shall tell of those that are always to be avoided in the śrāddha rite:

sanskrit_iast:
laśunaṃ gṛñjanaṃ caiva tathā vai palvalodakam /
karaṃbhādyāni cānyāni hīnāni rasagandhataḥ //
meaning:
लशुनं गृञ्जनं चैव तथा वै पल्वलोदकम् /
करंभाद्यानि चान्यानि हीनानि रसगन्धतः //
text_mt: garlic, carrots, and water from a puddle, / karaṃbha and others devoid of taste and fragrance.

sanskrit_iast:
śrāddhakarmaṇi varjyāni kāraṇaṃ cātra vakṣyate /
purā devāsure yuddhe nirjitasya baleḥ suraiḥ //
meaning:
श्राद्धकर्मणि वर्ज्यानि कारणं चात्र वक्ष्यते /
पुरा देवासुरे युद्धे निर्जितस्य बलेः सुरैः //
text_mt: These are to be avoided in the śrāddha rite, and the reason for this will be told: / anciently, in the war between the gods and the asuras, when Bali was defeated by the gods,

sanskrit_iast:
śaraistu vikṣatādaṅgātpatitā raktabindavaḥ /
tata etāni jātāni laśunādīni sarvaśaḥ //
meaning:
शरैस्तु विक्षतादङ्गात्पतिता रक्तबिन्दवः /
तत एतानि जातानि लशुनादीनि सर्वशः //
text_mt: drops of blood fell from his limbs wounded by arrows; / from them arose all these, beginning with garlic.

sanskrit_iast:
tathaiva raktaniryāsā lavaṇānyauṣaraṇi ca /
śraddhakarmaṇi varjyāni yāśca nāryo rajasvalāḥ //
meaning:
तथैव रक्तनिर्यासा लवणान्यौषरणि च /
श्रद्धकर्मणि वर्ज्यानि याश्च नार्यो रजस्वलाः //
text_mt: Likewise, red resins, salts from barren soils, / and women who are menstruating must be avoided in the śrāddha rite;

sanskrit_iast:
durgandhaṃ phenilaṃ caiva tathā vai palvalodakam /
labhedyatra na gaustṛptiṃ naktaṃ yaccaiva guhyate //
meaning:
दुर्गन्धं फेनिलं चैव तथा वै पल्वलोदकम् /
लभेद्यत्र न गौस्तृप्तिं नक्तं यच्चैव गुह्यते //
text_mt: foul-smelling, frothy water, and water from a puddle, / where a cow finds no satisfaction, and whatever is drawn at night;

sanskrit_iast:
āvikaṃ mārgamauṣṭraṃ ca sarvamekaśaphaṃ ca yat /
māhiṣaṃ cāmaraṃ caiva payo varjyaṃ vijānatā //
meaning:
आविकं मार्गमौष्ट्रं च सर्वमेकशफं च यत् /
माहिषं चामरं चैव पयो वर्ज्यं विजानता //
text_mt: milk of sheep, of deer, of camels, and of all one-hoofed animals, / milk of buffaloes and of yaks must be avoided by the discerning one.

sanskrit_iast:
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi varjyāndeśānprayatnataḥ /
na draṣṭavyaṃ ca yaiḥ śrāddhaṃ śaucāśaucaṃ ca kṛtsnaśaḥ //
meaning:
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि वर्ज्यान्देशान्प्रयत्नतः /
न द्रष्टव्यं च यैः श्राद्धं शौचाशौचं च कृत्स्नशः //
text_mt: Hereafter I shall describe with care the regions to be avoided, / those by whom a śrāddha should not be seen, and all matters of purity and impurity.

sanskrit_iast:
vanyamūlaphalairbhakṣyaiḥ śrāddhaṃ kuryāttu śraddhayā /
rājaniṣṭhāmavāpnoti svargamakṣayameva ca //
meaning:
वन्यमूलफलैर्भक्ष्यैः श्राद्धं कुर्यात्तु श्रद्धया /
राजनिष्ठामवाप्नोति स्वर्गमक्षयमेव च //
text_mt: One should perform the śrāddha with devotion, using wild roots, fruits, and foods; / [then] one attains the state of a king and imperishable heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
aniṣṭaśabdāṃ saṃkīrṇāṃ jantupyāptāmathāvilām /
pūtigandhāṃ tathā bhūmiṃ varjayecchrāddhakarmaṇi //
meaning:
अनिष्टशब्दां संकीर्णां जन्तुप्याप्तामथाविलाम् /
पूतिगन्धां तथा भूमिं वर्जयेच्छ्राद्धकर्मणि //
text_mt: Ground that has displeasing sounds, is crowded, infested with insects, turbid, / or foul-smelling, one should avoid in the śrāddha rite.

sanskrit_iast:
nadyaḥ sāgaraparyantā dvāraṃ dakṣiṇapūrvataḥ /
triśaṅkorvarjayeddeśaṃ sarvaṃ dvādaśa yojanam //
meaning:
नद्यः सागरपर्यन्ता द्वारं दक्षिणपूर्वतः /
त्रिशङ्कोर्वर्जयेद्देशं सर्वं द्वादश योजनम् //
text_mt: The rivers up to the ocean, the gateway to the south-east— / one should avoid the whole country of Triśaṅku for twelve yojanas,

sanskrit_iast:
uttareṇa mahānadyā dakṣiṇena ca vaikaṭam /
deśāstriśaṅkavo nāma varjyā vai śrāddhakarmaṇi //
meaning:
उत्तरेण महानद्या दक्षिणेन च वैकटम् /
देशास्त्रिशङ्कवो नाम वर्ज्या वै श्राद्धकर्मणि //
text_mt: north of the Mahānadī and south of Vaikaṭa: / regions named after Triśaṅku must be avoided in the śrāddha rite.

sanskrit_iast:
kāraskarāḥ kaliṅgaśca sidhoruttarameva ca /
pranaṣṭāśramadharmāśca varjyā deśāḥ prayatnataḥ //
meaning:
कारस्कराः कलिङ्गश्च सिधोरुत्तरमेव च /
प्रनष्टाश्रमधर्माश्च वर्ज्या देशाः प्रयत्नतः //
text_mt: The Kāraskaras, Kaliṅga, and the north of the Sindhu, / and regions where the duties of the āśramas have vanished, must be avoided with care.

sanskrit_iast:
nagnādayo na paśyeyuḥ śrāddhakarma vyavasthitam /
gacchantyetaistu dṛṣṭāni na pitṝṃśca pitāmahāṃna //
meaning:
नग्नादयो न पश्येयुः श्राद्धकर्म व्यवस्थितम् /
गच्छन्त्येतैस्तु दृष्टानि न पितॄंश्च पितामहांन //
text_mt: The naked and others must not look upon the arranged śrāddha rite; / when seen by them, these offerings do not reach the ancestors or the grandfathers.

sanskrit_iast:
śaṃyuruvāca
nagnādīnbhagavansamyagācakṣva paripṛcchataḥ /
bṛhaspatiruvāca
sarveṣāmeva bhūtānāṃ trayīsaṃvaraṇaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
शंयुरुवाच
नग्नादीन्भगवन्सम्यगाचक्ष्व परिपृच्छतः /
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
सर्वेषामेव भूतानां त्रयीसंवरणं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: Śaṃyu said: / "O venerable one, tell me fully about the naked and others, as I ask." / Bṛhaspati said: / "The three Vedas are declared to be the covering of all beings.

sanskrit_iast:
tāṃ ye tyajanti saṃmohātte vai nagnādayo janāḥ /
pralīyate vṛṣo yasminnirālaṃbaśca yo bṛṣe //
meaning:
तां ये त्यजन्ति संमोहात्ते वै नग्नादयो जनाः /
प्रलीयते वृषो यस्मिन्निरालंबश्च यो बृषे //
text_mt: Those who abandon them through delusion are indeed the 'naked' and the rest. / One in whom righteousness dissolves and who has no support in righteousness,

sanskrit_iast:
vṛṣaṃ yastu parityajya mokṣamanyatra mārgati /
vṛṣo vedāśramastasminyo vai samyaṅna paśyati //
meaning:
वृषं यस्तु परित्यज्य मोक्षमन्यत्र मार्गति /
वृषो वेदाश्रमस्तस्मिन्यो वै सम्यङ्न पश्यति //
text_mt: who, abandoning righteousness, seeks liberation elsewhere— / righteousness is the stages of life based on the Veda; one who does not see it rightly,

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyo vṛṣalaḥ sa na saṃśayaḥ /
purā devāsure yuddhe nirjitairasuraistathā //
meaning:
ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियो वैश्यो वृषलः स न संशयः /
पुरा देवासुरे युद्धे निर्जितैरसुरैस्तथा //
text_mt: be he a brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, or vaiśya, is indeed an outcaste, without doubt. / Anciently, in the war between the gods and the asuras, by the defeated asuras

sanskrit_iast:
pāśaṇḍā vai kṛtāstāta teṣāṃ sṛṣṭiḥ prajāyate /
vṛddhaśrāvakinirgranthāḥ śākyā jīvakakārpaṭāḥ //
meaning:
पाशण्डा वै कृतास्तात तेषां सृष्टिः प्रजायते /
वृद्धश्रावकिनिर्ग्रन्थाः शाक्या जीवककार्पटाः //
text_mt: heretics were created, my dear one, and their progeny came to be: / Vṛddhaśrāvakins, Nirgranthas, Śākyas, and Jīvaka beggars.

sanskrit_iast:
ye dharmaṃ nānuvarttante te vai nagnādayo janāḥ /
